# Design Library ↔ PRD / Architecture / Ghost Reconciliation

**Date:** 2026-08-27 · **Step:** 4a of `build-sequence.md` (unattended `/bmad-review`, verification-gap + adversarial lenses, category by category; step 4b — the Ghost Build Room — rules on what this file could not settle by reading).
**Inputs:** `design/claude-design-export/Inflozo/` — the 34 category specs `A1…A34 <Name> - Spec.md`, `P0 Editor Primitives - Spec.md`, the design frames, the S1–S14 app screens, the M1–M9 pages, `B Missing Surfaces`, `Editor Sidebar Kit` — vs `prd.md` v4.1 and its normative companions (`sections-inventory.md`, `appendix-b1-template-contexts.md`, `appendix-h1-string-catalog.md`, the five research companions), `ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md` (AD-1…AD-36b), `VERIFY-AT-BUILD.md` (items 1–46), and `CONTROL-PROMPTS.html` (§Decisions D1–D39, all ruled 2026-08-24; §Carry-forwards).
**Precedence applied (PRD preamble):** verification files › research companions on any Ghost fact › normative companions on scope, binding legality and strings › `prd.md` on every product decision. Designs are non-normative: where a design and the PRD disagree the PRD wins and the design moves — unless the design exposes something unbuildable, incoherent or contradicted by Ghost, which is a `prd-defect`. D1–D39 are treated as decided; this file checks that the specs honoured them and never re-opens one.
**Tags:** `ghost-infeasible` (cannot be built on Ghost as specified — cited) · `stale-design` (the spec contradicts a PRD rule, a ruled decision or a count — the design moves) · `prd-defect` (the design revealed a PRD/inventory line that is wrong or unbuildable — the PRD moves) · `arch-gap` (an ask of the spine or the registry with no owner) · `spec-incomplete` (a field, a no-JS line, a list control, a string key or a count the spec must carry and does not) · `needs-execution` (a Ghost claim reading cannot settle — probe listed at the end) · `consistent` (confirmation, listed only where useful).
**Standing rules honoured:** every Ghost claim carries its citation or goes to NEEDS EXECUTION; every finding names every place it reaches; every count below is derived from disk, never restated from a document; where two approved decisions collide the item stops and is flagged.

## A1 · Headers & Navigation

**Counts (derived):** designs on disk **16** (17 `A1-*` frames − `A1-0 Category Proof`) · spec **16** (§1–§16 headings; the §5 frame list names 16) · inventory **16** (sections-inventory.md line 54) · [Free] spec **0** (the spec carries no `[Free]` marker anywhere) / inventory **2** (#1 Classic Left, #2 Minimal Center) · modules declared: `core` · `nav-drawer` · `header-scroll` · `accordion` · `search-overlay` · `carousel` · `reading-progress` · `mode-toggle` (8, all registry §2.1 names) + **`nav-transform`** (D2's addition, still marked "ARCHITECT… not coined" in the spec) · custom-setting slots: **0** (nothing promoted to `@custom`) · authored lists: `navItems[].children[]` + grandchildren + `children[].description` (Authored mode), `stripItems[]` (A1·8), `panelColumns[]` + `panelColumns[].links[]` (A1·7), social extras (A1·8, A1·14) — all with P0·3 add/remove/reorder (§20) · Ghost-bound lists: `navItems[]`, `secondaryNav[]`, Ghost's social fields, prefix-mode children/groups/columns, bound `panelColumns`, BY TOPIC (`panelTags[]`), BY AUTHORS, `featuredPost`/rail post — all with no Add and the P0·3 Ghost-list card (§20).

Roster note (derivation): the export's sixteen names map to the inventory's sixteen only partly — Rail↔Classic Left, Split Rail↔Split Nav, Floating Pill↔Pill Float, Overlay↔Transparent Overlay, Utility + Nav↔Double Decker, Boxed↔Boxed Container, Search-Forward↔Command Bar, Side Rail/Drawer-First↔Sidebar Trigger, Big Type↔Mono Wordmark, Icon Utilities↔Members Aware (re-cut, avatar removed). No seed exists for Stacked Masthead, Mega Bar, Contrast Band, Centre Nav, Reveal; no export design exists for Minimal Center, CTA Forward, Underline Slide, Mega Search, Borderline, Tab Deck. See §2 and §6.

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility

- **needs-execution** — **A1·4 Overlay (hero precondition)** — claim: "the template resolves the image before render and picks A1·4 or A1·1… Nothing about that choice needs JavaScript" (§0 finding 2, §4 Behaviour module, §4 Data). Evidence: A1 compiles into `default.hbs` (inventory line 48/54, FR-D5 line 222); `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` §4 line 282: bare `{{feature_image}}` in `default.hbs` "resolve[s] against the child's root, so on a post render they are **empty**… Do not use bare resource fields here"; `appendix-b1-template-contexts.md` §3 `default` row: "bare resource fields are empty on every render… Requires `{{#get}}`: anything resource-specific"; `{{#is}}` is in the universal set (appendix-b1 §2 line 68), so *which template* is known, but neither companion says whether a block-wrapped `{{#post}}{{#if feature_image}}` inside `default.hbs` reaches the current post. For authored heroes (A4 on `home.hbs`) the fact is compile-time; for `post.hbs`/`page.hbs` (A24's two "Pair with A1·4 Overlay" designs, A24 spec line 78) it is per-post at render time. Verdict: **needs execution** (NE-A1-1). Separately, the spec's own "or its image fails to load" (§4 Data) is a client-side event (`onerror`) that no server-side precondition can see — that half contradicts "nothing needs JavaScript" and is `ghost-infeasible` as written (listed in §2). Reaches: spec §0 finding 2, §4, §18 item 4, register 45(d), inventory line 71, A24 spec §3 line 78, the route-awareness carry-forward.
- **buildable with a stated change** — **A1·3 Stacked Masthead (Site-timezone date)** — claim: "computed client-side by `core`'s date stamp — never server-rendered" (§3 "The date", §21 note 17). Evidence: `research-section-js-libraries.md` §2.1 row 0 — `core` is the registry, `data-i18n-*` reader, IO factory, reduced-motion gate, AbortController teardown; **no date stamp**; D13: "No registry module renders client-side dates… v1 date sources are Site timezone and Custom date only… the visitor's-clock option (a `local-date` module) is deferred." Ghost's `{{date}}` "falls back to the current date when `published_at` is absent" (`research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` line 721, citing docs.ghost.org/themes/helpers/data/date) in `@site.timezone`. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — the Site-timezone date is **server-rendered** by `{{date format="…"}}` at the `default.hbs` root, carries D13's staleness caveat ("may lag until the cache turns" — the same caveat A2's Schedule ships), and the line "Without JS the Site-timezone date is absent" is struck (a server-rendered `<time>` is present with JS off). The contradiction itself is in §2; the root-context probe is NE-A1-2. Reaches: spec §3, §0·7 last row, §21 note 17, D13, registry §2.1 row 0.
- **needs-execution** — **§0 Data / A1·6 / A1·8 (`secondaryNav`)** — claim: `secondaryNav` is Ghost's secondary navigation, iterated and capped at 5 (A1·8). Evidence: `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` line 141 lists `secondary_navigation` as public "yes (indirectly)" — unexplained; `{{navigation type="secondary"}}` is the documented route (line 1064) but renders Ghost's partial, not a capped, prefix-aware list. Verdict: needs execution (NE-A1-3) — whether `{{#foreach @site.secondary_navigation}}` iterates directly on T1 and T3. Reaches: §0 Data, §6, §8, §20 ownership table.
- **needs-execution / spec-incomplete** — **§0·8 social links (A1·8, A1·14)** — claim: "binds to Ghost's social accounts… Facebook and X only on 5.x; all nine on ≥ 6.36". Evidence: appendix-b1 §6 — the seven fields `@site.threads … linkedin` are ≥ 6.36.0, "absent… not offerable on 5.x"; `{{#social_accounts}}` is ≥ 6.38 and a gscan error below it; `{{social_url}}` is un-gated and the only sanctioned helper; research line 1129: "`{{social_url}}` — source byte-identical. Its wider platform coverage in 6.x is purely a consequence of `@site` gaining the fields." Verdict: the gate is stated correctly (D22 honoured) but **the spec never names the helper** — it must say `{{social_url type="…"}}` and never `{{#social_accounts}}`; and whether `social_url` accepts the seven new `type` values (and whether those fields hold handles or URLs) is unread — NE-A1-4. Reaches: §0·8, §8, §14, §20 social row, §21 note 22, appendix-b1 §6, D22.
- **buildable** (non-obvious mechanism) — **A1·7 Mega Bar count-bearing foot links and rankings** — "All {n} tags", "All {n} in series", BY TOPIC "tags ranked by post count", BY AUTHORS "authors ranked by post count", the Tag/Author picker "showing each option's post count". Evidence: appendix-b1 §5 — tag/author lists and counts are `{{#get "tags"|"authors" include="count.posts"}}`; the site-wide totals come from the block-param pagination object (`{{#get "tags" limit="1" as |t pages|}}{{pages.total}}`), since `limit="all"` is capped at 100 on 6.x (FR-H2, appendix-b1 §5). Ranking is `order="count.posts desc"`. Verdict: buildable; `pages.total` inside `default.hbs` and `order="count.posts desc"` on `authors` are NE-A1-5. Note the carry-forward "canonical post-count decision (pagination.total vs count.posts differ on member-gated sites)" now has two more consumers: A1·7's foot-link counts and A1·9's "Search N essays" placeholder. Reaches: §7 Data block, §9 Content fields, the Data & FR-H2 carry-forward.
- **spec-incomplete** — **A1·6 / A1·7 (`{{#get}}` in `default.hbs`)** — claim: bound columns, BY TOPIC, BY AUTHORS, the rail post and A1·6's `featuredPost` "are rendered server-side". Evidence: appendix-b1 §3 `default` row ("anything resource-specific requires `{{#get}}`") — so up to **seven `{{#get}}` calls run on every page of the site** (4 columns + tags + authors + rail); appendix-b1 §5: "A slow `{{#get}}` is **aborted**: it yields an empty collection plus a visible `<span data-aborted-get-helper>Could not load content</span>`… Every `{{#get}}`-driven section must degrade gracefully (FR-H8 guards cover this)." The spec designs the empty column ("Hide column · Show fallback") but no aborted state — on a header the span would print inside the mega panel on every template. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — the spec must state the aborted-get rendering per bound block and the per-page `{{#get}}` count. Reaches: §6 Data, §7 Data block, FR-H8, appendix-b1 §5.
- **stale-design** — **§0 Placement "Present on every template"** — Evidence: appendix-b1 §3c: "`error.hbs` / `error-{N}xx.hbs` must be self-contained in Inflozo output: **no layout inheritance**, no `{{#get}}`" — no `{{!< default}}`, so no `default.hbs`, so **no A1 header on error pages**; §7.4 line 588 emits `error.hbs`. Whether `private.hbs` inherits `default.hbs` (and therefore shows the header over the password gate) is unstated anywhere. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — A1 §0 must say "every template that inherits `default.hbs`; not `error.hbs`", and A31's error designs must say what header (if any) they draw. Reaches: A1 §0 Placement, A31 spec, appendix-b1 §3c, FR-I1/§7.4, inventory line 54 ("Used on `default.hbs` (site-wide)"). Private-gate inheritance is NE-A1-7.
- **arch-gap** — **§0·4 search affordance + A1·9 (the `/search/` route)** — claim: the registry sentence "The trigger is a real `<form action="/search/" method="get">`" and A1·9's "the round trip lands the reader on… the A23 surface with the query prefilled". Evidence: Ghost has no `/search/` route of its own (Sodo search is hash-driven); §7.4 line 583 emits `routes.yaml` "only if Routes Manager used"; the PRD text contains no `/search/` at all (python scan of prd.md, 0 hits); A23 spec line 164 assumes the route exists. Verdict: not buildable as written unless the compiler emits a `/search/` route + template unconditionally whenever any search affordance is placed — a FR-I2/`routes.yaml` obligation no FR names. Reaches: registry §7 `search-overlay` row, A1 §0·4/§9, A23 line 164, FR-I1/I2, §7.4. Probe NE-A1-6.
- **arch-gap** — **§0·4 "opens the A23 surface via `search-overlay`" on all 16** — Evidence: appendix-h1 §3.7: "A23 #1–#8, #11, #14 are *triggers* for Ghost's native search overlay"; only #9/#10/#12/#15 render Inflozo's own overlay against the Content API. A project whose A23 choice is a native trigger needs a `data-ghost-search` button and **no** registry module in the header, and Sodo — Ghost's script, not the theme's — does nothing with JS off (the register 45(c) class). The spec hardwires the module and one degradation for both worlds. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — the affordance follows the site's A23 design; two degradation lines. Reaches: §0·4, §0 module table, every design's module line, A23, FR-J4, register 45(c).
- **spec-incomplete** — **§0·3 Actions (Portal targets)** — Evidence: register 45(c): "`#/portal/…` fragments do nothing with JavaScript off — no registry module can fix this and the specs now say so instead of inventing a fallback." Every A1 design's Sign in/Subscribe/Account default is a Portal action (`signin`, `signup`, `account`, `account/plans` — FR-F6) and **no A1 design's JS-off line says the buttons are inert**. Verdict: buildable; the sentence is missing sixteen times. Reaches: §0·3, §1–§16 JS-off lines, P0·4, register 45(c).
- **spec-incomplete** — **§0·3 the free-member upgrade ask (`account/plans`)** — Evidence: FR-H6 / build-contract carry-forward: "every paid CTA gates on `@site.paid_members_enabled` + tiers filtered `type:paid+visibility:public`". The slot ships off in A1 but the editor offers it (P0·4 defaults, lines 187–189); neither A1 nor P0·4 states the gate. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — the P0·4 Paid/Upgrade link compiles inside the FR-H6 gate. Reaches: §0·3, P0·4, FR-H6, A30/A32 (same gate).
- **spec-incomplete** — **A1·4 Accessibility "AA is checked against the scrimmed image"** — Evidence: for `post.hbs` heroes the image is `post.feature_image`, unknown at edit time; A24 §9 (line 454) resolves the same problem as "contrast stated as advice rather than computed… rather than the section computing an image's luminance". A1·4 claims a computed check and an auto-pick ("Match pack", "choosing None disables the Light/Dark auto-pick and warns") that cannot run over a bound image. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — computed for authored heroes, advisory (A24's rule) for bound ones. Reaches: §4 Controls/Accessibility, A24 line 454/460.
- **consistent** (useful) — **A1·3 `reading-progress` "post and page templates only; disabled elsewhere with the reason shown"** — on a `default.hbs` singleton this compiles to `{{#is "post, page"}}` (universal set, appendix-b1 §2); the control is global, the guard is per render. Also consistent: `@site.logo` may be empty (research line 131) and every design's "no logo → wordmark as text" honours it; `@site.title` is seeded and never empty (line 129), so `siteTitle (req)` holds; `@site.description` may be cleared (line 130) and the tagline empty state covers it.

#### 2 · Contradictions

- **stale-design** — **`nav-transform` "flagged, not coined"** (§0·5 "no module name is coined", §0 module table "ARCHITECT: `nav-transform`… flagged, not coined", §2, §6, §7, §18 item 5) — D2 (ruled 2026-08-24) coined it: "a new registry module, `nav-transform`". The waiver text is honoured exactly ("Without JS the nav renders Ghost's flat list as-is — prefixes visible, one level. That is the module's whole degradation line, and nothing is designed for that case"; §21 note 18 calls it the one waived place) — only the coinage is stale, and §0 finding 1's "a thirty-second module" numbering is wrong once `nav-transform` and `contact-form` (D28) land. Reaches: spec §0·5, §0 table, §2, §6, §7, §18 item 5; registry §2.1 (new row) and §7 (new sentence = the spec's owner-ruling text); FR-G7 count.
- **stale-design** — **A1·3 date "client-computed by `core`'s date stamp"** (§3, §21 note 17) — contradicts D13's premise ("No registry module renders client-side dates") and registry §2.1 row 0 (`core` has no date facility). A client-computed date **is** the deferred `local-date` module under another name. Ruling: contradiction — the Site-timezone value is server-rendered with the D13 caveat (§1 above). Reaches: §3 "The date", §3 Accessibility (`<time>` datetime is then server-set), §0·7, §21 note 17, D13.
- **stale-design** — **A1·9 "most-read posts"** (§9 Behaviour module JS-off line, Data, Empty state, Flagged) — the Data & FR-H2 carry-forward: "'Most read' does not exist as data — struck from A23"; A23 spec line 211: "'Most read' is struck — no view counts reach a theme"; A23's `beforeQuery` offers Featured/Latest/Nothing. Reaches: §9 (four mentions), A23 source group, FR-H2.
- **stale-design** — **D6 Count stepper** — A1·7 "Show: Three · Four · Six" and A1·9 "Results at a time: 5 · 8 · 10" are fixed count enums; D6: "One stepper with per-design min/max and locked values drawn disabled replaces them all." Reaches: §7 Data block, §9 Controls, D6, Appendix C Stepper row.
- **stale-design** — **D3: A1·9 and A23 own the same index settings** — `Search in` (A1·9 "Titles and excerpts · Full content" = A23 `searchIn`, same values) and `Match highlight` ("Marked · Plain" = A23 `matchMark`) are owned by both, yet `search-overlay` builds **one** site index — two values with no precedence. Same names, different value sets: Result meta (A1·9 "Show · Hide" vs A23 "Section, author, date · Section and date · Date · Off"), results count (A1·9 "5 · 8 · 10" vs A23 `resultCap` "10 · 20 · 50 · All matches"), pre-query (A1·9 "Recent, then results · Results only · Off" vs A23 `beforeQuery` "Recent searches, then featured · Featured posts · Latest posts · Nothing"), minimum (A1·9 hard-codes 3 as "mine"; A23 `minChars` 2·3·4 says "A1·9's minimum"). Fix: index-scope settings (`searchIn`, `matchMark`, `minChars`) are site-level, owned once (A23's source group), read by A1·9; A1·9 keeps only its field/panel controls. Reaches: §9 Controls/Data/Flagged, A23 lines 209–215, D3, FR-F7.
- **stale-design** — **D10 / appendix-h1 strings** — (a) "More", "Menu", "Close" are made **fields** (`moreLabel`, `menuLabel`, `closeLabel`, §0·7) though the catalog owns them as chrome: `nav.more`, `nav.menu`, `nav.close` (§3.11) — one string, two homes. (c) A1·9's "No matches for '…' — try a tag" diverges from the existing pair `search.overlay_no_results` + `search.overlay_no_results_hint` ("Try a different word."). (d) `aria-label="Primary"` / `"Secondary"` (§0 floor, §8) are hard-coded English where `a11y.main_navigation` exists and `a11y.secondary_navigation` would be needed. Reaches: §0·7, §0 floor, §6, §7, §8, §9, §14, appendix-h1 §3.7/§3.11/§3.12, FR-Q6.

Reaches: §11, §13, §15 (+ frame), §16, FR-F2, Appendix C "Forbidden anywhere at section level".
- **stale-design** — **FR-F7 union collisions** — one control name needs one domain for park-and-restore (FR-D19): A1·11 "Actions (Pinned to the foot · Under the nav)" is a *placement* control wearing the category-wide "Actions (None · Sign in · Subscribe · Sign in + Subscribe)" name; "Wordmark size" has two value sets (A1·2 Small · Medium · Large; A1·15 Large · Larger · Largest); "On scroll" has nine (Static·Sticky·Shrink / Static·Re-form left·Hide / Static·Nav row sticks·Whole header sticks / Stay transparent·Solidify to surface·Solidify to contrast / Static·Stick·Stick and narrow / Static·Main bar sticks·Whole header sticks / Static·Stick and fill·Hide / Static·Collapse to bar·Hide). Rename A1·11's to "Actions placement"; declare the union domain for the other two. Reaches: §2, §11, §15, §1–§16 On scroll rows, FR-F7, FR-D19, inventory line 55.

- **ghost-infeasible** — **A1·4 "or its image fails to load"** (§4 Data) — a load failure exists only in the browser; a server-side precondition cannot fall back to Rail on it, and the spec forbids itself a JS fallback. Strike the clause or name the module (none exists). Reaches: §4 Data, §0 finding 2.

#### 5 · Spec completeness

- **Ten fields:** all sixteen carry Descriptor · Structural descriptor · Archetype · Responsive · Content fields · Controls (tables on 1–4, 6, 8, 9, 11, 15; prose lists on 5, 7, 10, 12, 13, 14, 16) · Data · Empty state · Behaviour (module line + Behaviour paragraph) · Accessibility. Complete.
- **Tuples:** all sixteen are six slots (§19 table). First five are closed-vocabulary throughout — archetype ∈ {bar ×7, stack ×3, overlay ×2, split, form, edge rail, sticky}; containment ∈ {none ×14, pill, box}; ground ∈ {page ×11, surface ×3, contrast, transparent ×2}; count ∈ {few ×8, many ×7, variable}; media ∈ {none ×12, background, inline, edge, top}. No off-vocabulary word. **Six-slot uniqueness passes. One first-five collision:** **A1·1 Rail / A1·13 Centre Nav** — `bar · none · page · few · none`, separated by the emphasis slot only (the spec admits it, §19: "If any pair in A1 is to be merged into one design with a Nav-position control, it is this one"). Register 46 is the class.
- **[Free]:** no marker on any design (inventory: two). Listed in §2.
- **No-JS lines per declared module (tally, per design):** `header-scroll`, `accordion`, `nav-drawer` sentences are quoted on every design that declares them **except A1·9** (declares `accordion` and `nav-drawer`, quotes neither). `mode-toggle` is declared on all sixteen and its sentence quoted on **A1·8 and A1·14 only** (§0·4 quotes it once category-wide; FR-G7(3) requires restatement per design). `search-overlay` is declared on A1·6 and A1·9, quoted on A1·9 only — and is invoked on fourteen more (§3). `carousel` and `reading-progress` (A1·3) quoted. `core` "not repeated" by the spec's own rule. `nav-transform`'s line is the owner ruling, present where declared (§0·5, §2, §6, §7).
- **Lists:** every authored list (children, grandchildren, `stripItems[]`, `panelColumns[]`, `links[]`, social extras) carries P0·3 add/remove/reorder with placeholder content named (§20); every Ghost-bound list carries none and the Ghost-list card (§20) — except `panelTags[]`'s ownership is unstated (§3). The Social row in §20 mixes Ghost fields (no handle) and authored extras (P0·3) in one list — stated, acceptable.
- **Control counts:** max ten listed (A1·3, A1·9) — under the ≈ 15 cap; universal trio outside all lists (D7 honoured); no Preview control (P0·8 honoured); D26 gap names on A1·13 (honoured); D1 Tabler named on A1·14 (honoured); D9 link options in §0·2 (honoured).

#### Needs execution (this category)

- **NE-A1-1** — `default.hbs` can read the current post's `feature_image` inside a block — probe (T1 6.58.0, T3 5.130.6): a fixture theme whose `default.hbs` contains `{{#is "post, page"}}{{#post}}{{#if feature_image}}<meta name="x-hero" content="yes">{{else}}<meta name="x-hero" content="no">{{/if}}{{/post}}{{/is}}`; render one post with a feature image, one without, and `/`; expected: `yes`/`no`/nothing. Also gscan the fixture for a `{{#post}}` warning. Settles §0 finding 2's server-side half; the "fails to load" half is client-only regardless.
- **NE-A1-2** — `{{date}}` at the `default.hbs` root renders today in `@site.timezone` — probe: `<time datetime="{{date format="YYYY-MM-DD"}}">{{date format="D MMMM YYYY"}}</time>` in `default.hbs`; render `/`, a post, a tag; T1 with timezone set to `Asia/Kolkata` at 01:00 IST (UTC previous day); expected: the IST date on all three; then confirm the page-cache staleness window on Ghost(Pro)-like caching (D13 caveat wording).
- **NE-A1-3** — `{{#foreach @site.secondary_navigation}}{{label}}→{{url}}{{/foreach}}` in `default.hbs` on T1 and T3 with two secondary items set; expected: both rows; compare with `{{navigation type="secondary"}}`.
- **NE-A1-4** — the seven ≥ 6.36 social fields: on T1 set Bluesky to a handle and to a full URL in Ghost Admin; render `{{@site.bluesky}}` and `{{social_url type="bluesky"}}`; on T3 render the same and gscan the fixture; expected: the field's stored shape, whether `social_url` accepts the new `type`, and no gscan error on 5.x for a guarded `{{#if @site.bluesky}}`.
- **NE-A1-5** — `{{#get "tags" limit="1" include="count.posts" as |t pages|}}{{pages.total}}{{/get}}` and `{{#get "authors" include="count.posts" order="count.posts desc" limit="3"}}` in `default.hbs` on T1/T3 against the 32-post fixture; expected: 6 and the three authors in descending post count.

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **needs-execution** — **§0 Visibility group (Schedule: From date · Until date · Between dates) and A2-6 Countdown (a page rendered after `endsAt` "carries the expired sentence server-side")** — claim: "dates are server-evaluated". Evidence: no companion names a server-side date comparison. `{{date}}` with no context renders the current date in the site timezone (`research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` line 721; Casper `default.hbs` uses `{{date format="YYYY"}}` for the year); `{{#match}}` compares values (`appendix-b1` §6 table, gscan GS090 note: "use `{{#match}}` to compare"); Handlebars subexpressions would give `{{#match (date format="YYYY-MM-DD") ">=" "2026-09-05"}}`, but nothing in the research has executed that shape, and `appendix-b1` §5 warns helpers do not run inside `filter` strings (a different place, but the same class of surprise). D13's caveat ("an expired bar may show until the cache turns") is honoured in the panel text — the mechanism that produces the staleness is not named. Verdict: **needs execution** (NE-A2-1). Reaches: A2 spec §0 "The Visibility group", A2-6 Behaviour module, D13, Appendix C Date Picker row, PRD §7.3 missing-construct table (a new construct: server-side date comparison — see amendments).
- **stale-design** — **A2-7 Dateline, Meta: Latest post date** — claim: "reads `published_at` — the current post's on a post template, the newest published post's everywhere else". Evidence: A2 compiles into `default.hbs` (inventory line 73, FR-D5); `appendix-b1` §3 `default` row: "Inherits the child render's root, so bare resource fields are empty on every render … Anything resource-specific requires `{{#get}}`"; `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` §4: "Cross-context safety: what is safe in `default.hbs` is `@site`, `@custom`, `@member`, `@config`, `{{navigation}}`, `{{#is}}` guards". A `{{#is "post"}}{{#post}}{{date}}{{/post}}{{/is}}` arm would probably work (the layout shares the child's root, which carries `post` on entry renders) but the FR-H7 matrix marks it un-offerable on `default.hbs`, and the two-armed shape is §7.3 missing-construct 3. Verdict: **buildable with a stated change** — either Meta: Latest post date is always `{{#get "posts" limit="1" order="published_at desc"}}` (one query, no route awareness), or `appendix-b1` §3's `default` row gains a guarded `{{#is "post"}}{{#post}}` pattern after NE-A2-3 proves it. Reaches: A2 spec §7 Data, `appendix-b1` §3 (`default` row), FR-H7, §7.3 item 3, the route-awareness carry-forward (Product mechanisms).
- **consistent** — **§0 posts source, A2-12 Content source, A2-7 Latest post title** — `{{#get "posts"}}` in `default.hbs` is legal: `research-ghost-membership-pages.md` line 447 ("an ordinary async helper with no context dependency"), `appendix-b1` §4 `default` row ("Requires `{{#get}}`: anything resource-specific"). Counts (≤ 6, 1, 1) are under FR-H2's 100. One consequence the spec should carry: `appendix-b1` §5 — a slow `{{#get}}` is **aborted** and yields an empty collection plus a visible `<span data-aborted-get-helper>`; the §0 zero-items floor ("the section does not render") must apply to that state too, so the span never sits alone above the header. Reaches: A2 spec §0 "Posts as a source", §8/§9/§15 Data, §12 Data.
- **needs-execution** — **§0 posts source at Hand-picked (P0·5: "drag reorders … the picked list is the count and the order"), A2-12 Hand-picked** — claim: authored pick order is drawn order. Evidence: the only compilable shape is `{{#get "posts" filter="id:[a,b,c]"}}` (`appendix-b1` §5 query shapes); NQL's `id:[…]` is a set membership test and the result comes back in the query's `order` (default `published_at desc`), never in list order — no companion has executed the contrary. Library-wide (D5), first reached by A2 here. Verdict: **needs execution** (NE-A2-2); if confirmed, the compiler emits one `{{#get}}` per pick or the reorder claim is dropped from P0·5. Reaches: A2 spec §0, §8/§9/§12/§15 Data, P0·5 Hand-picked row, D5, A3-9, FR-H2.
- **spec-incomplete** — **A2-6 Countdown, `endsAt` "site time zone from Ghost" and the inside-24-hours sentence "ends tonight at 23:59 (UK)"** — claim: the module names the time and the zone. Evidence: `@site.timezone` exists and is seeded `Etc/UTC` (Appendix B; `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` line 137); the module's strings are `data-i18n-*` (`appendix-h1` §3.3a — six `countdown.*` keys, none of which is a time-and-zone sentence); `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with `timeZone` is Baseline, so formatting a fixed instant in the site zone client-side is not the deferred `local-date` (D13 — that was the *visitor's* clock). "(UK)" is not derivable from an IANA name (`Europe/London` gives GMT/BST). Verdict: **buildable with a stated change** — the compiler emits the absolute instant on `datetime` plus `data-timezone="{{@site.timezone}}"`, and the sentence becomes a catalog key with `{time}` and `{zone}` placeholders (S3), the zone being the IANA name or a site-authored label. Reaches: A2 spec §6 Content fields/Behaviour, `appendix-h1` §3.3a, FR-Q6, D13.
- **spec-incomplete** — **A2-5 Capture, `member-form`** — claim: "posts to Ghost's members subscribe endpoint … an already-subscribed address gets Ghost's response, shown in the success slot … members off → button linking to the site's subscribe page". Evidence: Ghost's contract is `data-members-form` with values `signin` · `signup` · `subscribe` plus `data-members-email` (Appendix B; `research-ghost-membership-pages.md` line 409); the spec names neither the form value nor the email attribute; Ghost writes **its own** server message into `[data-members-error]` (`appendix-h1` §3.4 "Precision on error strings" — not catalog-controlled), so "the error line is a catalog string that matches what the API rejected" is only true for the theme's client-side validation keys `member.error_*`; "the site's subscribe page" is undefined — with members disabled there is no Portal signup and `@site.signup_url`'s value in that state is unverified (`appendix-b1` §6 lists it as a Ghost-5 field, nothing more). If the substitute link is `#/portal/…`, register 45(c) requires the spec to say the fragment does nothing with JS off — it does not. Verdict: **buildable with a stated change** (name `data-members-form="subscribe"` + `data-members-email`, split the error copy into Ghost's message vs `member.error_*`, define the members-off target) + **needs execution** (NE-A2-5, NE-A2-6). Reaches: A2 spec §5 Behaviour module/Content fields/Data/States, Appendix B `data-members-*`, FR-H6 (members-disabled warning — the spec substitutes silently), register 45(c), A3-4 (same claims).
- **needs-execution** — **A2-7 Dateline, Custom date (Date Picker) drawn at three lengths ("Wednesday 12 March" / "Wed 12 Mar" / "12 Mar") in the site's language** — claim: server-rendered. Evidence: `{{date}}` formats a value in the site locale (`appendix-h1` §5: date output is Ghost's), but every documented use passes a post field; a literal ISO string as the first parameter (`{{date "2026-03-12" format="dddd D MMMM"}}`) is undocumented. Verdict: **needs execution** (NE-A2-4); the fallback is compile-time formatting in the project language, which then ignores a site-locale change made later in Ghost Admin. Reaches: A2 spec §7 Data/Responsive, FR-Q6 (locale), Appendix G RTL/date note.
- **consistent** — **§0 Audience (Everyone · Logged out · Free members · Paid members), members-disabled collapse** — `{{#if @member}}` server-side (FR-G7 rule 5, Appendix C Member Visibility row); Free vs Paid is `@member.paid` / `status` and is §7.3 missing-construct 4's subject (owned there); `@member` is `null` when members are disabled entirely, so the collapse-to-Everyone rule is safe (`appendix-b1` §2). The control is the PRD's **Member Visibility / show to** under the local name `audience` — carry the PRD name into the inventory entry at merge (line 81 "show to").
- **consistent** — **A2-12 Takeover `imageAlt` (empty = decorative) and Image focus in the Image Picker popover** — FR-H8 media guard hides the element; focus is one `data-image-focus` attribute (AD-3). Useful only because the spec says "never a hidden field": it *is* a stored value and compiles as an attribute like any control.

#### 2 · Contradictions
- **stale-design** — **§0 "One A2 per site" + A2-11 Toast and A2-13 Notice "may coexist with one top bar"** contradicts **FR-D5**: site-wide sections are "single shared instances … cannot be duplicated" and A2 is one of the three singletons compiled into `default.hbs` (inventory line 73, Synthesis Defaults §2). The spec licenses up to three A2 instances (top + Toast + Notice) with no rule for how Layers, the Site-wide group or the compiler hold them. Flag, not guess: the owner must rule (one A2 singleton and the two floats become a second slot, or FR-D5 gains "one top bar plus optional bottom-anchored instances"). Reaches: A2 spec §0 Placement, §11 Data, §13 Data, FR-D5, inventory line 73, Synthesis Defaults §2, A3-16 (reserves space for "a bottom-anchored A2·13").
- **stale-design** — **"Edit-safe" is defined backwards.** A2 preamble: "Edit-safe means the module does not run while the section is being edited … All seven are edit-safe, which is why every frame is a resting state." **FR-D20**: "edit-safe modules — sticky/shrink headers, scroll reveal, tabs, accordions — **run always**, because designing their open and closed states requires it; the rest **wait for Preview**" — and FR-D20 names "a rotator that swaps content mid-edit, a marquee that slides text from under the cursor" as exactly the behaviours that must *not* run. Under the PRD's definition `rotator`, `marquee`, `countdown`, `slide-in-card`, `member-form` and `dismiss` are **edit-safe: no** (they wait for Preview) and only `accordion` (14 Edge) is edit-safe. The carry-forward "lightbox is the only edit-safe: no module" was written under the same inverted reading, so this is library-wide. Reaches: A2 preamble, every "Edit-safe" line in §1–§15, FR-D20, the Registry carry-forward (`lightbox` line), A3 preamble (same sentence), P0·8.
- **stale-design** — **A2-9 Rotator: "Only Dots can be pressed to stop the rotation; with Numbers or None, hover, focus and reduced-motion carry the whole burden"** contradicts the registry's normative a11y verdict for `rotator` (`research-section-js-libraries.md` §3.1: "WCAG 2.2.2 … auto-rotating content over 5 s **needs a pause control**") and FR-G4's AA guarantee. Hover and focus are not operable on touch, and Indicators: None ships 4–8 s auto-rotation with no stop. Reaches: A2 spec §9 Controls (Indicators), §9 Motion, §9 Accessibility, registry §3.1 `rotator`.
- **stale-design** — **A2-8 Ticker at ≤ 767: "the pause button leaves the bar … its job passes to tap-to-pause"** contradicts registry §3.1 `marquee`: "a **visible** pause control is mandatory, not optional". A pause that appears only after a tap, on a strip where the first tap intercepts the link, is neither visible nor discoverable; the spec's own accessibility line ("stays in the accessibility tree at every width") describes a hidden control. Reaches: A2 spec §8 Responsive/Accessibility, registry §3.1 `marquee`.
- **arch-gap** — **A2-8 Ticker under `prefers-reduced-motion`: "message 1, centred, with A2·9's three dots at the right end and no auto-advance … identical to Rotator"** — the registry's `marquee` is "hard stop under `prefers-reduced-motion`" (§3.1) and its §7 line is a static scrollable row; the spec makes marquee's reduced-motion branch *rotator's manual state* (dots, press-to-advance). That is the "marquee's reduced-motion-vs-no-JS precedence" ruling the Registry carry-forward already owes, with a new twist: the branch now needs rotator's markup and script. Owner: Registry carry-forward (`marquee`) — owned, but the spec's answer must reach it. Reaches: A2 spec §8 Motion, A2-0 convergence note, registry §3.1/§7 `marquee`, `rotator`.
- **arch-gap** — **A2-14 Edge, Opens on: Hover and focus, and Escape-to-collapse** — `accordion` is `<details>/<summary>` and "~0.2 KB, and *only* for single-open groups and A9's default state" (registry §3.1). Hover-open and Escape are behaviours no module names; the spec admits Hover degrades to Click with JS off but never says which module runs it with JS on. P0·8 rule 4: an instruction needing behaviour no module covers is marked ARCHITECT: registry addition — it is not. Owner: **no owner; needs one** (drop the value, or `accordion` grows a hover/Escape option). Reaches: A2 spec §14 Controls/Accessibility/Behaviour module, registry §3.1 `accordion`, P0·8 rule 4.
- **stale-design** — **Scale labels borrowed:** A2-10 "Air around it: Close · **Comfortable** · Far" borrows the universal Vertical spacing label for a different ladder. Appendix C: "Scale vocabularies are closed and distinct … no surface invents a fourth value or borrows another scale's labels"; D7 said genuinely different ladders are *renamed*. Reaches: A2 spec §10 Controls, Appendix C scale table.
- **stale-design** — **Swatch Row value "Background"** in every A2 Background role row (§2, §3, §5, §7, §9, §12, §13) and the tuple ground `page`: Appendix C and the inventory's universal-controls line name the roles **Base / Surface / Accent / Contrast / Image**, and the Synthesis Defaults set "Background role **Base**". "Background" is a fourth name for one role. Reaches: A2 controls tables ×7, Appendix C Swatch Row row, inventory universal-controls line, A3 (same drift).
- **prd-defect** — **§7.3 missing-construct item 1 lists 11 categories with authored arrays and omits A2**, which now carries `messages[]` (2–6, authored, baked at compile as N static blocks per that row) — and register 44's discrepancy note names A3 and A23 but not A2 either. Reaches: PRD §7.3 item 1 (list and the "~166 designs" count), register 44, D12.
- **prd-defect** — **Registry §2.1 rows still cite retired A2 designs and one module is now orphaned:** row 6 `dismiss` "A2 #2 Slim Dismissable intrinsic", row 7 `rotator` "A2 #9 up to 3 crossfading" (the spec ships 2–6), row 9 `marquee` "A2 #3", and row 10 **`confetti` "A2 #15 Seasonal Confetti" — no design in the export declares it** (A2 §"Modules A2 deliberately does not use" names it). FR-G7 rule 2: a module ships with its section; a module with no section is dead weight in the registry and in FR-G4's "only `confetti` and `toc` render nothing" sentence. Reaches: registry §2.1 rows 6/7/9/10, §7 `confetti`, FR-G4, FR-G7(3), inventory line 96 (#15).
- **prd-defect** — **Appendix G is "binding in both directions" and lists neither deferral A2 now carries:** `local-date` (D13 — "the visitor's-clock option is deferred") and the `consent` module (D4 — "recorded as the upgrade path, deferred"; A2 spec §13 and Findings 1: ARCHITECT: registry addition (`consent`)). Reaches: Appendix G, D4, D13, register 45(a), A2 spec §13.
- **spec-incomplete** — **Strings (D10 / FR-Q6 / `appendix-h1`).** (a) Keys the spec needs that the catalog lacks: `<aside aria-label="Announcement">` / "Announcements" / "Site notice" (a11y.*), Edge's "Show announcement" (nav.*), Ticker's "Pause announcements" / "Play announcements" (JS), Rotator's "Show announcement {n} of {total}" (JS), Countdown's "ends tonight at {time} ({zone})" (JS), Notice's "Dismiss notice". (b) `nav.announcement_dismiss` exists with default "Dismiss" — the spec writes "Dismiss announcement"; use the key (S2 permits revising the default). (c) **S6 violated in the other direction:** a catalog string that becomes a field takes the catalog default as its initial value — A2-5's `emailPlaceholder` default "you@example.com" vs `member.email_placeholder` "Your email address"; `successMessage` "You're in. Check your inbox to confirm the address." vs `member.signup_success` "You're in. Welcome aboard."; "Subscribing…" vs `member.sending` "Sending…". Either the fields start from the catalog defaults or the catalog defaults are revised at merge. Reaches: A2 spec §0 "Editing on canvas", §5 Content fields/States, §6, §8, §9, §13, §14; `appendix-h1` §3.3a, §3.4, §3.11, §3.12; FR-Q6.

- **spec-incomplete** — **Ghost's own announcement bar is absent from the spec.** Inventory lines 74–80 (Appendix A §2 — the "takes over" rule), FR-C4 (seed: text → message, `announcement_visibility` → show to, `announcement_background` → Background role; one-click "turn Ghost's bar off"; declining leaves both bars), FR-H5(2) (the shim strip at the top of the canvas, occupying real height, honouring the member-state toggle) and register 21 (closed: all three settings readable) — none is mentioned. Reaches: A2 spec §0 Placement / Compact ceiling / Height and reflow / Above A1·4 Overlay, inventory lines 74–80, FR-C4, FR-H5(2), FR-D16 (the strip follows the member-state toggle), register 21.

Two facts to state: `home` matches the site root only — `/page/2/` is `index` (`research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` line 74), so "Home only" is absent from page 2 by construction; and this is the route-awareness mechanism the carry-forward names for A24/A26/A27/A28 — A2 (and A3's Site-wide "Shows on") are consumers five and six. #### 4 · Architecture asks
- **arch-gap** — **`dismiss` "read before paint so a dismissed bar never flashes" (§0 Height and reflow) needs a synchronous inline head script.** FR-J4: `main.js` is `defer`red; PRD line 463: "no render-blocking JS — every theme script is `defer`red or `type="module"`". Registry §3.1 grants `mode-toggle` "a tiny inline head script to avoid the flash" — the only precedent. Either `dismiss` joins that exception (one inline script reading `localStorage` and setting a class before first paint) or the no-flash sentence is withdrawn. Owner: FR-J4 / registry §3.1 `dismiss` row — **no owner for the exception; needs one**. Reaches: A2 spec §0 Height and reflow, §0 Dismissal, FR-J4, PRD line 463 (NFR performance), registry §3.1.
- **arch-gap** — **`dismiss` storage and TTL.** Registry §3.1: `localStorage` + a content-hash key. The spec adds `dismissMemory` (This session · 30 days · Never comes back · Always shows) — a TTL and a sessionStorage branch the module does not have — and "Success counts as dismissed" (A2-5) makes `member-form` write `dismiss`'s record. The hash must be of *rendered* content (bound post titles change without a redeploy), so it is computed client-side, not at compile. Owner: registry §3.1 `dismiss` (owned); the cross-module write is new. Reaches: A2 spec §0 Dismiss memory, §5 States, registry §3.1 `dismiss`, `member-form`.
- **arch-gap** — **The combined sticky offset (bar + header, recomputed on dismissal, written to every anchor's `scroll-margin-top`).** The spec assigns the measurement to `header-scroll`; registry §3.1 `header-scroll` is "IO on a zero-height sentinel" and says `scroll-margin-top` "handles WCAG 2.4.11 in CSS" — nothing measures a second element or publishes a sum. With JS off, the header's sticky `top` must equal the bar's height, which the spec says is "measured, never assumed" — a CSS-only fallback needs the bar's ladder px as a custom property per breakpoint. Owner: **no owner; needs one** (`header-scroll` or `core` publishes `--sticky-offset`; the A1 spec is the other consumer). Reaches: A2 spec preamble "Placement: Sticky declares no module", §0 Height and reflow, §0 Dismissal, §10 Accessibility, registry §3.1 `header-scroll`, A1 spec.
- **arch-gap** — **`slide-in-card` grows on A2-11 Toast:** Appears (Immediately · After 2 seconds · After 25% scroll) vs the module's "IO on a near-footer sentinel"; Escape-anywhere key handler; Position; stacking "12 px above the Notice bar" needs the Notice's rendered height (CSS anchor positioning is not Baseline). The carry-forward's "slide-in-card must name its dismissal storage" is answered here: `dismiss`. Owner: Registry carry-forward (`slide-in-card`) — owned for storage; the trigger/Escape/stacking options are new. Reaches: A2 spec §11 Controls/Motion/Placement against other fixed things/Accessibility, §13 Data, registry §3.1 `slide-in-card`, A3-16 (same module).
- **arch-gap** — **A2-15 Triple: module set changes with width** (`dismiss` above 768, `rotator` below) and the design hands off to another design's markup at a breakpoint. The registry has no width-conditional activation and FR-G4 has designs collapse under their own archetype; the spec records it as Finding 3 and leaves it to the architect. Owner: **no owner; needs one**. Reaches: A2 spec §15 Behaviour module/Responsive, Findings 3–4, FR-G4, registry §7 `rotator`.
- **arch-gap** — **Pack-token asks A2 adds to the carry-forward family** (Product mechanisms: on-accent/on-contrast as real tokens, tabular figures, dark hover-surface step): §0 "Accent on contrast" (inverted button = lightest surface on contrast), A2-6 "numerals are tabular, a requirement on the pack's body font", A2-9's dark inactive-dot `#453E35` "that no pack defines", A2-10/A2-11's dark shadow `0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,.32)` ("the brief's two shadows are both light-mode"). Owner: carry-forward pack-token asks — owned; add A2 as consumer. Reaches: A2 spec §0, §6, §9, §10, §11, Reconciliation note 14, Style Pack token list (FR-E1).
- **consistent** — **D4 honoured; register 45(a) closes.** A2-13 is Notice, carries `dismiss`, records nothing, gates nothing; the upgrade path is ARCHITECT: registry addition (`consent`) on the frame and in Findings 1. Propagate: register 45(a) → closed by D4 (2026-08-24); Appendix G gains the deferral (see Contradictions).
- **consistent** — **D12 (bars pull posts).** The posts source lives on the shared list with the P0·5 panel; `bindingContext` stays `none` under the inventory's Data-group opt-in precedent (line 51: "A7's tiers, A12's optional authors and A15's optional posts are Data-group opt-ins, not context changes"), so the Shuffle ring needs no FR-D13 partition — the architect records that reading or partitions anyway (owner-flag row).
- **consistent** — **D13 honoured:** no client-side date module is declared or implied; Dateline offers Site-timezone `published_at` and a Date Picker Custom date only; the visitor's-browser value is "deferred by owner ruling — not offered"; Schedule ships the staleness caveat verbatim. The countdown's zone-named time (Feasibility above) is a formatting question, not `local-date`.

#### 5 · Spec completeness
- **Ten fields:** Descriptor · Structural descriptor · Archetype · Responsive · Content fields · Controls · Data · Empty state · Behaviour module · Accessibility are present on all 15; an explicit **Items** field on all 15 (P0·3). "Behaviour" as a named field is absent on §5, §12, §13, §15 (Gaps).
- **Tuples:** 15 tuples, six slots each. First five closed-vocabulary throughout: archetypes {bar ×9, stack, form, carousel, overlay, split, grid-of-N}; containment {none ×13, card ×2}; ground {contrast ×4, surface ×5, page ×4, accent}; count {one ×12, variable ×2, few}; media {none ×14, left}. **Unique within the category: yes.** **First-five collisions (separated only by the emphasis slot): three pairs** — 1 Rule / 6 Countdown (`bar · none · contrast · one · none`), 3 Badge / 7 Dateline (`bar · none · page · one · none`), 2 Split / 13 Notice (`bar · none · surface · one · none`). The spec names all three; they are register-46-class (human judgement is the check). No off-vocabulary word in slots 1–5; "page" is the tuple ground while the control says "Background" (Contradictions).
- **Modules:** every declared module carries the registry §7 sentence, quoted, per design — `dismiss` ×15, `member-form` (5), `countdown` (6), `marquee` (8), `rotator` (9; 15 below 768), `slide-in-card` (11), `accordion` (14). `core` is stated once in the preamble, flagged. No invented names. The D2 waiver does not touch A2. Two no-JS statements are *contradicted by the spec's own a11y text*: §8 keeps a pause control "in the accessibility tree at every width" that the no-JS branch hides; §14 specifies `<button aria-expanded>` where `accordion` compiles `<details>` (spec Finding 2).
- **Lists:** `messages[]` carries Add (with content, lands last) / Remove (undoable, floor is a hand-off) / Reorder (drag, ⌥↑↓) on 8, 9, 15 — P0·3 ✓; bound (From posts) hides Add/Remove/drag and marks rows "From Ghost" ✓; the P0·3 Ghost-list sentence ("Add and remove them in Ghost — this design chooses how many to show, and in what order") is not quoted — minor. The twelve non-list designs state "None" explicitly ✓.
- **Controls:** largest own list is 6 rows (Rule, Split, Badge, Dateline, Countdown, Ticker, Rotator, Pill, Edge) plus the Visibility group (5) and the universal trio — under ≈ 15. Universal trio never appears in a design's own list ✓ (rows are labelled "(universal)" inside the tables, which is presentation, not membership). Px readings sit beside every named value (ladders, Speed "40 px/s", Field width "Narrow 200") — spec readings, not sidebar values ✓. Edge's "Chip label | Text, ≤ 14" duplicates the `chipLabel` content field as a control row (Text Field is a vocabulary type; harmless).
- **Plan gates:** none marked (Gaps).

- **stale-design** — **A3-16 Back to top is "a `<button>` named 'Back to top' that scrolls and then moves focus to the document's skip target"** — registry §2.2 lists Back-to-top for "A3 ×16 **+ A3 #16**" as `<a href="#top">` + `scroll-behavior: smooth` (no JS), and FR-G7 rule 5 makes that normative. The spec's own Finding 2 ships the anchor for fifteen designs and keeps the `<button>` on the sixteenth, where with JS off the control is "absent" — a real link would have worked. - **stale-design** — **Accordion at a breakpoint over one markup (A3-2, A3-3, A3-8; A3-7 and A3-14 at Links: Columns): "First-group-open is that `open` attribute; the counts are static text; what the module adds is the 160 ms transition and nothing else."** A `<details>` without `open` does not render its content at any width, and CSS cannot force it (the `::details-content` pseudo-element is not Baseline Widely on the 2026-08-18 pin, and FR-G8 Tier 2 forbids layout on Newly features). So server-rendered `open` on the first group alone collapses columns 2–7 **on desktop**. The only markup that works is `open` on every `<details>` with `accordion` removing it from groups 2+ below 768 — which makes the no-JS mobile state *all open*, not "first open", and turns the registry's "zero JS for the base case" into JS-required for the closed state. Reaches: A3 spec §2/§3/§7/§8/§14 Behaviour module + Responsive, Findings 3, registry §3.1/§7 `accordion`, FR-G8, A9 (`default state` control — same question), A2-14 (unaffected: always a disclosure).

#### 5 · Spec completeness
- **Ten fields:** Descriptor · Structural descriptor · Archetype · Behaviour module · Items · Content fields · Controls · Data · Responsive · Empty state · Accessibility on all 16 ✓ (A3-4 adds States; A3-16 adds Behaviour). Data at 0 / 1 / many is stated for every list (A3-9 posts "2–4, down to two, fewer → removed"; A3-13 "three is the floor"; columns per design) ✓.
- **Tuples:** 16 tuples, six slots each; slots 1–5 closed-vocabulary throughout — archetypes {bar, grid-of-N ×5, stack ×3, form, feed, article body, nav ×2, media frame, sticky}; containment {none ×15, card}; ground {page ×11, surface ×3, contrast, image}; count {none, variable ×4, one ×3, few ×5, many ×3}; media {none ×14, top, full-bleed}. **Unique within the category: yes. First-five collisions: none** — the closest pair (2 Columns / 8 Sitemap) separates on the count slot (`variable` vs `many`), as the spec says. No off-vocabulary word.
- **Modules:** `accordion` carries the registry §7 sentence on §2, §3, §7, §8, §14 ✓; `member-form` on §4 ✓; `slide-in-card` on §16 ✓; `nav-transform` carries the D2 sentence (no registry line exists yet); `core` once in the preamble (flagged). No invented names (the spec's own P0·8-compliant ARCHITECT marks on 2 and 11). D2 is the only no-JS gap ✓. Two declared no-JS statements are contradicted by the spec's own markup: §2/§3/§8 `<button aria-expanded aria-controls>` + `hidden` vs `<details>` (spec Finding 3), and the "first group open" claim (Contradictions).
- **Lists:** `linkColumns[]`, `legalLinks[]`, `social[]` extension, `credits[]`, `creditsGroups[]` carry Add-with-content / Remove (undoable; disabled at a design minimum with reason) / Reorder (drag, ⌥↑↓) ✓; Ghost-bound repeats carry none and say so ("no Add and no Remove … the sidebar says this in the posts group"; "Ghost-sourced rows never show an Add") ✓; the P0·3 Ghost-list sentence is paraphrased, not quoted — minor. The hybrid `social[]` is the one shape P0·3 lacks (Contradictions).
- **Controls:** largest own list is 7 (A3-14) + universal trio + Legal layout + Site-wide (3) — under ≈ 15 ✓; the universal trio never appears in a design's own list ✓ (locks with reasons on 3, 5, 14, 16 ✓ D7). Px readings beside named values are spec readings ✓. Off-vocabulary: "Footer below: Any A3 design" (a design-valued control); borrowed scale labels ×8 rows (Contradictions).
- **Plan gates:** FR-J15 ✓; [Free] unmarked (Gaps).

Reaches: inventory 119–138; FR-G1 (484 floor — unchanged, 18 = 18); FR-G7(1) (typed.js is the licence example — text survives, the module may not); research §2.1 rows 9/14/15/29 and §7 line 570; A4-10; register 45 (registry coverage).

3. **stale-design** — **"Edit-safe" is defined backwards** — spec preamble: "Edit-safe means the module does not run while the section is being edited and writes nothing to authored DOM. All four are edit-safe." FR-D20: "edit-safe modules — sticky/shrink headers, scroll reveal, tabs, accordions — **run always**, because designing their open and closed states requires it; the rest wait for Preview." The carry-forward uses the PRD's sense ("`lightbox` is the only 'edit-safe: no' module — state the editor-suppression guarantee"). Under the PRD's term A4's claim reads "all four run on the canvas", the opposite of what the spec means; and `lightbox` (needed on A4-10, next item) is the one module that is NOT edit-safe. A5's preamble carries the same inversion. Reaches: spec preamble; A5 preamble; FR-D20; §7.3; registry contract; carry-forward Registry.

The spec's "labelled `<button>` that opens a dialog with focus trapped and returned; A15 owns the player inside it" is `lightbox`'s mechanism by the registry's own definition, so A4-10 is a **multi-module section** (carry-forward: "multi-module sections … need an explicit blessing") that omits `lightbox`, its §7 line ("Each thumbnail is an `<a href>` to the full-size image" — for a video the same canonical URL as `video-facade`'s anchor, which is why the two coincide), and its consequence: `lightbox` is edit-safe: no, so the dialog never opens on the canvas and the open state is reached only through P0·6. The spec's finding 1 (button vs anchor) is real and is the same finding read from the other module. 5. **arch-gap** — **controls that move or remove markup contradict AD-3/§7.3** — A4-4 "Over the picture moves elements between two server-rendered positions rather than at runtime"; A4-10 "Over the poster works as it does in 4"; A4-12 "Header mode Below is a markup decision taken before render"; A4-8 "Card at 390"; A4-17 Arrangement (one right-slot occupant); A4-2 Below the sub (Note vs Proof row). Either these are CSS (`order`, grid areas, `display`) and the spec must say so — the prose says the opposite — or the table needs a 14th construct ("control-conditional markup"). 7. **arch-gap** — **same-named controls with different value sets break FR-D19's carry rule** — `Actions` is Both · Primary · None on the designs that have it (§0) but None · Primary on A4-7; `Headline size` has Display disabled on A4-18 and becomes `Headline scale` (Display · Huge · Fill width) on A4-6; `Alignment` is Centred · Left on 8/9/16 and Left · Centred on 17. #### 2 · Contradictions
1. **stale-design** — **the roster vs the inventory (normative for scope)** — `sections-inventory.md` 140–157 lists 16 named designs; 7 have no export counterpart (Big Icon Center, Accordion Features, Mini Cards Dense, Comparison Split, Sticky Scroll, Illustration Rows, Stat-Backed Cards) and 7 export designs are new. Registry consequences, keyed to inventory numbering: `accordion` row 11 loses "A5 #8" (15 → 14 designs; A9/A28 keep it alive), `scroll-spy` row 20 loses "A5 #12 Sticky Scroll" (2 → 1: A13 #6 alone, sharing its implementation with `toc`), `tabs` row 12's "A5 #9" is the export's #12, and `carousel` row 13 gains A5-14 (7 → 8) which it never listed. The brief's category checks ("accordion", "tabs A5-9", "scroll-spy on A5-12") are inventory numbers. D11 ruled A31's divergence; nothing rules A5's. Reaches: inventory 140–157; FR-G1 (16 = 16); research §2.1 rows 11/12/13/20 and §7 lines 552/553/554/561; A9; A13-6.
2. **spec-incomplete** — **[Free] markers absent** — the spec marks no tier; inventory #1/#2 are Icon Grid and Alternating Rows (one icon grid, one picture-and-copy design); the export's first two are Three Up and Two Up — two icon grids, so a Free user gets no feature design with a picture. FR-G2's mechanical rule is satisfied only if the merge takes export order. Reaches: FR-G2; Appendix F.1 (70); inventory 142–143; FR-L3 swap targets.
3. **stale-design** — **"Edit-safe" is defined backwards** — preamble: "Edit-safe means the module does not run while the section is being edited and writes nothing to authored DOM. Both are edit-safe"; A5-12: "Edit-safe: it does not run while the section is edited — the panel draws whichever item the sidebar has selected". FR-D20: "edit-safe modules — sticky/shrink headers, scroll reveal, **tabs**, accordions — **run always**, because designing their open and closed states requires it". The PRD names `tabs` as the canonical module that runs on the canvas; the spec replaces it with an editor mechanism (sidebar selection drives the panel) and calls the result edit-safe. Either is buildable; the term now means opposite things in the PRD and in two specs. Reaches: spec preamble, §12 Behaviour module/While editing, §14; A4 preamble; FR-D20; §7.3; P0·6.
4. **arch-gap** — **controls that remove markup contradict AD-3/§7.3** — A5-3 "Body copy Hide removes the paragraph from the DOM rather than hiding it visually … keeps the copy in the editor"; A5-13 "at Hidden the entries are absent server-side rather than hidden in the browser, so nothing is downloaded and unread … absent from the DOM"; A5-15 Compact "with the body dropped … the meta unavailable". AD-3: a control is one `data-{control}` attribute on the root and the stylesheet selects on it; §7.3: static attributes, zero runtime cost. No directive branches emitted markup on a control value, and `display: none` does not satisfy "nothing is downloaded" for pictures or "not found by in-page search". Either the spec accepts CSS hiding (and drops the DOM claims) or §7.3's table needs a 14th construct. Reaches: AD-3; §7.3 directive list + missing-construct table; spec §3, §13, §15; A4 report Contradictions 5 (same class).
5. **stale-design** — **A5-11's per-width content is per-breakpoint editing** — "At On a phone: Keep two columns the site may author a shorter wording for the phone, **the one piece of per-width content in A5** — it is a second string on the same entry" (flagged as the author's reading). FR-D8: "Sections are auto-responsive; there is no per-breakpoint editing"; Appendix G: per-breakpoint editing is deferred and "binding in both directions". A second string rendered only under one media query is per-breakpoint editing by definition. Same family: A5-11's "On a phone" and A5-7's "Alternate sides (no effect at ≤767)" are phone-scoped controls (A4-8, A4-18). Owner rules; until then the PRD wins and the second string goes (the "One column keeps the desktop wording" value already covers the need). Reaches: FR-D8; Appendix G; spec §11 Inside an item/Responsive; §7 Controls; A4 report Contradictions 8.
6. **arch-gap** — **per-design mode-specific values (and a hex) contradict AD-30 and FR-F2** — A5-1 "the container's dark-mode step to `#2B2620` on a surface ground"; A5-4 "`#2B2620` on a dark card" and "a hairline instead of the shadow in dark — A4·18's rule"; A5-8 "`brightness(.96)`, `1.04` in dark"; A5-10 "the icon's lift is dropped [in dark], with Icon the default and the substitution named"; A5-16 "a hairline and no shadow in dark". AD-30: only the token block and the base stylesheet mention a mode; a design stylesheet that does fails the build. FR-F2: no hex at section level (a hex in a spec is a reading, but this one names a value no pack token carries). The carry-forward's "dark hover-surface step (A17/A18/A19/A26/A34)" is exactly `#2B2620` — A5 is a sixth consumer; the shadow→hairline substitution and the brightness inversion are two more token asks. Reaches: AD-30; FR-E4; FR-F2; spec §1 Flagged, §4, §8, §10 Dark, §16; carry-forward Product mechanisms (pack tokens); A4 report Contradictions 6.
7. **arch-gap** — **same-named controls with different value sets break FR-D19's carry rule** — `Media`: Icon · Icon in a tint · Icon in accent · None (1) · "36 px container" (3) · Icon · Icon in a tint · None (5, 16) · Icon · **Icon in a lift** · None (10) · Picture · Icon · None (14) · split into Large tile media / Small tile media (9); `Item link`: None · Text link (1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 12) · + Whole item (4, 8, 9, 14, 16) · + Whole row (6) · "on the spotlight only" (13); `Head alignment`: Centred · Left (1) · Left · Centred, Left default (2, 6) · absent (11, 13, 15); `Below the set` (1, 2, 4, 8, 10, 11) vs `Below the head` (5). #### 5 · Spec completeness
- **Ten fields.** All sixteen carry Descriptor, Structural descriptor, Archetype, Responsive rule, Content fields, Controls, Empty, Behaviour and an explicit Accessibility line — the fullest category of the two. **Data** is stated on 8, 13, 14 only; §0's "Features are authored — there is no feature object in the API" covers the other thirteen, and the per-design "0, 1 and many" behaviour the inventory asks for is in each Items block ✓.
- **Tuples.** All sixteen are six slots; first five are closed-vocabulary throughout (`carousel`, `split`, `stack`, `grid-of-N`; `card`; `contrast`, `surface`; `few`, `variable`; `left`, `right`, `top`, `inline`). No off-vocabulary word. Unique within the category (the spec's own table; `tuple-check-specs.txt` OK). **First-five collisions:** **{1 Three Up, 3 Four Up, 4 Cards, 11 Checklist, 15 Index}** on `grid-of-N · none · page · many · none` — ten pairs separated only by the emphasis slot, the library's largest cluster (register 46). {2 Two Up} differs from the cluster on count; {16 Panel} on containment + ground; {5 Split Head} is alone on `split · none · page · many · none`; {7} and {13} share `split · none · page · … · left` and differ on count (`few`/`variable`); {12} and {14} share `carousel · none · page` and differ on count and media. 12's `carousel` for a `tabs` module is stated by the spec (and is a collapse-ladder question — Gaps).
- **Modules.** Two declared; both restate §7 verbatim (`tabs` line 553, `carousel` line 554). `core` assumed category-wide (flagged as the author's). Near misses refused in words: `count-up` (none needed), `scroll-spy` (5), `lightbox` (7, 8), `rotator` (12 — by the hand-off table). No coined name.
- **Lists.** `items[]` on all sixteen: add / remove / reorder per P0·3 by name ✓, per-design floors and ceilings stated ✓, placeholder content named (flagged as the author's) ✓, keep-on-switch ✓ (FR-D19), P0·3's partial-display line ("8 items · 3 shown") covered by "kept, counted in the sidebar and not drawn" ✓. Bound lists (8/13/14 at From posts): no Add/Remove/drag, "From Ghost", plain-text-locked ✓; Count/Order missing (Contradictions 10).
- **[Free].** 0 markers (Contradictions 2).
- **Strings.** Two arrow labels routed to the catalog with no key; one mis-stated (Contradictions 9). Everything else a reader sees is an authored field ✓.

## A6 · CTA Banners
**Counts (derived):** designs on disk 15 (frames 16 − `A6-0 Category Proof`) · spec 15 (`## 1`…`## 15`) · inventory 15 (`sections-inventory.md` line 159) · [Free] spec **0 marked** (the string `[Free]` does not occur in the spec) / inventory 2 (#1 Accent Band, #2 Boxed Border — by FR-G2's first-two rule the export's #1 Centred and #2 Flush Left) · modules declared: `member-form` (6, and 14 at Signup: Inline form) + `core` assumed once in the preamble — both registry names; the registry's own A6 entry (`research-section-js-libraries.md` §2.1 row 8, `countdown` — "A6 #11 Countdown CTA") is **not** declared by any design · custom-setting slots: 0 · authored lists: `reasons[]` (11 Reasons only) · Ghost-bound lists: none (7/8 bind one post through P0·5 at count one, 15 binds one staff user — single-item bindings, no list) · frames carry no template code at all (no `{{`, no `data-members-*`, no `data-portal` in any A6 frame — every binding claim below is checked against the spec's prose).

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **needs-execution** — **A6-6 Inline Form / A6-14 Members (Inline form) — `member-form`'s no-JS line** — claim (quoted from the registry): "The `<form>` posts natively to Ghost's members endpoint; Ghost's own server response replaces the designed sent state." — evidence: `research-section-js-libraries.md` §3 row `member-form` says the module is "`<form>` + `fetch`; Ghost's `data-members-form` contract"; `research-ghost-membership-pages.md` §4 says form state is exposed as `loading`/`success`/`error` **classes on the `<form>`** (script-driven) and §5 lists `/members/api/send-magic-link` and `/members/api/integrity-token` as JSON API routes; a `data-members-form` `<form>` carries no `action`, so a native submit is a GET of the current page — nothing posts, and no companion cites a server-rendered response. — verdict: **needs execution** (probe NE-A6-1). If it fails, A6's §0 sentence "no A6 design loses content without JavaScript" is false for 6 and 14, and the registry's row is a defect of the research companion, not of the spec. Reaches: spec preamble ("A6 uses one module"), A6-6 Behaviour module, A6-14 Behaviour module, roster "Findings, not gaps" bullet 3, registry §7 `member-form` row, FR-G7(3), FR-G4, the same row quoted by A22, A30 and A31-10, carry-forward "Build contract: members forms carry `data-members-form/-email/-name`".
- **ghost-infeasible** — **A6-15 Signature — Signer source: Ghost staff user** — claim: "bound, `signerName` ← the staff user's name and `portrait` ← their profile image" from "a chosen staff user". — evidence: the binding is `{{#get "authors"}}` (appendix-b1 §5 "Author list… `{{#get "authors"}}`"; `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` line 985), and the Content API's authors resource is the subset of users who have published posts (`docs.ghost.org/content-api/#authors` — "Authors are a subset of users who have published posts"); a staff user with no published post returns nothing, and FR-H8's text fallback plus the design's own empty rule ("No `signerName` → the design is 1 Centred at Left") swallow the failure silently. — verdict: **buildable with a stated change** — the picker offers only authors (the P0·5 author select already shows a post count), the spec says so, and the un-publishable case is named. Probe NE-A6-2 confirms the subset rule on both majors. Reaches: A6-15 Fields/Data, recon note 7, P0·5 author select, FR-H7 (offer only what resolves), FR-G3 `bindingContext`.
- **ghost-infeasible** — **§0 Data / every design whose primary ask is Portal · Sign up (1–13, 15)** — claim: the ask is always live; the only guard stated is "Members off in Ghost → A3·4's substitution". — evidence: `research-ghost-membership-pages.md` §7 — with `members_signup_access: 'invite'` Portal suppresses the signup form, with `'none'` Portal is not injected at all when donations and recommendations are also off, and `#/portal/signup` then "merely writes a hash"; §4's default resolution sends a logged-out visitor on an invite-only or price-less site to **signin**; `@site.allow_self_signup` and `@site.members_invite_only` are Ghost 5 fields, always defined (appendix-b1 §2, §6). — verdict: **buildable with a stated change** — the compiled free ask gates on `@site.allow_self_signup` exactly as FR-H6 gates a paid ask on `@site.paid_members_enabled`, and the editor warns at connect. Reaches: §0 Data, A6-6 Data, A6-14 Data ("Members off" is the only case handled), FR-H6 (the pre-deploy warn covers paid CTAs only), Appendix B, P0·4 defaults.
- **spec-incomplete** — **A6-6 / A6-14 — the members-form attributes** — the spec declares `member-form` but never names the markup contract: `data-members-form` (`signup` or `subscribe` — Appendix B lists both and they differ in what Ghost emails), `data-members-email`, `data-members-error`, whether `data-members-newsletter` is emitted, and which of the `newsletter*` copy fields become `data-i18n-*` versus `{{t}}` (registry §3 `member-form`: "Strings via `data-i18n-*`"; FR-Q6 scopes `{{t}}` to `.hbs` output). "Posts to Ghost's members subscribe endpoint" is the whole of it. Reaches: A6-6 Data/Behaviour, A6-14 Behaviour, carry-forward "Build contract" (which names the attributes for A22/A30 only), Appendix B, FR-Q6.
- **needs-execution** — **A6-6 — "an already-subscribed address gets Ghost's response in the same slot"** — no companion describes a distinct "already subscribed" server response; Ghost's magic-link endpoint is designed not to disclose whether an address exists. If the response is identical for a new and an existing address, the designed slot (and appendix-h1's `member.already_subscribed` key) has nothing to render. Probe NE-A6-3. Reaches: A6-6 Data, A3·4 (same sentence), appendix-h1 §3.4.
- **ghost-infeasible** — **A6-8 Image Split — "authored on a post or page, the picture defaults to that page's feature image"** — claim: available wherever the design is placed ("Every design is offered on every route", §0). — evidence: `feature_image` is a post-scope field legal only inside `{{#post}}` on `post`, `page` and entry `custom-*` templates (appendix-b1 §3, §4.2); on `index`/`home`/`tag`/`author` it renders empty with no error (§0 of that file). Bound images also carry no intrinsic dimensions from the Content API, so the design's "dimensions on the element" must come from the rendition size, not the source. — verdict: **buildable with a stated change** — that mode is offered only on post/page templates (FR-H7 prevention) and the spec says so. Reaches: A6-8 Data/Behaviour, §0 Data "every route", FR-H7, FR-D12/D13 (placement and shuffle filter on `bindingContext`), FR-G3.

Reaches: A6-7 a11y/Data, NFR-2, FR-H8, appendix-b1 §4.2.
- **spec-incomplete** — **A6-7 / A6-8 / A6-15 — the aborted `{{#get}}`** — a slow `{{#get}}` yields an empty collection plus a visible `<span data-aborted-get-helper>Could not load content</span>` inside the section (appendix-b1 §5, FR-H8 "every `{{#get}}`-driven section must degrade gracefully"); the specs' "no post matching → renders as authored" does not say what happens to that span. Reaches: A6-7 Data, A6-8 Data, A6-15 Data, FR-H8.
- **spec-incomplete** — **Member Visibility on 14 designs, and A6-14's three states** — consistent with Appendix C (server-side `{{#if @member}}`, no JS) and Appendix B/FR-D16 (`@member.paid` is `status !== 'free'`, so comped reads as paid — `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` line 215); what the spec never states is the compiled test for "Free members" (`@member` and not `@member.paid`) and "Logged out" (`{{#unless @member}}`), which §7.3's missing-construct 4 says "is not a plain path" — E4 needs the four tests written once. #### 4 · Architecture asks
- **Portal fragments do nothing with JavaScript off** (14, and every design's default ask) — owner: register **45(c)** — stands; the spec's per-design statement is the outstanding half (§2 above).

Two candidates: a compile-time per-template hook into `default.hbs`, or a sibling rule in A6-13's own stylesheet (`main:has(> .a6-13:last-child) + footer {…}` — `:has()` is Baseline Widely 2026-06-19 per registry §2.2, inside FR-G8's pinned date). Same family as the carry-forward route-awareness mechanism (A24/A26/A27/A28) — **no owner; needs one**.

AD-30 forbids a design stylesheet selecting on mode, so each must be a token whose dark value differs (a shadow-sm that resolves to none in dark, a field-ground token, an on-contrast muted token). The carry-forward pack-token family lists on-accent/on-contrast; A6 adds the field ground and the derived dark accents — owner: AD-30 + FR-E1's token set, **no owner named for A6's additions**.
