## A7 · Pricing and Tiers
**Counts (derived):** designs on disk 15 (frames 16 − `A7-0 Category Proof`) · spec 15 (`## 1`…`## 15`) · inventory 15 (`sections-inventory.md` line 177) · [Free] spec **0 marked** (the string `[Free]` does not occur in the spec) / inventory 2 (#1 Card Trio, #2 Minimal Table — by FR-G2's first-two rule the export's 1 Cards and 2 Table) · modules declared: `price-toggle` (1–14, at Billing period Both only) and `tabs` (10) — both registry names; 15 declares none · registry cross-check: §2.1 row 16 gives `price-toggle` reach "A7 billing toggle (15) + A7 #4 Toggle Cards intrinsic" — the export's reach is 14 and A7-4 is Split Head; row 12 lists `tabs` on four designs and none in A7 — A7-10 is a fifth consumer · custom-setting slots: 0 (the `@custom.a7_show_member_count` that `research-contested-variants.md` §2 proposed for #12 is moot — the export has no #12 Founding Member) · authored lists: `reasons[]` (14 Assurances) · Ghost-bound lists: the tier list on all 15 (`{{#get "tiers"}}`) and `@member.subscriptions` on 13 · frames carry no template code (no `{{price`, no `{{#get`, no `data-portal`; they draw `href="#/portal/signup/reader/monthly"` — a slug — and `@site.paid_members_enabled` ×30 as caption text), so every binding claim below is checked against the spec's prose.

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **ghost-infeasible** — **§0 No-JS baseline, and 10 Tabs — "all fifteen designs render complete and subscribable with JavaScript off"; "A7 therefore has no hard JavaScript dependency at all"** — claim: every action is "an `<a>` to a Portal fragment", so subscribing survives without script. — evidence: register 45(c) (`VERIFY-AT-BUILD.md` row 45): "Portal is Ghost's script, not the theme's, so `#/portal/…` fragments do nothing with JavaScript off — no registry module can fix this and the specs now say so instead of inventing a fallback"; `research-ghost-membership-pages.md` §4 (the fragment is parsed by Portal's own `hashchange` listener) and §7 ("`href="#/portal/signup"` merely writes a hash"). Every A7 action but 8's pricing-page link and 12's Actions None is a Portal fragment (`signup/{tier}/{cadence}`, `signup/free`, `account/plans`). — verdict: **not buildable as claimed**; the correct sentence is A6-14's — the section renders complete, the ask is inert without Ghost's script, nothing is designed for it — stated per design. Reaches: §0 No-JS baseline, the Behaviour module field on 1–15, 10 ("no hard JavaScript dependency"), 13 ("All member actions go to `#/portal/account/plans`"), 8's one-paid-tier Portal fallback, register 45(c), A6's same finding.
- **spec-incomplete** — **every price, 1–15 — `{{price}}` is never named** — carry-forward Build contract: "Prices render via `{{price}}` (tier prices are in the smallest currency unit — a raw print of $6 is '600')"; `research-ghost-membership-pages.md` §6: "Prices are integers in the smallest currency unit — format with `{{price monthly_price currency=currency}}`" (`docs.ghost.org/themes/helpers/data/price`); gscan's `GS001-DEPR-CURR-SYM` prescribes `{{price currency=currency}}` for the bare symbol (`verify-mechanical-ghost-claims.md` §13). The spec's typography needs the mark and the number as **separate elements** — "the currency mark is full size and in `text`, never raised and never muted", the cadence "words in the body font, 15 px muted", 9's "tracking is applied to the number and not to the cadence", 9's width rule ("€7 is 130 px at Display 88; €1,200 is 720 at Huge") — which the helper's one-string output does not give unless an amount-only form (`{{price monthly_price}}`) and a symbol-only form (`{{price currency=currency}}`) both exist and are combined. Zero-decimal currencies (JPY) and the helper's `locale` handling are unverified. — verdict: **needs execution** (NE-A7-1) and the spec must name the two helper forms it composes. Reaches: §0 price ladder, 1–15, 9 (width rule), 15 (two prices), Appendix B Tier row, carry-forward Build contract.
- **spec-incomplete** — **the currency-symbol rule for non-symbol currencies (carry-forward, A7)** — absent. 9 mentions "a currency written as a code" only as a width case. Needed: what the mark is when `Intl` yields a code (CHF, PLN, SEK, INR in some locales), whether `locale=@site.locale` is passed (symbol placement "7 €" vs "€7", decimal comma), what `currencyFormat` is set, and how the ladder treats a three-letter mark beside a 56 px number. Reaches: §0 ("never raised and never muted"), 9, 15, carry-forward Build contract; NE-A7-1.
- **needs-execution** — **§0 Data floor and every count-driven state — the tier count** — the spec branches on the number of paid tiers everywhere (zero → free-tier state; one → 6 Single Tier; exactly two on 11; three → 1 Cards on 6/9; four or more → 3 Stack / 2 Table; 8's "with one paid tier it becomes that tier's Portal link"). The inventory's authoring rule 1 (line 179, VERIFY 14b): emptiness is tested on a **filtered** get, never on `tiers.length` — proven for `filter="visibility:public"` alone; 14b also showed `filter="type:paid"` reporting length **1** with **0** rows on a hidden paid tier, because `type` filters at the query and `visibility` after the count. Under FR-H6's combined `type:paid+visibility:public` the count is therefore unproven and, by the stated mechanism, likely counts hidden paid tiers. Probe NE-A7-2. Also: (a) the query's `limit` is never stated — inventory rule 2 / FR-H2 / VERIFY 33: emit `limit="100"`, never `all`; (b) the free tier's "own `type:free` object" is not filtered on visibility, and the free tier **can** be hidden (`visibility: none` — the state 6 calls "no free tier — a site can disable it"), so it needs `type:free+visibility:public`. Reaches: §0 Data floor, 6, 8, 9, 11 Empty, inventory lines 178–180, FR-H2, FR-H6, VERIFY 14b/33.
- **ghost-infeasible** — **the free ask (`signup/free`) on 6, 9, 11, 15 and §0's Portal hand-off — never gated** — evidence: `research-ghost-membership-pages.md` §7 — with `members_signup_access: 'invite'` Portal suppresses the signup form; with `'paid'` `allow_self_signup` is false and a free signup is refused while the free tier object still returns; `@site.allow_self_signup` / `@site.members_invite_only` are Ghost 5 fields, always defined (appendix-b1 §2, §6). The spec gates paid asks on `@site.paid_members_enabled` and nothing on the free one. — verdict: **buildable with a stated change** — the free CTA gates on `@site.allow_self_signup`, and the editor warns at connect (FR-H6's warn covers only members-off). Reaches: §0 Portal hand-off and Data floor, 6 ("No free tier"), 9, 11, 15, FR-H6, Appendix B.
- **needs-execution** — **`signup/{tier}/{monthly|yearly}` — the tier segment** — the spec writes `{tier}`; the frames draw `signup/reader/monthly` (a slug); Appendix B and research §4 give `signup/{tierId}` and the reference theme emits `{{id}}`. Whether Portal resolves a slug is unverified (NE-A7-3); the spec must say `{{id}}` and whether the compiler emits `href` alone or `href` + `data-portal` (Appendix B: "Link Picker → `data-portal`"; both syntaxes feed one parser, research §4). §7.3's missing-construct 11 ("mixed literal-and-bound attribute value — `data-portal="signup/{tier}"`") lists A22, A30, A32 and not A7, which needs it on 1–14. Reaches: §0 Portal hand-off, 1–14 actions, Appendix B, §7.3 row 11.
- **ghost-infeasible** — **15 Both Prices — the server-rendered saving line; §0's "the saving is computed from Ghost's prices in whole months, rounded down"** — evidence: Ghost's Handlebars has no arithmetic helper (FR-H5's shim list and Appendix B name none; `{{match}}` compares, `{{plural}}` pluralises); with `price-toggle` the line is computed client-side from prices already in the DOM (registry §3 row `price-toggle`), and 4 correctly says the line "goes with the switch" when JS is off. 15 declares **no module** and draws the same computed line as content with a Saving line (Show · Hide) control. — verdict: **not buildable as specified** — either 15 declares `price-toggle` for its saving line (then 15 is not "the one design with no behaviour"), the compiler computes it from the connected site's tiers at compile (stale the day a price changes — AD-14, FR-H6 "live"), or the line is dropped. Also unstated on 1–3, 5–9, 11–14: the saving line vanishes with JS off (only 4 says so), and the module needs the raw prices on the markup (data attributes in subunits) to compute anything. Reaches: 15 Fields/Controls/Behaviour, §0 cadence switch, 1–14 JS-off paragraphs, registry §3 `price-toggle`.
- **ghost-infeasible** — **2 Table — "the rows are derived, and this is the category's one derivation"** — claim: each benefit string becomes a row when it first appears, more expensive tiers are ticked cumulatively, "Everything in Free" is parsed as inheritance, and "the whole matrix… all three being CSS". — evidence: nested `{{#foreach}}` with `{{#match}}` can test string equality between two tiers, but Handlebars has no variables or set operations, so a row that already appeared in an earlier tier cannot be suppressed, and a benefit string cannot be parsed for a tier name. — verdict: **not buildable server-side**; options: a registry addition (client-side matrix build; no-JS = the per-tier "degenerate" list the Reconciled paragraph already names) marked **ARCHITECT: registry addition** (P0·8 rule 4), compile-time derivation from the connected site's tiers (stale), or one row per (tier, benefit) with no dedup — which is the spec's own "degenerate case" hand-off to 1 Cards. Reaches: 2 "The rows are derived", Behaviour module, Reconciled, Flagged ("both rules are invented"), FR-G7, P0·8.
- **ghost-infeasible** — **2 Table at ≤ 767 — "hands off to 1 Cards' single column, every included row drawn in its tier's card"** — a `<table>` is row-major DOM; CSS cannot gather one column's cells into a per-tier card for an unknown row count (grid placement needs enumerated `nth-child` rules). Not a Ghost limit — a CSS one. — verdict: **buildable with a stated change** — keep the 1080 sideways scroll at ≤ 767, or emit a second per-tier list hidden above 767 (duplicate markup, a11y cost, stated). Reaches: 2 Responsive/a11y.
- **ghost-infeasible** — **11 Free and Paid at ≤ 767 — "the paid tier comes first, and the DOM order changes with it"** — server markup has one order; CSS `order` moves the visual only. — verdict: **buildable with a stated change** — DOM paid-first at every width (then DOM ≠ visual above 767) or accept the phone mismatch; the a11y field must say which. Reaches: 11 Responsive/a11y, §0 "the order is Ghost's own… at every width".
- **ghost-infeasible** — **13 Members — three data claims** — (a) "the join date for a free [member]": `@member` is `uuid, email, name, firstname, avatar_image, subscriptions, paid, status` (FR-D16, appendix-b1 §6) — no `created_at`; not bindable, and `{{date}}` on an absent field renders **today** (`research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` line 721). (b) "A cancelled or expired subscription reads as a visitor": `@member` is non-null for any signed-in member (appendix-b1 §2); a lapsed member is `status: 'free'` and reads as the free-member state, not a visitor; an active subscription with `cancel_at_period_end` still reads paid and its "renewal date" will not renew (the carry-forward verify for A30 — `cancel_at_period_end` in templates — reaches 13). (c) "`status: comped` reads as Paid" is right for the gate (`@member.paid` is `status !== 'free'`, line 215), but "which tier" comes from `@member.subscriptions`, and a comped member has no Stripe subscription — whether a tier is exposed for them is unverified (NE-A7-4). — verdict: (a) not buildable; (b) buildable with a stated change; (c) needs execution. Reaches: 13 Data, Reconciled, Empty, FR-D16, Appendix B `@member`, carry-forward "Verifies before build".
- **needs-execution** — **§0 cadence switch — "unavailable where any tier has no yearly price"** — if Ghost Admin requires both prices on a paid tier the clause is dead; if not, the editor-time disable does not survive a later price edit and the deployed theme needs a runtime rule the spec lacks (15 has one — "per-card, not per-section"). NE-A7-5. Reaches: §0 cadence switch, 1–14, 15 per-card rule.
- **needs-execution** — **trials (carry-forward: "tier `trial_days` reachability and whether sections should mention trials")** — §0: "Nothing about a discount, offer, **trial**… appears anywhere in A7: Ghost's Offers own them." A trial is a **tier** property, not an Offer: `trial_days` is in the tiers serializer (`research-ghost-membership-pages.md` §6, `serializeTier()`), so it is reachable by code reading; Portal's checkout then labels the button with the trial. The product half (mention trials or not) is the owner's; the reachability half is NE-A7-6 (confirm the value is populated through the Content API on both majors). Appendix B's Tier row lacks `trial_days`, `id` and `slug`. Reaches: §0 Portal hand-off, 14 ("no guarantee, trial or refund copy"), Appendix B, carry-forward.
- **spec-incomplete** — **`{{#get "tiers"}}` aborted** — a slow get yields an empty collection plus `<span data-aborted-get-helper>Could not load content</span>` inside the section (appendix-b1 §5, FR-H8); §0's Empty covers zero tiers, not the abort. Reaches: §0 Empty/Data floor, FR-H8.
- **consistent** — the gate and the filter as written (`@site.paid_members_enabled` on every paid CTA and the switch; `type:paid+visibility:public`; the seeded $5 tier never implies purchasability; members off → no section via `@site.members_enabled`) match FR-H6, `research-ghost-membership-pages.md` §6/§7 and Appendix B. The pre-Stripe state (gate closed → 6's free-tier arrangement) is the right reading.
- **consistent** — `recommendedTier` compiles to a literal tier id tested with `{{#match id "=" "<id>"}}` inside the loop (FR-H5 shim carries `{{#match}}`); "the theme never picks a tier by position" holds. 7's "without one the section draws as 1 Cards" after the tier is deleted in Ghost is expressible as `ul:not(:has(.is-recommended))` — `:has()` is Baseline Widely (registry §2.2) — worth stating.
- **consistent** — Description (Show · Hide), Member Visibility and 7's Small tiers each write one value on the section root (AD-3, symmetric by construction); tier facts plain-text-locked ("Edit tiers in Ghost") match FR-Q3/AD-4 — Ghost's tier name, description and benefit strings are plain strings (research §6).

#### 4 · Architecture asks
- **Portal fragments do nothing without JavaScript** on 1–15 — owner: register **45(c)** — stands; the per-design statement is A7's outstanding half.
- **Count-driven hand-offs to a different design** ("four or more → 3 Stack", "one → 6 Single Tier", "three → 1 Cards", 11's "a second paid tier → 1 Cards", 8's one-tier Portal fallback) — a hand-off names a different partial, and the tier count is live data unknown at compile (FR-H6, AD-14). At runtime only CSS inside the placed design's own markup can react (`li:only-child`, `:nth-last-child(n+4)`, `:has()`); at edit time the editor knows the count from the Content API and can name the other design. The spec never says which it means. Owner: FR-D19/AD-2 — **no owner; needs one**.
- **Arithmetic the theme cannot do** — the saving line on 15 (and the switch's line, which must live in the module) and 2 Table's matrix derivation: registry additions or compile-time rules, each marked "ARCHITECT: registry addition" per P0·8 rule 4, or dropped. Owner: FR-G7 — **no owner; needs one**.
- **`price-toggle`'s contract** — buttons + `aria-pressed` (spec) vs radios in a fieldset + `data-billing` on the root (registry §3): one markup, one no-JS rule, and the prices the module reads (data attributes in subunits on the markup). Owner: FR-G7 / registry §3 — the architect.
- **Pack-token asks (AD-30)** — 2's dark alternate tint `#1D1A15` "a step down… and the recommended column's hairline goes with it" (a mode-dependent hairline), 5's derived 22 / 7 / 14 % panel mixes and 45 % outline ("derived rather than tokens — the one place this design invents colour"), 5's re-tuned dark muted `#57524A`, §0's recommendation plane step "in dark always to the hover surface", the tokenisation proof's derived dark accents. AD-30 forbids a design stylesheet selecting on mode; each needs a token with a dark value or `color-mix()` over tokens (FR-G3: stylesheets consume pack custom properties only — check `color-mix()` against FR-G8's pinned date). Carry-forward pack-token family (on-contrast, the dark hover-surface step) — A7 adds the derived mixes and the mode-dependent hairline — **no owner named for A7's additions**.
- **`@member` tier awareness** (13) — join date (absent), comped tier (unverified), cancel-at-period-end (carry-forward for A30) — owner: Appendix B / FR-D16 — the architect, after NE-A7-4.
- **Tier-level View as** (13) — owner: FR-D16 — **prd-gap already recorded (reconcile-mockups S4), unowned**.
- **Cross-category shared field** (`reasons[]` "verbatim" from A6·11) — FR-G3 — same ask as A6's `newsletter*`.
- **Custom settings** — none promoted; 0 of 17 slots.

#### 5 · Spec completeness
- **Ten fields:** every design carries Descriptor, Structural descriptor, Archetype, Responsive, Fields, Controls, Empty, Behaviour module and a11y; an explicit **Data** field exists on 13 only — the other fourteen rely on §0's Data floor and the frames' "DATA · from Ghost" group (recon notes: "with the per-design sentences on 2, 6, 8, 12, 13 and 15" — drawn, not written into the spec sections). 11 and 15's Fields double as Data.
- **Tuples:** all fifteen are six slots; first five in the closed vocabularies (archetypes: grid-of-N ×5, split ×4, stack ×2, table ×2, bar, nav; containment none ×15; ground page ×14, contrast; count few ×10, variable ×4, one; media none ×15). **First-five collisions:** {1 Cards, 13 Members, 14 Assurances, 15 Both Prices} on `grid-of-N · none · page · few · none`; {7 Highlight, 11 Free and Paid} on `split · none · page · few · none` — both stated by the spec ("The close pairs"). Register 46's bound applies to the first family (four designs separated by device alone). No off-vocabulary word; unique (`tuple-check-specs.txt`: A7 disk 15 · tuples 15; OK). 10's `selected panel only` describes the JS-on view, as recon note 17 says.
- **Modules:** 1–14 quote the registry's `price-toggle` sentence and 10 the `tabs` sentence verbatim; no coined name survives (the `M-cadence`/`M-tabs` correction is recorded). Every "none"/"nothing to degrade" claim is wrong about the Portal ask (§1).
- **Lists:** the tier list shows no Add button (correct) but not the P0·3 Ghost-list card and refuses its minimum controls (§2); `reasons[]` on 14 carries Add-with-content, Remove, drag per P0·3 with the floor conflict; 13's `@member.subscriptions` is read, never listed.
- **Strings:** no `tier.*` keys exist; one hardcoded `aria-label` (10); channel unstated (§3).
- **[Free]:** absent (§3).
- **Internal counts:** §0 says "The site authors: `eyebrow`, `title`, `sub`, `note`, `recommendedTier`, `badgeLabel`, `payLabel`, `freeLabel`" (eight) and 1's Fields says "the authored eight"; Category artefacts says "nine authored fields and six read from each Ghost tier". After this pass the authored set is those eight + 6's and 9's `freeLine`, 15's `freeSecondLine`, 13's `yourPlanLabel` / `upgradeLabel` / `changeLabel` / `memberTitle` / `memberSub`, 14's `reasons[]`, 8's unnamed section action label. The "six read per tier" are name, description, monthly price, yearly price, currency, benefits — `id` (needed for the Portal link) and `type` are read too.

#### Needs execution (this category)
- **NE-A7-1** — `{{price}}` forms and currencies — probe: on T1 (6.58.0) and T3 (5.130.6), tiers priced in EUR, USD, JPY (700 / 70000 subunits), CHF, INR, PLN; a fixture rendering `{{price monthly_price currency=currency}}`, `{{price monthly_price}}`, `{{price currency=currency}}`, each with and without `locale=@site.locale` (`en`, `de`, `fr`, `ja`); record symbol vs code, placement, decimals, the JPY divisor; expected: amount-only and symbol-only forms exist, non-symbol currencies render a code, JPY may be divided by 100 — the spec then writes its composition and its non-symbol rule.
- **NE-A7-2** — the count under the combined filter — probe: one public paid tier, one paid tier at `visibility: none`, public Free; `{{#get "tiers" filter="type:paid+visibility:public" limit="100"}}` → `{{tiers.length}}` and the `{{#foreach}}` row count; also `filter="type:free+visibility:public"` with the free tier hidden via Portal settings; expected (from 14b's mechanism): length 2, rows 1 — then every count-driven state in A7 must derive from the rows (`@last`/`@number`) or CSS, never `length`.
- **NE-A7-3** — Portal fragment tier segment — probe: `<a href="#/portal/signup/<slug>/monthly">` and `…/<id>/monthly` on T1 with Stripe test mode; expected: the id opens checkout, the slug falls to Portal's default screen.

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **consistent** — **all 15** — claim: "Nothing comes from Ghost" (§0); tagged-posts source refused — evidence: FR-G3 (`bindingContext: none`, `compileTarget: any`); D5's hand-picked list does not name A9 — verdict: buildable; no binding to check in appendix-b1; FR-H4/H8 do not apply (zero items = authored-empty → compiles to nothing; every "no X → hands off" case is a content branch, not a bound-prop guard). Reaches: spec §0, inventory 216, FR-G3.
- **arch-gap** — **Member Visibility on 14 designs (all but 13)** — same as A8: Appendix C's row and §7.3 item 4 list A2, A6, A22, A26 (+A30, A32); A9 is on neither. Verdict: buildable with a stated change. Reaches: Appendix C, inventory preamble, §7.3 item 4, spec §0 "Member visibility", 14 Controls lines.
- **spec-incomplete** — **the section link (14 designs) and 14 Ask's button** — "the section link can be a Portal target" (§0) — register 45(c): Portal fragments do nothing with JS off and a spec must say so; not said. Reaches: spec §0, §14, register 45(c), FR-H6.
- **arch-gap / needs-execution** — **`<details name>` on the ten accordions (Open rows: One at a time)** — claim: "native `<details name>` grouping — one open row per group, no JavaScript" (§0 Settlement 1, D19) — evidence: FR-G8 pins Baseline **Widely** at `widelyAvailableOnDate: 2026-08-18`, i.e. `baseline_low_date ≤ 2024-02-18` (research §A3's script); the `name` attribute on `<details>` shipped Chrome 120 / Safari 17.2 (Dec 2023) but **Firefox 130 (Sep 2024)**, so its Baseline-low date is after the cut and it is **Newly**, not Widely, on the pin; FR-G8's Tier-2 allowlist does not list it and Tier 2 forbids anything that "may carry … interaction"; the research never mentions the attribute (grep: no `name=`, no `exclusive`) — verdict: **D19 (ruled) and FR-G8 (PRD) contradict on the pinned floor** — Firefox 122–129 visitors get Many at the One-at-a-time value with no error. The registry's own `accordion` row already budgets "~0.2 KB, and *only* for single-open groups and A9's `default state` control" (research §3.1), i.e. the registry assumed JS for exclusivity before D19 was ruled. Not re-litigating D19: the reconciliation available is emit `name` **and** let `accordion`'s 0.2 KB enforce exclusivity where `name` is unsupported, with the spec's "no JavaScript at all" softened to "no JavaScript on browsers that support `name`"; the no-JS state on a pre-130 Firefox is Many. Owner must rule. Reaches: D19, FR-G8 (Tier 2 list), research §3.1 `accordion`, §6.3/§6.5, spec §0 Settlement 1, §1/2/5/6/7/8/10/12/13/14 Behaviour + Controls, §16.1, §18.1, §18.18 ("Open rows needed no addition — `<details name>` is markup").
- **needs-execution** — **"a browser's find matches text inside a closed `<details>` and opens the row it found"** (§0 ×3, rewritten into ten panels as user-facing advice) — evidence: this is Chromium's auto-expand behaviour (Chrome 97+); it is not in the research, not a Ghost fact, and Firefox 122 / Safari 17.2 — the pinned floor — are not known to do it — verdict: needs execution (browser, not T1/T3); until then the ten panels state a browser-specific behaviour as universal. Reaches: spec §0 "The accordion's cost", §0 "Three structures", §1 Flagged, §18.4, all ten accordion panel frames.
- **needs-execution** — **"Print: every row prints open, in every design, and the marker is not printed"** (§0) with no module — evidence: a closed `<details>`' content is not rendered and print CSS cannot reveal it; opening rows for print needs a `beforeprint` handler (script) — so the claim is either a JS behaviour the `accordion` module must own (and a no-JS print shows closed rows) or false — verdict: needs execution (browser) and a spec correction either way. Reaches: spec §0 "Print", §2/§4/§6/§7/§8/§11/§14 print lines, research §3.1/§7 `accordion` (no print behaviour stated).
- **arch-gap** — **Settlement 3's answer: "limited rich text … paragraphs, one level of unordered or ordered list, inline links, inline code, bold and italic"; 13 Slim hands off "with a list or inline code in it"** — evidence: FR-D4 "exactly four inline marks — bold, italic, underline, link … stored as text plus marks … over exactly those four marks — never as an HTML string"; AD-4 "`{ text, marks[] }` over exactly `strong | em | u | a`"; `marks.ts` is the single serializer — verdict: **not buildable as specified on the current spine**: block structure (paragraphs are arguable via "line breaks honored"; lists are not) and a `code` mark are outside AD-4's model, and 13 Slim's hand-off needs the compiler to inspect that structure. The spec records only the mark set as "a PRD delta" (§0, §18.19); the block model is the larger delta and is unrecorded. - **NE-A9-1** — `<details name>` is Baseline Widely on 2026-08-18 — probe: research §A3's script against `web-features@3.35.0`, print `status.baseline_low_date` for the `<details>` `name` (exclusive accordion) feature; expected: a date after `2024-02-18` (Firefox 130 shipped 2024-09-03), i.e. **Newly** → D19 needs the `accordion` module's 0.2 KB fallback or a Tier-2 exception the FR-G8 text currently forbids.
- **NE-A9-2** — find-in-page opens a closed `<details>` — probe: a `<details>` with the search term only in its closed content; Ctrl-F in Firefox 122 and Safari 17.2; expected: no match/open outside Chromium → ten panels' disclosure rewritten to "in some browsers".
- **NE-A9-3** — "every row prints open" without script — probe: print preview of a closed `<details>` with `@media print { details > * { display: block } }` in all three; expected: content not rendered → the mechanism is a `beforeprint` handler in `accordion` (JS-marked) and the no-JS print state is "closed rows".
- **NE-A9-4** — `<h3>` inside `<summary>` exposes both the button and the heading — probe: VoiceOver (Safari 17.2) and NVDA (Firefox 122) on `<details><summary><h3>Q</h3></summary>`; expected: "heading level 3, button" — if the heading role is dropped, the "heading rotor" win the spec claims is lost on that AT.

## A10 · Stats and Numbers
**Counts (derived):** designs on disk 15 (16 `A10-*` frames − `A10-0 Category Proof`) · spec 15 (`## 1 · Row` … `## 15 · Big Type`, §17 table has 15 rows) · inventory 15 (line 234–250 — a **different roster**, see C1) · [Free] spec **0 markers anywhere in the file** / inventory 2 (#1, #2 → by FR-G2's first-two rule these are export 1 Row and 2 Cards) · modules declared: `count-up` on all 15 (Off by default, §0/§19); `core` assumed once; `reveal`, `typewriter`, `countdown`, `lightbox`, `video-facade`, `filter-strip`, `dismiss`, `header-scroll`, `mode-toggle` named only as refusals — all 31-registry names, none invented · custom-setting slots: 0 (Appendix B line 903: the two count helpers are keyless and spend no slot; nothing is promoted) · authored lists: `stats[]` 1–8 (P0·3 named on all 15 panels; Add/Remove/Reorder stated in the §0 floor and per design) · Ghost-bound lists: none · item-level Ghost binding: `Value source: Authored · Member count · Paid member count` on every stat (the library's first, §18 finding 8).

Spec sources: `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/design/claude-design-export/Inflozo/A10 Stats and Numbers - Spec.md` (790 lines, read in full); `A10-0 Category Proof.dc.html` carries `{{total_members}}` (grep-verified); the A10 controls prompt is the text extract of `CONTROL-PROMPTS.html` lines 678–739 (category-wide items 1–5, per-design 1–3).

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **consistent** — **Value source (all 15)** — claim: `{{total_members}}` / `{{total_paid_members}}` are public theme helpers rendering a pre-rounded string — evidence: `research-contested-variants.md` §2.1 (helper source quoted; registered in `register-ghost-helpers.js:53-54`; gscan `knownHelpers` lists both), Appendix B line 903, FR-H5 line 324 (shim contract), §7.3 missing-construct row 9 ("bare-helper binding … `{{total_members}}`") — verdict: buildable. The premise reversal the spec records (§19 item 4) is correct. **But the spec cites none of these** — §0 asserts "public theme helpers" and "each renders a pre-rounded string" with no citation, so nothing in the spec would catch it if the helper's shape changed (verification-gap; see F2).
- **needs-execution** — **F1 · Value source at zero members / members disabled** — claim (§0): the bound value "renders Ghost's helper string verbatim — '1,200+'". Evidence: the helper source in `research-contested-variants.md` §2.1 is `total > 0 ? memberCountRounding(total) : 0` — a site with zero members renders the **number `0`**, not a string, and §2.2 says so ("sites with 0 members render `0`"); ≤ 50 members renders the exact count with no `+` (`memberCountRounding`). The spec has no zero case, no "exact below 51" case and says nothing about a site with members disabled. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — the spec must state the three outputs (exact · rounded+`+` · `0`) and what a stat draws at `0` (a 128 px "0" on 4 Single is the likely first-run state of every new site). Probe under NE-A10-1. Reaches: spec §0 "Two figures come from Ghost", 4 Single §Reconciled, 13 Slim §Reconciled, FR-H5, Appendix B.
- **spec-incomplete** — **F2 · The compiled guard for a helper-bound value (FR-H8)** — claim: the helper's output "replaces `value` verbatim". FR-H8 (line 331) says every bound prop compiles inside a guard and text falls back to the static value; §7.3 row 9 records that a bare helper has no bound path, and `research-contested-variants.md` §2.2 says there is no `{{#if}}`-able form of the count and the gate is `{{#if @site.members_enabled}}` (paid: `@site.paid_members_enabled`, FR-H6). The spec never names the guard, never names the fallback (the authored `value`, per FR-H8's text rule), and its "Paid member count is offered only where the site has paid members enabled" is an **editor-time** offer with no compiled counterpart. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — compile as `{{#if @site.members_enabled}}{{total_members}}{{else}}{authored value}{{/if}}` (paid → `@site.paid_members_enabled` + `{{total_paid_members}}`), and state the unlinked-project default (FR-H5: a sample value). Reaches: spec §0, every design's Items line, FR-H8, §7.3 row 9, appendix-b1 (F3).
- **needs-execution** — **F3 · Where the helpers are legal (FR-H7)** — `appendix-b1-template-contexts.md` §2 ("available in every template, unconditionally") lists `@site.*`, `@member`, `@custom.*`, `@config.posts_per_page`, `{{meta_title}}`, `{{navigation}}`, `{{body_class}}`, `{{ghost_head}}`, `{{ghost_foot}}`, `{{asset}}`, `{{#is}}`, `{{t}}` — **no core helper**, and §6's version gates do not mention them. FR-H7 says the editor offers only what the matrix permits, so as written the editor cannot offer Value source on any template. A10 is `compileTarget: any` (inventory preamble), which includes `error.hbs` — the helper is `async` and runs the internal stats query per render, and appendix-b1 §3c/§8 row 2 records that what `error.hbs` may run is unverified (Inflozo's own rule bans `{{#get}}` there). Also the helper reads `this.total` first (source, §2.1) — inside a block whose context carries `total` it would print that instead. Verdict: needs execution (NE-A10-2) and an appendix-b1 amendment. Reaches: appendix-b1 §2/§3c/§6, FR-H7, spec §0, inventory preamble (`compileTarget: any`).
- **prd-defect** — **F4 · FR-H5's "real rounded string on a linked project"** — FR-H5 (line 324) promises the count helpers "render a sample value on an unlinked project and the real rounded string on a linked one". Appendix B's data surface is the Content API (Posts, Pages, Tags, Authors, Tiers, Settings) plus template context — it has no member count; the helper is server-side inside Ghost's render. AD-10 forbids a client-side Admin call and routes every Admin read through `apps/web/server/ghost-admin/*` with an audit row. Nothing in the PRD names the source the canvas would use. Verdict: prd-defect — either FR-H5 names the mechanism (a server-side Admin read of Ghost's member stats through AD-10's module, with its P5 cost stated) or downgrades to "sample value on every project". A10 rests on the promise: 4 Single "is the design the member-count binding was written for" and its canvas would show a fixed sample on every linked site. Probe NE-A10-4. Reaches: FR-H5, Appendix B, AD-10, spec §0 and 4 Single/5 Lead Stat/13 Slim §Reconciled.
- **ghost-infeasible** — **F5 · 14 Change with a bound value and a `prev`** — claim (14 Change §Reconciled): "a bound value still able to carry a `prev` (Ghost gives this year's figure, the site types last year's)" with the direction word chosen by the parse. The parse happens "before the page is served" (§Behaviour) — i.e. in Inflozo's compiler — but a helper's value exists only at Ghost render time, is a `SafeString` like "1,200+" (research §2.2: "never attempt arithmetic on it"), and Handlebars/Ghost have no helper that parses and compares it. Verdict: not buildable as stated; buildable with the spec's own fallback — a bound value with a `prev` always draws the "was …" form with no glyph and no direction word (the design's rule for a figure that fails to parse), stated in the item panel. Reaches: 14 Change §Items/§Arrangement/§Reconciled, appendix-h1 (`stats.was` is the only key the bound case can use), §7.3 row 9.
- **arch-gap** — **F6 · 9 Bars' fill is an inline `width` from an authored number** — claim (9 Bars §Behaviour/§Arrangement): "the fill's width is an inline percentage on a `<span>`, server-rendered from `share`". AD-3's rule: the only inline `style` a theme may carry is a single `--custom-property` assignment **from bound Ghost data** (Round 3 decision B), and the FR-J17 gate fails any other inline style; §7.3 row 12 records that the custom-property case "collides with AD-3 and must be ruled on". `share` is authored, not Ghost data, so even `style="--share:62"` is outside the carve-out as written. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — emit `style="--share: 62"` (integer validated 0–100 per AD-36 item 4) and read `width: calc(var(--share) * 1%)` in the stylesheet, **and** AD-3's carve-out is widened to validated authored numerics. Reaches: AD-3, §7.3 row 12, FR-J17, AD-36 item 4, 9 Bars §Behaviour/§Arrangement/§Fields.
- **arch-gap** — **F7 · 11 Inline's chip has no representation in AD-4** — claim: the lede is rich text carrying "one chip per stat … a figure cannot be typed into the sentence by hand". AD-4: a text prop is `{ text, marks[] }` over **exactly** `strong | em | u | a`, serialized in one place; §7.3 row 13 names this design ("A10 #7 — stats embedded within a flowing sentence") only for text-node interpolation of **bound** text. An authored inline reference to `stats[i]` is neither a mark nor a bound path. Verdict: not buildable until AD-4 gains an inline-reference mark (or the design is re-specified as three text fields around two chips). Same construct in A11-14 Inline. Reaches: AD-4, §7.3 row 13, 11 Inline §Behaviour/§Fields/§Items, P0·1 (the "Insert figure" button lives in its frame).
- **spec-incomplete** — **F8 · `count-up`'s parse contract contradicts §0's "no separator guessing"** — §0: "The value is a text field, not a number field — no formatter, no locale, no separator guessing", and §19 item 5 makes that rule "load-bearing" for the helper. A count-up module must turn the value text into a number to animate it: "41,800", "99.98", "3.4" (units are separate spans), "Sold out", and the helper's "1,200+" or "0". The spec never says which strings animate, what the module does with a European "1.200", whether the `+` is kept, or that "Sold out" renders static. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — the module animates only a value matching ASCII digits with optional `,` groups and one `.` decimal, keeps every non-digit glyph in place, and leaves anything else static; the rule belongs in the registry's module contract, restated here. Reaches: §0, 11 Inline §Reconciled ("the run reserves the final value's width" needs the same parse), 9 Bars/14 Change §Reconciled, `research-section-js-libraries.md` §2.1 row 18 (module contract).
- **consistent** — **9 Bars / 14 Change: the module on half a design** — the design's own static markup marks the animated node (a `data-countup` hook on the value `<span>` and not on the fill or the `prev`) — that is the design's HTML, not a per-item control, so AD-3 holds and no registry vocabulary is needed for "module on, one element excluded" (§18 finding 9 asks; this answers it). Useful because the spec thought it needed a ruling.
- **consistent** — **`count-up` degradation and reduced motion** — the §7 sentence ("The final value renders as static text — it is already in the HTML before JS ever runs.") is quoted verbatim in §0, §18, §19; reduced motion resolves through `core`'s `matchMedia` gate (FR-G4/FR-G7(4)); FR-D20's list makes `lightbox` the only non-edit-safe module. Consistent — but see C2 on the word "edit-safe".
- **arch-gap** — **F9 · 7 Contrast Band's per-mode percentages and the `contrast` / on-contrast tokens** — claim: "muted = the carried colour at 72% in light and 70% in dark; hairline = 18%", "resolved in the stylesheet". FR-E4 (line 259): "no section stylesheet ever selects on `prefers-color-scheme`, on a scheme class or on `data-mode`"; AD-30: the token block and the base stylesheet are the only files that mention a mode. A design stylesheet cannot carry "72% in light and 70% in dark". FR-E1's token list (line 251) is background, surface, text, muted text, border, accent, on-accent — **no `contrast`, no on-contrast** — while Appendix C's Swatch Row and `claude-design-prompt-2.md` line 231 do name `contrast`; the carry-forward already asks for "on-accent/on-contrast as real tokens". Verdict: buildable with a stated change — the three derived values become mode-resolved tokens in the token block (`--on-contrast-muted`, `--on-contrast-hairline`), and A10-7 must cite the carry-forward rather than assume the pair. Reaches: 7 Contrast Band §Derived colours/§Reconciled, AD-30, FR-E4, FR-E1, Appendix C, the pack-token carry-forward.
- **arch-gap** — **F10 · Tabular figures are a font feature the packs never declare** — §0's stat component ("tabular figures"), 8 Ledger (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so "the digits line up") and 14 Change ("13 px … tabular") all depend on the pack's **heading** face shipping a `tnum` table; display faces routinely do not, and FR-E1/Appendix D declare families, weights and variable/static — not OpenType features. The carry-forward lists "tabular figures" as a pack-token ask from A17/A18/A19/A26/A34; A10 makes the same ask on three designs and cites nothing. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — the pairing table gains a per-family `tnum` flag and 8 Ledger's alignment claim is scoped to pairings that carry it. Probe NE-A10-5. Reaches: §0 stat component, 8 Ledger §Behaviour/§Arrangement, 14 Change §Arrangement, FR-E1, Appendix D, the pack-token carry-forward.
- **arch-gap** — **F11 · P0·2's per-icon colour role is per-item styling** — "Icons: None · Shown" is a section toggle (AD-3-clean), but the spec then gives each stat "the picker's size and colour-role popover" (§0, 1 Row §Reconciled, 7 Contrast Band §Reconciled "the P0·2 popover's colour roles resolve to the carried colour"). Register 44 states the rule A10 itself repeats — "no control in the sidebar addresses one item" — and AD-3 writes every control value on the section root. A per-stat colour role is a second attribute per item. A10 already fixes the icon **size** per design (20 / 24 / 28 / 32), so only the role remains. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — either the colour role is one section value on the Icons control, or AD-3 gains a carve-out for a closed-set per-item class that is item *content* (the glyph already is). Reaches: P0·2 (the popover), AD-3, register 44, §0 "Four other things", every design's Icons line.

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **stale-design** — **F1 · `<picture>` with a `prefers-color-scheme` source is the wrong mode signal** — claim (§0 Structure, 7 Contrast Band §Behaviour): "`<picture>` with a `prefers-color-scheme` source is used, and only when `logoDark` exists … the inversion survives with JavaScript off for the same reason `mode-toggle` degrades to Auto". Evidence: FR-E4 (line 255–259) has **three** mode signals — the media query (Auto only), the owner's pin server-rendered as `scheme-light` / `scheme-dark` on `<body>` (FR-Q5's `color_scheme`), and the visitor's `[data-mode]` from `mode-toggle` — and "both resolve into the same token block; sections consume tokens exclusively". A `<source media>` obeys only the first: a site pinned Dark in Ghost Admin, or a visitor who toggled dark, gets the **light** file on a dark ground — the exact defect the second upload exists to prevent. AD-30: "a per-mode image swap is the one case needing markup, and it emits **both sources with one generic rule authored once, in the base stylesheet**". Verdict: buildable with a stated change — emit both `<img>`s (light and dark) and let the base stylesheet's generic rule select on the resolved mode; no `<picture>`. Reaches: §0 Structure, §0 "A dark ground is where a logo wall breaks", 7 Contrast Band §Behaviour/§a11y/§Flagged, AD-30, FR-E4, FR-Q5.
- **arch-gap** — **F2 · 7 Contrast Band selects by ground, not by mode** — the band "always wants the opposite file from the mode it is in" (dark file in light mode, light file in dark). AD-30's one generic swap rule is keyed on mode; the band needs it keyed on **ground**. AD-3 lets the design write `data-ground="dark"` on its root, but the *base* stylesheet must read it (the design's own stylesheet may not mention mode). Verdict: buildable with a stated change — the base rule becomes "dark file when (mode is dark) XOR (section is `data-ground=dark`)", authored once. Reaches: 7 Contrast Band, AD-30, AD-3, §16 amendment 1.
- **arch-gap** — **F3 · Two per-mode constants live in design stylesheets** — (a) the plate: "the pack's **light-mode** `surface` — `#FFFFFF` in Paper — … the dark-mode `surface` token cannot be used" (§0). Under AD-30/FR-E4 a design stylesheet consumes `--surface`, which resolves to the *dark* value in dark; the light value is unreachable without a mode-invariant token. (b) Treatment Muted: "`grayscale(1)` at 64% in light and 74% in dark" — a mode-dependent number in a design stylesheet (7's "70% in both modes" is a design constant and is fine). Verdict: buildable with a stated change — two tokens in the token block, `--plate` (mode-invariant, = light surface) and `--logo-muted-opacity` (per mode). Reaches: §0 dark ground, §0 Treatment, 5 Cards ("the card becomes the plate"), 12/13/14/15's plate variants, AD-30, FR-E1, the pack-token carry-forward.
- **arch-gap** — **F4 · "The pack's hover surface" does not exist** — §0 Links: "the cell takes the pack's hover surface at the pack radius"; 7 derives one "because the pack supplies a hover surface for a ground and a surface but not for a band". FR-E1's token list (line 251) is background, surface, text, muted text, border, accent, on-accent; prompt-2 line 231 lists seven roles (…contrast) — no hover surface anywhere. The carry-forward names "the dark hover-surface step" as a pack-token ask from A17/A18/A19/A26/A34; A11 makes the same ask on all 15 designs and cites nothing. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — a `--hover-surface` token per mode (7's 10 % mix via `color-mix()`). Reaches: §0 Links, 1 Row §Reconciled (the three hovers), 5/11/13 §Reconciled, FR-E1, the carry-forward.
- **arch-gap** — **F5 · Aspect classes "computed by the theme"** — §0: "Aspect classes, computed by the theme from the file's intrinsic ratio". A Ghost theme computes nothing at render (Handlebars, no JS declared on thirteen designs); the class must be emitted by the **compiler** from the asset's stored intrinsic dimensions. AD-12 stores rendition paths on `assets.renditions`; I found no rule in the spine storing intrinsic width/height (grep: none). FR-K2 allows SVG (sanitised) — the spec says "SVG preferred" — and an SVG with only a `viewBox` reports no natural size to the sanitiser's consumer unless the editor reads the `viewBox`. The spec also has no rule for an unknown ratio. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — the editor records intrinsic w/h at upload (raster from the decode, SVG from `width`/`height` or `viewBox`), the compiler emits the class, and an unknown ratio falls to `Regular`. The "editor warns below 2×" advice needs the same metadata. Reaches: §0 Aspect classes, §16 §8.2, 13 Dense, AD-12, FR-K2, FR-K1 (its Image/SVG/Logo filter).
- **ghost-infeasible** — **F6 · 9 Rail's precondition is decided at render** — claim (9 Rail §Fields/§Items): "The precondition is measured at render, not counted: if the list is not wider than the viewport the section draws as 1 Row, so the same list can be a rail at 834 and 1 Row at 1440 … Adding … can bring this design into existence". Evidence: AD-3 — a design switch replaces the attribute set (compile-time, by the user); FR-G4 — the server-rendered state is the real one; the spec's own head finding 2 — "no module measures", and with JS off "the section stays a rail". A module that measured and rebuilt a cell grid would be a runtime design switch, which the architecture has no path for. Verdict: not buildable as specified; buildable with a stated change — drop the runtime hand-off: a rail whose track does not overflow simply shows no fade and no arrows (a module may hide chrome on `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`; that is a measurement it can make without rebuilding), and the editor advises 1 Row when the authored set cannot overflow at 1440 (count × (box height × 3 + gap) < 1,296). Reaches: 9 Rail §Descriptor/§Items/§Fields/§Empty/§Flagged, head finding 2, §16 "9 Rail's hand-off is decided by the window", register 45.
- **arch-gap** — **F7 · `carousel`'s degradation is restated and contradicted in the same field** — FR-G7(3): the §7 sentence is an acceptance criterion restated per design. 9 Rail quotes it ("a native horizontally-scrollable `scroll-snap` strip — fully usable") and then refuses scroll-snap. The carry-forward's open ruling ("`carousel` needs a non-snap variant or A11-9's refusal is out of scope") is **verified still open**: the spec did what P0·8 rule 4 requires (ARCHITECT note on frame and in spec; no-JS state designed; no name coined) and nothing else could. Verdict: needs the ruling — register 45 gains row (e). Reaches: 9 Rail §Behaviour/§Not offered, head finding 1, §18 item 10, registry §7 row `carousel`, register 45.
- **spec-incomplete** — **F8 · 8 Marquee "hands the design to 3 Grid" under reduced motion** — a `prefers-reduced-motion` media query cannot hand one design to another (AD-3); what the spec describes is the marquee's **own** reduced-motion layout — its single `<ul>` wrapping at 3 Grid's cell geometry with an auto-fit column count — which FR-G4 permits ("CSS-only motion … sits inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`"; only mode selection is forbidden). With JS on, `core`'s gate stops the module before the duplicate copies are made, so the wrapped list is clean. The precedence (reduced motion beats no-JS; "the pause button is hidden and 2.2.2 is still met") is flagged "mine" and is the carry-forward's open item — verified still unruled. Also unstated: whether the fade mask persists over the no-JS static scrollable row (it would hide the row's ends). Verdict: buildable with a stated change — reword as the design's own state, name it for P0·6, rule the precedence. Reaches: 8 Marquee §Behaviour/§Counts/§Empty/§a11y, head finding 3, registry §7 row `marquee`, FR-G4, P0·6.
- **spec-incomplete** — **F9 · The duplicate copies are `aria-hidden` but still focusable** — 8 Marquee: the module renders the list twice or three times, "the copies `aria-hidden` with empty alts"; URLs are allowed. `aria-hidden` does not remove an `<a>` from the tab order, so a keyboard reader tabs through hidden duplicate links — and "focus pauses the track" would fire on a copy. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — the copies carry `inert` (Baseline Widely, within the FR-G8 pin — confirm under NE-A11-2) in addition to `aria-hidden`; the module contract (registry row `marquee`) states it. Reaches: 8 Marquee §a11y/§Inside an item, registry §7 row `marquee`.
- **spec-incomplete** — **F10 · Five catalog strings with no key and no channel** — the spec names "Pause the logo wall" / "Play the logo wall" / "Logo wall, scrollable" / "Scroll left" / "Scroll right" as "theme catalog strings" and stops. `appendix-h1-string-catalog.md` has no namespace for them (`gallery.*` and `a11y.*` do not cover a marquee or a rail); S9 requires the key before the design is authored; S5 and the table legend require the channel per key — the pause button is **module-written** ("What the module supplies is … the pause button", hidden with JS off) so its two strings are **JS** → `data-i18n-*` on the marquee mount; "Logo wall, scrollable" is a server-rendered `aria-label` → `{{t}}`, **a11y**; the arrows are hidden with JS off per `carousel`'s line — the spec must say whether they are server-rendered-and-hidden (`{{t}}`) or module-written (JS). Verdict: buildable with a stated change — `logos.pause` · `logos.play` (JS, a11y) · `logos.scrollable` (a11y) · `logos.scroll_left` · `logos.scroll_right` (channel per the arrow ruling). Reaches: 8 Marquee §a11y/§Reconciled, 9 Rail §a11y/§Reconciled, §0 "Editing, strings and data", appendix-h1 (new namespace), FR-Q6 S5/S9.
- **stale-design** — **F11 · `logoDark` is a second field where the PRD has a per-mode swap** — FR-D7: "Mode-scoped controls (Background role, **per-mode image swaps**, mode-specific toggles) apply to the active mode only and display a moon badge when a dark override exists"; Appendix C Image Picker: "per-mode swap capable"; FR-F5 the moon badge. A11 models the dark file as a separate item field `logoDark` with its own upload, warning and "effectively required" rule on 7 Contrast Band. The spec's own amendment 1 ("`logoDark` is not a dark-mode file, it is a dark-ground file") is the argument for a field — the PRD's model is per mode, the band's need is per ground, and neither document names the other. Verdict: flag, do not guess — the owner rules whether the dark logo is the Image Picker's mode override (then 7 Contrast Band reads the override in light mode) or an item field (then FR-D7's swap is not used here and the moon badge does not appear). Reaches: §0 field list, §0 dark ground, 7 Contrast Band §Inside an item/§Fields, FR-D7, FR-F5, Appendix C, AD-30.
- **consistent** — SVG uploads: FR-K2 sanitises SVG (script/`foreignObject` stripped) and FR-K1 has an Image/SVG/Logo filter, so "SVG preferred" is supported; raster uploads become WebP ≤ 2400 px, so "PNG at 2×" is really "WebP at 2×" — a wording fix. `color-mix()` for 7's derived values and `filter: grayscale(1)` are inside the FR-G8 pin. D39 ✓ (9 Rail refuses auto-advance). No Ghost binding anywhere → FR-H8 has nothing to guard and the spec says so (§18 item 15/16). The `marquee` §7 sentence is quoted verbatim in 8 Marquee's Behaviour field ✓.
- **needs-execution** — **F12 · `mask-image` and `inert` against the FR-G8 pin** — 8 Marquee's fade and 9 Rail's end mask need `mask-image`; FR-G8 forbids every prefix but three, so `-webkit-mask-image` is a CI failure and the unprefixed property must be Baseline Widely on 2026-08-18; `inert` (F9) likewise. Probe NE-A11-2. Reaches: 8 Marquee §Arrangement (Edge: Fade), 9 Rail §Arrangement, FR-G8.

#### Needs execution (this category)
- **NE-A11-1** — claim (§0, 7 Contrast Band): `<picture>` + `prefers-color-scheme` selects the right file "with JavaScript off, in both modes". Probe: fixture theme on T1/T3 with `config.custom.color_scheme` pinned **Dark** (FR-Q5's built-in), a `<picture>` with a dark `<source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">` and a light `<img>`, rendered in a browser whose OS is light; record which file loads. Expected: the light file (the browser has no idea about `scheme-dark`) — evidence for F1. Repeat with `[data-mode="dark"]` set by `mode-toggle`.
- **NE-A11-2** — claim: `mask-image` (unprefixed) and `inert` are usable under FR-G8. Probe (not Ghost): `web-features` lookup with `widelyAvailableOnDate: 2026-08-18` for `mask-image` / `masking` and `inert`; confirm `stylelint-plugin-use-baseline` at `available: "widely"` passes an unprefixed `mask-image` rule. If `mask-image` is Newly, the fade needs the Tier-2 allowlist (it is decorative, so it qualifies) — state it.

## A12 · About and Team
**Counts (derived):** designs on disk 15 (16 frames `A12-*` − `A12-0 Category Proof`) · spec 15 (`## 1 · Grid` … `## 15 · Groups`) · inventory 15 (line 270–286 — **but under different names, see C5**) · [Free] spec **0 marked** / inventory 2 (#1 Founder Letter, #2 Team Grid; by FR-G2's "first two" the export's [Free] pair is 1 Grid + 2 Cards) · modules declared: `carousel` (13 Rail), `accordion` (14 Reveal), `core` "assumed, not declared" — all registry names, none invented; `reveal`, `load-more`, `filter-strip`, `toc`, `search-expand`, `count-up` named only as refusals · custom-setting slots: **0** (no design promotes anything; grep "custom setting" → none) · authored lists: `people[]` (1–24, item `{name, role, bio, photo, url, group, socials[]}`) with a **nested** authored list `socials[]` (0–4 per person) · Ghost-bound lists: the same `people[]` at Source Ghost authors (`{{#get "authors"}}`, Limit ≤ 24, P0·3 Ghost card **plus one editable field per row**) · control high-water mark 7 (2 Cards, 3 Rows) + 4 Data rows + 3 universal = 14, under FR-F3's ≈15+3.

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **ghost-infeasible** — **§0 "The initials block" / every design's Empty line except 10 Directory, at Source Ghost authors** — claim: a person with no `profile_image` draws two initials ("first letter of the first word and the first letter of the last word … 'van der Meer' gives VM"), "server-rendered", "no A12 design loses an authored person without JavaScript". Evidence: Ghost's helper directory has no substring/first-letter helper — `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` line 71/1076 (49 helper files, byte-identical 5.130.6 → 6.0.0) and line 1149 (the only v6 additions: `split`, `json`, `color_to_rgba`, `contrast_text_color`, `raw`, `search`, `social_accounts`); `{{split}}` (≥ 6.5, appendix-b1 §6) yields words, never characters. For an **authored** list the compiler knows the name and bakes "RF" at compile (§7.3 construct 1) — fine. For a **Ghost** author the name exists only at render, and Handlebars cannot produce "RF" from "Rosa Ferreira". Verdict: **not buildable on Ghost as drawn at Source Ghost authors**; buildable with a stated change — one letter via CSS `::first-letter` over the hidden name, or the silhouette `{{> "icons/avatar"}}` both official themes use (`research-ghost-empty-values.md` line 129–134), which §0 refuses, or a `core` JS branch, which §0's "server-rendered roster" refuses. Reaches: spec §0 initials paragraph, 1–9/11–15 Empty lines, A12-0 proof (photo-families card), inventory line 271 Data, register 45 (a fifth "registry does not cover" item), FR-H8 media fallback.
- **needs-execution** — **all 15 Data lines** — claim: "Only authors with at least one published post appear — the Content API returns no others". No companion states it (grep across `research-ghost-*.md` and appendix-b1 → nothing). Nothing would catch it if wrong (a Contributor with zero posts would appear as a nameless card). → NE-A12-1. Reaches: 15 Data lines, the panel copy on 15 control frames, FR-H2's `authors` shape (carry-forward).
- **needs-execution** — **§0 Order / 15 Data lines** — claim: "Order: Name A–Z · Most posts … resolved server-side". `Name A–Z` = `order="name asc"`; `Most posts` = `{{#get "authors" include="count.posts" order="count.posts desc"}}`. appendix-b1 §5 cites `include="count.posts"` for author lists but never an `order=` on an included count. → NE-A12-2. Reaches: §0 Order, 8 Founder ("whoever the Order returns first"), 9 Faces ("Order Name A–Z is the Ghost-mode equivalent of Sort A–Z"), FR-H2 `authors` shape.
- **buildable with a stated change** — **§0 Data "Authors: All · Hand-picked"** — Hand-picked authors compile to one `{{#get "authors" filter="slug:[a,b,c]" limit="N"}}`; the API returns them in **its** order, so a pick order cannot be honoured (same class as D5's hand-picked posts). A12 handles this correctly by keeping the Order row live at Hand-picked — but **P0·5 says the opposite** ("Hand-picked … Count and Order hide — the picked list is the count and the order"), see C6. Verdict: buildable as A12 states; P0·5 must not promise pick order for authors. → NE-A12-6 confirms `slug:[…]` on authors. Reaches: P0·5 Filter row, A12 §0 Data, FR-H2 shape, D5.
- **needs-execution** — **§0 "The name is the link" / 15 Data lines, "Socials arrive from the author's own handles, version-gated: Facebook and X on Ghost 5.x, all nine platform fields on ≥ 6.36"** — D22 rules the gate and the spec restates it, but appendix-b1 §6 gates only the seven **`@site.*`** fields at ≥ 6.36.0; §4.4 lists all nine **author** handles with **no gate**, and `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` line 1090 speaks of `@site` only. Whether the author-object handles share the 6.36 floor, or a different minor, is unread. → NE-A12-3. Reaches: appendix-b1 §4.4 (needs the gate row), FR-H7 version axis, D22, twelve Data lines, `ghostCompat.minVersion` per design (FR-G3) — a design at Socials Shown + Source Ghost authors has a conditional floor the spec never states.
- **buildable with a stated change** — **socials row at Source Ghost authors (12 designs)** — the spec never names the helper. The legal emission is one `{{#if bluesky}}<a href="{{social_url type="bluesky"}}" rel="me">…{{/if}}` per platform inside the authors loop: `{{social_url}}` is ungated (appendix-b1 §6 "not gated, contrary to common belief"), both official themes iterate the handles this way (`research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` line 494), and `{{#social_accounts}}` (≥ 6.38, a gscan **error** below it — appendix-b1 §6) must never be emitted. Verdict: buildable once the spec names `{{social_url}}` and bans `{{#social_accounts}}`. Reaches: §0 link paragraph, 1–8/12–15 a11y lines, `ghostCompat.helpers[]`.
- **buildable with a stated change** — **Role override and Image focus "stored in the theme against the author's slug" (§0, Items ×15, Reconciliation note 6)** — the theme has no per-author storage; "stored in the theme" can only mean the compiler bakes a `{{#match slug "=" "okonjo"}}Editor{{/match}}` chain (or `data-focus` equivalent) inside the loop — `{{#match}}` with `=` per `research-ghost-empty-values.md` line 508. That needs (a) a content-model map `roleOverrides{slug→role}` / `focusOverrides{slug→focus}` that the sixteen-field list does not carry (§5), and (b) disclosure that a renamed Ghost slug orphans the override silently. Verdict: buildable with the map added and the staleness stated. Reaches: §0 shared field list, P0·3 (register 44), §7.3 directive table (a per-key override on a Ghost repeat is a construct the eight directives cannot express), AD-3 (see §4).
- **needs-execution** — **15 Data lines, "a name links to the author page only where the site's routes actually publish author pages … nothing is generated where they do not"** — the theme cannot know at render whether the `author` taxonomy exists; Inflozo can, because it authored `routes.yaml` (FR-I2) — so this is a **compile-time** condition, and the spec should say so. What `{{url}}` returns for an author when the taxonomy is removed (null, or a path that 404s) is unread. → NE-A12-4. Reaches: carry-forward "route-awareness mechanism — one mechanism, four consumers" (A12 is a fifth), FR-I2, 15 Data lines.
- **needs-execution** — **§0 "Ghost's bio has no length limit, so an over-length Ghost bio is clamped by line"; 2 Cards / 3 Rows / 13 Rail / 8 Founder clamp lines** — Ghost's `users.bio` column is, to my reading of core `data/schema/schema.js`, `maxlength: 200`, which would make the premise false (the clamps stay useful — 200 characters still exceed three lines in a 306 card — but "no length limit" is a Ghost claim no companion backs). → NE-A12-5. Reaches: §0 role/bio paragraph, four clamp lines, inventory line 271.
- **buildable with a stated change** — **`{{#get "authors"}}` placement** — legal on every template (appendix-b1 §5 "Author list, author post counts") **except** `error.hbs` under Inflozo's rule (appendix-b1 §3c, "no `{{#get}}` in error.hbs"). The spec never says A12 at Source Ghost authors is unplaceable on `error.hbs` (or that the source disables there). Reaches: §0 Data, FR-G3 `compileTarget`, A31.
- **consistent** — Limit ≤ 24 sits under FR-H2's 100 cap; `limit="all"` never needed. 12 Big Type's "held people are not in the DOM" is §7.3's `data-repeat-limit` for authored lists and `limit=` in Ghost mode — one mechanism, correctly described. 15 Groups at Source Ghost "draws as 1 Grid" is a **compile-time** hand-off (Source is a compile-time value) — the one hand-off in Ghost mode that needs no render-time switch.

#### 2 · Contradictions
- **C1 · stale-design** — **14 Reveal, Behaviour module + a11y; head finding 1** — the drawn trigger is `<button aria-expanded aria-controls>` "named with `aria-labelledby`", and the spec rules "the drawn panel is the authority". The registry's `accordion` no-JS statement is **native `<details>`** (`research-section-js-libraries.md` §7 line 552), FR-G7(3) and FR-G4 say **the server-rendered state is the real one and JS enhances it**, and the PRD outranks a design (brief §Precedence). A `<button>` has no server-rendered state, so as drawn the design has **no no-JS state at all** — the registry's `<details>` is the markup and the button is what JS must not replace it with. The spec's premise that `aria-labelledby` "is not expressible in `<details>` markup" is also unsupported: `aria-labelledby` is a global ARIA attribute and is valid on `<summary>`; whether assistive tech honours it on a summary is the open question, not the HTML. Reaches: 14 Reveal Behaviour/a11y/Behaviour-modules table, head finding 1, D19 (`details-name` grouping presumes `<details>`), register 45, FR-G7 §7 accordion row.
- **C2 · stale-design** — **13 Rail, Behaviour module + Behaviour; head finding 3** — declares `carousel` and "refuses snapping"; the module's no-JS statement **is** a `scroll-snap` strip (§7 line 554), so the JS-on state would have to *remove* the snap the no-JS state ships — enhancement inverted. The carry-forward already names it ("`carousel` needs a non-snap variant or A11-9's refusal is out of scope"); A13-8 settles for snap. Reaches: 13 Rail Behaviour, A11-9, registry row 13, carry-forward Registry.
- **C3 · stale-design** — **9 Faces Controls "Row gap: Tight 24 · Comfortable 32"** — D26 rules gap names **Tight/Even/Airy** library-wide; "Comfortable" is the Vertical-spacing scale's label, and Appendix C (line 943) forbids borrowing another scale's labels. Should read Tight · Even. Reaches: 9 Faces Controls, `A12-9` panel frame, Appendix C scale table, D26.
- **C4 · stale-design** — **2 Cards "Card padding: Compact · Comfortable · Spacious"; 10 Directory "Density: Compact · Comfortable"** — both borrow another scale's labels (Vertical spacing's trio; the Style Pack's Spacing density Compact/Comfortable/Airy) for a different ladder, against Appendix C's "no surface … borrows another scale's labels"; D7 asks genuinely different ladders to be **renamed**, not relabelled with the universal's words. Reaches: 2 Cards / 10 Directory Controls and panel frames, Appendix C, D7.
- **C5 · prd-defect** — **inventory line 270–286 vs the export** — the inventory's A12 is fifteen *other* designs (Founder Letter, Team Grid, Portrait Split, Timeline Story, Values Cards, Photo Collage, Mission Big Type, Team Masonry, Author Bind Grid, Culture Gallery, Split Manifesto, Stats-Backed About, Quote-Led About, Compact Bio List, Hiring Capped) with content `team[] {name, role, image, link?}`, `values[]?`, `images[]` and controls "team columns, portrait shape (Square/Rounded/Circle), values toggle". The export's fifteen implement none of them by name; `team[]` is `people[]`; there is no `values[]`, no `images[]`, no portrait-shape control (the spec refuses a family switch in §0), no values toggle, no masonry, no timeline, no stat row, no join-us band. D11's precedent (the export stands; the inventory merge re-derives) exists for A31 only. Reaches: inventory line 270–286, FR-G1/FR-G2 Free mapping (#1/#2 names), register 44 (`team[]`), §7.3 construct 1 (`team[]`, `values[]`), `research-section-js-libraries.md` §2.2 masonry row ("A12 #8" — the export's #8 is Founder; **no masonry exists in A12**, so the brief's "masonry CSS on A12-8" check is moot).
- **C6 · stale-design** — **A12 §0 Data vs P0·5 Filter table** — A12 keeps **Limit and Order live at Hand-picked**; P0·5 says Hand-picked **hides Count and Order** and "the picked list is the … order". For authors the platform sides with A12 (one `{{#get}}` returns API order — §1). Two design documents disagree; do not pick silently. Reaches: P0·5 Filter row, A12 §0 Order, D5's compile mechanism for hand-picked posts (the same question, unanswered there too).
- **C7 · spec-incomplete** — **D10 / FR-Q6 / appendix-h1 S9** — the spec names four catalog strings ("Team, scrollable", "Scroll left", "Scroll right", pattern "{name} on {platform}") and **none has a key** in appendix-h1 (grep: only `post.share_on` "Share on {network}"). ## A13 · Process
**Counts (derived):** designs on disk 15 (16 frames `A13-*` − `A13-0 Category Proof`) · spec 15 (`## 1 · Three Up` … `## 15 · Sticky Rail`) · inventory 15 (line 288–304 — **under different names, see C5**) · [Free] spec **0 marked** / inventory 2 (#1 Numbered Row, #2 Vertical Timeline; by FR-G2 the export's pair is 1 Three Up + 2 Track) · modules declared: `tabs` (11 Walkthrough), `carousel` (8 Rail), `scroll-spy` (15 Sticky Rail), `core` "assumed, not declared" — all registry names; `reveal` and `count-up` refused in all fifteen, `accordion`, `filter-strip`, `search-expand`, `toc` named only as refusals · custom-setting slots: **0** · authored lists: `steps[]` (2–8, item `{title, body, label, duration, icon, image, imageAlt}`) · Ghost-bound lists: the same `steps[]` at Source From posts (P0·5 reading path: By tag · Oldest first · Count ≤ design ceiling, P0·3 read-only card) · controls: five on fourteen designs, six on 3 Rows, + Data (Source · Filter · Order · Count) + 3 universal — under FR-F3.

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **buildable with a stated change** — **D23 reading path, Data lines ×15** — claim: steps bind "a tag's posts read oldest-first". The legal emission is `{{#get "posts" filter="tag:<slug>" order="published_at asc" limit="<N≤8>" as |steps pages|}}…{{/get}}` — `{{#get "posts"}}` is legal on every template (appendix-b1 §5 "Any post list on post / page / error / private"; on list templates it is a secondary feed), a literal slug satisfies FR-H5/FR-G3's template-level-only filter rule, `limit ≤ 8` is under FR-H2's 100 cap, block params per appendix-b1 §5. **The spec never names the query or the helper** — every Data line says "P0·5 configured for reading paths" and stops. Verdict: buildable; state the emission. Reaches: 15 Data lines, A13-1 bound-state strip, FR-H2 (a "By tag, Oldest first, fixed" configuration of the Data group), inventory line 289 Data (currently none).
- **buildable with a stated change** — **"0 and 1 → does not render", Data lines ×15** — `{{else}}` on `{{#get}}` fires **only on error** (appendix-b1 §5), so zero is the inner `{{#foreach}}`'s `{{else}}` (FR-H4 (2): a secondary feed renders nothing, heading and container together); **one** needs a count test before the loop — `{{#match pages.total ">=" 2}}` (`{{#match}}` operators `=, !=, >, >=, <, <=` — `research-ghost-empty-values.md` line 508; `posts.length` used the same way at line 283). Unstated; and the aborted-`{{#get}}` state (`<span data-aborted-get-helper>`, appendix-b1 §5, FR-H8) has no Empty line. → NE-A13-2 for `pages.total` under a `limit`. Reaches: 15 Data/Empty lines, FR-H4, FR-H8.
- **stale-design** — **`body ← custom excerpt`, Data lines ×15** — `{{custom_excerpt}}` is in post scope (appendix-b1 §4.2), but **D30 rules "list/grid excerpts fall back to Ghost's generated excerpt; framed excerpts stay custom-only"** and the spec binds custom-only without saying which class a step's body is (a step in 1 Three Up is a grid cell; in 4 Cards a card). A post with no custom excerpt draws "a numeral and a title alone" in bound mode — the D30 fallback (`{{excerpt}}`) would fill it. Also the 240/400 ceiling: `{{custom_excerpt}}` has no `characters=` argument (`{{excerpt characters="240"}}` does) — the clamp for a long custom excerpt is unstated. Verdict: buildable either way; the owner picks. Reaches: 15 Data lines, D30, FR-H2 meta toggles ("excerpt").
- **spec-incomplete** — **`image ← feature image`, `imageAlt` in bound mode** — the spec lists `label`, `duration`, `icon` as source-less but is silent on `imageAlt`; post scope carries `feature_image_alt` (appendix-b1 §4.1/§4.2) and the build-contract carry-forward's pattern is "feature-image captions bind `post.feature_image_caption`, never a section field". Emission: `{{#if feature_image}}<img src="{{img_url feature_image size="m"}}" alt="{{feature_image_alt}}">{{else}}plate{{/if}}` (FR-H8 media guard). Reaches: 7/8/11/12 Data + a11y lines ("the picture carries `imageAlt`").
- **needs-execution / spec-incomplete** — **gated posts in a reading path** — `posts` default `visibility` is `'all'` (appendix-b1 §4.1), so a members-only or paid post appears as a step whose link lands on a paywall; FR-H2's Data group has no visibility filter and the spec is silent. What `{{custom_excerpt}}` / `{{excerpt}}` render for a paid post through `{{#get}}` is unread. → NE-A13-1. Reaches: 15 Data lines, FR-H2, P0·5 constraints.
- **consistent (useful)** — **the numeral** — bound mode: `@number` (appendix-b1 §4.1 loop vars; §7.3 construct 5), zero-padded with `{{#match @number "<" 10}}0{{/match}}{{@number}}` or CSS `counter(step, decimal-leading-zero)` in a `::before` (which is also natively `aria-hidden`); authored mode: the position is baked at compile (§7.3 construct 1). `<ol role="list">` for Safari's `list-style: none` is correct. `{{url}}` for the bound link inside the open `{{#get}}` context (appendix-b1 §4.2).
- **buildable with a stated change** — **8 Rail's precondition** — the spec calls it "a measurement no module makes" and then does the arithmetic itself: "a 380 card at 3:2 … three and a bit fill 1,296, which is why a fourth step makes this a rail". At the pack's content width (a Style Pack token, FR-F2) it is a **count**: Standard 3 × 380 + 2 × 24 = 1,188 fits, four overflow; Narrow 4 × 306 + 3 × 24 = 1,296 fits exactly, five overflow. Compile-time for authored lists; `{{#match steps.length ">" 3}}` in bound mode; below 1,296 the rail ↔ grid is a media query on the same `<ol>`. Verdict: buildable without any module branch. Reaches: head finding 3, 8 Rail Behaviour/Data, A12-13 (same), register 45 ("A1's hero probe is not a module — resolved server-side").
- **consistent** — `carousel` (8) accepts snap: its no-JS line is registry §7 line 554 verbatim and the JS-on state adds only arrows and fades — the one rail in the library where JS-off and JS-on agree. `scroll-spy` (15): registry line 561 verbatim; `position: sticky` and real `<a href="#step-n">` anchors are the no-JS state. FR-D20 edit-safe on all three ✓ (`lightbox` is the only "no").
- **consistent** — D24 `duration` is text ≤ 12, never a `<time>`, never a client-side date — D13-safe; drawn in 14 Index and 3 Rows, held elsewhere. D6: Count is a stepper at each design's ceiling; Order fixed at Oldest first is D6's "locked value drawn disabled" convention.

#### 2 · Contradictions
- **C1 · stale-design** — **11 Walkthrough a11y vs FR-G7(3)** — `role="tablist"` on the `<ol>`, `role="tab"`/`aria-selected`/`aria-controls` on each item, `role="tabpanel"` on the panel are written as the markup. With JS off, FR-G7(3)'s "server-rendered state is the real one" means the page announces a tab widget whose tabs do nothing and whose one panel is six stacked panels — an ARIA lie, and `role="tablist"` also strips the `<ol>`'s list semantics the category's headline finding depends on. The roles must be **applied by the `tabs` module** and absent from the no-JS markup. The heading-per-panel collision (registry line 553) stays the carry-forward's ruling (§6). Reaches: 11 Walkthrough a11y/Behaviour module, registry `tabs` row, A15-10/15, A8-11, A9-8, A20-4.
- **C2 · stale-design** — **P0·2 icon slot vs A13's `icon` popover** — P0·2's filled-slot popover is Size **Small · Medium · Large at the pack's icon scale (Paper 16 · 22 · 28)** and Colour **Text · Muted · Accent · On-accent**; A13 ships "Size (Small 20 · Medium 24) · Colour role (Muted · Text)". Dropping Large and Accent is a stated narrowing (accent refused on sequence marks) — fine; **20 · 24 is a different pixel ladder from the pack's 16 · 22 · 28**, so the same slot resolves to different sizes in A13 and everywhere else. Reaches: §0 `icon` paragraph, 4 Cards / 10 Panel / 13 Slim Bar Editing, component inventory "Icon box", P0·2 popover table.
- **C3 · stale-design** — **4 Cards "Card padding: Compact · Comfortable · Spacious"; 10 Panel "Panel padding: Compact · Comfortable · Spacious"; 14 Index "Density: Compact · Comfortable"** — Appendix C: scale vocabularies are closed **and distinct**; "no surface … borrows another scale's labels". All three borrow Vertical spacing's or the Style Pack's Spacing-density labels for a different ladder; D7 asks them renamed. Reaches: the three Controls lines and panel frames, Appendix C, D7.

#### 4 · Architecture asks
- **Render-time hand-offs in bound mode** — the Data lines say "7 or 8 → 14 Index, **bound or authored**", "2 → 7 Alternating Media", "5 or more → 3 Rows", "under four → 1 Three Up". Count caps the over-case; the **under-case is live**: a tag with two posts on 11 Walkthrough, or one post on any design, is known only at render, and after deploy the tag's post count changes. A render-time design switch needs two designs' markup and CSS in one partial — FR-G7(2) emits only placed designs, AD-14 compiles a pure function. Buildable alternative: in bound mode the design draws what arrives within its own range and the hand-off is an FR-H4 editor advisory. **No owner; needs one** (AD-14, FR-G7(2), FR-H4). Same class as A12.
- **`bindingContext` per Data value; main-feed exclusion** — owner: **FR-G3 / FR-H2 — no owner; needs one**.
- **`tabs` no-JS heading branch** — carry-forward Registry ruling ("settle once"; covers A8-11, A13-11, A15-10/15). Owner: the architect / register 45. Add C1: the ARIA roles are module-applied.
- **Per-width module declaration** (15 Sticky Rail) — the registry has no such concept; either `scroll-spy` gains a "no list → no-op" guarantee or the list stays in the DOM. Owner: **registry / no owner; needs one**.
- **Per-item Image focus vs AD-3** — same ask as A12 (an authored `image` per step carrying `object-position`; AD-3's carve-out is bound-data-only). Owner: **AD-3**.
- **8 Rail precondition = count at the site-width token** — owner: **register 45** (the "not a module — resolved server-side" family). Head finding 3 dissolves.
- **`carousel` snap** — 8 Rail accepts it; A12-13 and A11-9 refuse it → the same module cannot have both; owner: carry-forward Registry ("non-snap variant or the refusal is out of scope"). A13 is the registry-conformant side.
- **`duration` timing rule** (head finding 4 / Reconciliation note 7): "adding to a shared list after a category is drawn changes every design's kept-and-not-drawn line" — a process rule for FR-G3's `contentSchema` union. Owner: **no owner; needs one** (the architect, for A16 onward).
- **D30 scope** — whether a bound step body is a "list/grid" excerpt (fallback) or "framed" (custom-only). Owner: the D30 ruling's author, at the merge.
- **Four catalog keys** — appendix-h1 at the merge (D10).
- **P0·5 "reading path" configuration** — the spec configures P0·5 with Filter By tag only, Order fixed, Count ≤ 8; P0·5 has no "locked configuration" concept. Owner: P0·5 — no owner; needs one (one sentence: a category may fix P0·5 rows with the reason shown).
