#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **consistent** — **all 15 · the query** — claim: `{{#get "authors" include="count.posts" limit=N order="count.posts desc"}}` / `order="name asc"` — evidence: `appendix-b1-template-contexts.md` §5 line 208 ("Author list, author post counts → `{{#get "authors" include="count.posts"}}`"), `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` lines 985/988, docs `themes/helpers/functional/get` (its own example orders authors by `count.posts desc`) — verdict: buildable. Reaches: spec §0 Data group, every design's item 7.
- **needs-execution** — **all 15 · Order: Newest account** — claim: `order="created_at desc"` on the Content API authors browse — evidence: no companion lists `created_at` on the author object (`appendix-b1` §4.4 line 191 omits it; the Content API strips it from the output) so whether the endpoint accepts it as an order key is unread — verdict: needs execution (NE-A21-1). Reaches: spec §0 Data group `authorOrder`, 10 Directory item 6 (Group by letter gates on Order).
- **consistent** — **author fields** — claim: `name`, `profile_image`, `bio`, `location`, `website`, `url`, `count.posts` (with `include`), nine handles legal inside `{{#foreach authors}}` under a `{{#get}}` — evidence: `appendix-b1` §4.4 line 191 + §5 line 193 ("No `count.posts` without `{{#get}}`") — verdict: buildable. `cover_image` is equally legal and no design binds it (§3 G1). Reaches: shared field list lines 348–356.
- **needs-execution** — **6 always; 1, 2, 12, 13 at Social links: On · the nine handles** — claim: "Ghost ≥ 6.36 stores nine handles and a website; version-gated below 6.36 to Facebook, X and the website" (D22) — evidence: `appendix-b1` §6 line 232 gates the **`@site.*`** seven at ≥ 6.36.0; **no companion states the floor for the author-level seven** (§4.4 lists them ungated), and no companion states the stored value shape per platform (username vs URL), which decides whether a raw field can be an `href` at all — verdict: needs execution (NE-A21-2). Reaches: spec settlement 1, finding 7, `a21-kit.js` `legacy` flag, FR-H7's version axis, Appendix B "Author" line 909 (lists only twitter/facebook — stale against `appendix-b1` §4.4).
- **ghost-infeasible as written** — **the social row's URLs** — claim: "The author's own fields are read, never `social_url` — that helper falls back to the site's Facebook and X" — evidence: the stored values are **handles, not URLs** — the docs' author object (`docs.ghost.org/content-api/authors/`) shows `"twitter": "@example"`, `"facebook": "example"`, `"bluesky": "ghost.org"`, and `schema.js` `users.*` social columns carry no URL validation; `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` line 1114 (the `*_url` helpers exist to build the URL) and `appendix-b1` §6 line 241 (the deprecated `{{twitter_url}}`/`{{facebook_url}}` are gscan-warned; use `{{social_url type=…}}`) — the brief's standing rule says the same — verdict: a raw field cannot be an `href`; the row must go through `{{social_url}}` or a stated per-platform URL rule. The spec's fallback claim is uncited — NE-A21-3: whether `{{social_url type="x"}}` inside `{{#foreach authors}}` reads `this.x` or `@site.x`, and whether it accepts the seven new types. Reaches: §0 "The social surface, corrected", finding 7 third consequence, 6 Founder item 5/10, component "Author social row", `a21-kit.js` `socialRow`.
- **buildable with a stated change** — **all 15 at Hand-picked · picked order is drawn order** — claim: "Picked order is drawn order, which is why Order disables" — evidence: `{{#get "authors" filter="slug:[a,b,c]"}}` returns Ghost's order, never the pick order, and Handlebars cannot reorder; read queries (`{{#get "authors" slug="a"}}`) accept only `include` (`appendix-b1` §5 line 220) and would cost one round trip per reference with the §5 line 222 abort risk each — verdict: buildable with a stated change: the compiler emits one `{{#get}}` over the slug list and then, per reference (known at compile time), `{{#foreach authors}}{{#match slug "=" "<pick>"}}…{{/match}}{{/foreach}}` — drawn order = pick order, one query. **This emission pattern is stated nowhere** and is the same problem for every hand-picked source D5 added (A20 tags, A12 authors, A17/A18/A19/A27/A3-9 posts, A22-12). Reaches: spec §0 "Hand-picked, in full", finding 8, FR-H2 `authors` carry-forward, P0·5 "the picked list is the count and the order", §7.3 compiler constructs.
- **buildable with a stated change** — **7 Panel, 8 Faces, 11 Rail, 15 Slim · the remainder and the count line** — claim: `pagination.total` gives "12 writers" and "and N others" — evidence: block params `{{#get "authors" as |authors pagination|}}` are legal (`appendix-b1` §5 line 221) — verdict: buildable at *All writers*; **at Hand-picked the filtered query's `pagination.total` equals the number of picks**, so "and N others" is always 0 (which the spec forbids drawing) and "12 writers" reads the pick count. A second unfiltered `{{#get "authors" limit=1 as |a p|}}` is needed for the true total — not stated. Reaches: 7 item 7, 8 item 7, 11 item 7/8, 15 item 7, component "Assembled credit sentence" / "Generated count line".
- **ghost-infeasible** — **10 Directory · Group by letter: On** — claim: a letter-grouped directory drawn server-side at Order: Name A–Z — evidence: Handlebars has no access to the previous item and Ghost ships no first-letter helper (`{{split}}` ≥ 6.5 splits on a separator, `{{#match}}` compares whole values — `appendix-b1` §6, §9); inserting a heading when the initial changes needs either a module (none coined — the spec says "This pass coined no module name") or 26 pre-scanned sub-loops that still cannot emit a heading conditionally on "any match" — verdict: not buildable on Ghost as specified; either a registry module (client-side grouping, with a no-JS state of the ungrouped table) or the value is cut. Reaches: 10 item 6/10, roster row 10, inventory line 453 (#15 Alphabet Index), FR-G7 registry, P0·8 rule 4 (must carry "ARCHITECT: registry addition").
- **buildable with a stated change** — **12 Carousel · "Arrows and dots render only when the strip overflows, decided server-side from the item count and card width, not by the module at runtime"** — evidence: overflow depends on viewport width (three 280-px cards overflow a 754 box at 834 and not a 1,296 box at 1440); the registry's `carousel` contract is that the module shows dots/arrows and the no-JS strip hides them (`research-section-js-libraries.md` §7 line 554) — verdict: buildable only if the runtime decides; a server-side decision is wrong at two of the three widths. Reaches: 12 item 7/8, FR-G7 `carousel` entry.
- **consistent** — **all 15 · "`{{#get "authors"}}` returns only authors with a published post" (finding 1)** — evidence: no companion cites it (A12 repeats it uncited), but `docs.ghost.org/content-api/authors/` states it: *"Authors that are not associated with a post are not returned"* — verdict: buildable as claimed; NE-A21-4 narrows to the Contributor-with-one-published-post case. **Contributor/staff roles**: the Content API author object (`appendix-b1` §4.4; the docs' example object) carries no `roles` and no `created_at`, so finding 5 ("Ghost authors have no role") holds for templates whatever the Admin API knows — **consistent**. Reaches: finding 1, finding 5, §0 "Internal accounts have no control", A12.
- **consistent** — **1–4, 6, 10, 12, 13 · `roleOverride`** — claim: a slug-keyed authored string drawn inside the Ghost loop — evidence: compile as `{{#match slug "=" "<slug>"}}<static text-plus-marks>{{/match}}` inside `{{#foreach authors}}` (`appendix-b1` §9 sub-expressions, AD-4) — verdict: buildable; the **content-model shape** (a map keyed by a Ghost slug) is the ask (§4).
- **consistent** — **14 Image Band · `backgroundImage`** — claim: "a CSS background on a real `{{img_url}}`" — evidence: an Inflozo-hosted upload is an external URL to `{{img_url}}`, which passes it through unsized (renditions are made at upload — AD-12) — verdict: buildable; `Image focus → background-position` is CSS.
- **consistent** — **4, 6, 8, 11, 15 · the member-gated action** — claim: server-side `@member` — evidence: FR-G7(5), `appendix-b1` §2 line 64 (`{{#if @member}}` safe unconditionally) — verdict: buildable; the control's *scope* is the contradiction (§2 C2).
- **needs-execution** — **all 15 · the aborted query** — claim: none — evidence: `appendix-b1` §5 line 222: a slow `{{#get}}` yields an empty collection **plus a visible `<span data-aborted-get-helper>Could not load content</span>`** — verdict: every A21 design has an undesigned visible state (the span lands inside the section, and at *Hide the section* the `{{#if authors}}` wrapper hides the head but not the span unless the span is inside it). Reaches: every item 8, FR-H8.

#### 2 · Contradictions
- **stale-design** — **§0 Data group `authorLimit` "Three · Six · Twelve · All"** contradicts **D6** (Count is ONE stepper 1–100 with per-design min/max, locked values drawn disabled) and A12's own reconciled "Limit (stepper, ≤ 24)"; **"All" would emit `limit="all"`**, which FR-H2 and `appendix-b1` §5/§6 forbid (gscan v6 warning, capped ≥ 6.0). The enum also cannot hold its own defaults — "One in 6", "Four in 15", "Eight in 7 and 13" are not values of it. Reaches: §0 Data group table, "Hand-picked, in full" ("the list is the count"), 2/6/7/9/10/11/12/13/15 "How many defaulting to …", roster "Built for" line, inventory line 438 "Count".
- **stale-design** — **§0 "Member Visibility on the five CTA-bearing designs" (4, 6, 8, 11, 15)** declares Appendix C's **Member Visibility** control but scopes it to **the action alone** ("heads, rosters, faces and credit sentences are shown to everyone"). Appendix C line 938 and P0·4 define Member Visibility as **SECTION** scope ("hides a whole section"); per-action show/label/link is **P0·4's own Show toggle per state** ("ONE ACTION"). The spec has fused the two. Either the five designs carry P0·4 (and no "Member visibility" row — counts fall to 5/5/6/5/4 and the total to 82) or they carry the section-level control with SECTION semantics. Appendix C's category list ("A2, A6, A22, A26") does not include A21 either way. Reaches: §0 Editing block, 4 item 6/8/10, 6 item 6, 8 item 6, 11 item 6/10, 15 item 6, roster Ctl column, Appendix C, D8.
- **stale-design** — **§0 settlement 4 / Data group `emptyBehaviour` default "Head and notice"** contradicts **P0·5's library-wide constraint** ("A secondary feed renders nothing at zero items — heading and container together") and FR-H4 rule (2); D16 flipped A27 to "Hide the section" on exactly that rule. Whether an authors list is a "secondary feed" is the owner's call — flagged, not decided (§6). Reaches: settlement 4, every design's "0 →" line, `emptyText` (all 15), A20's equivalent row.
- **stale-design** — **`compileTarget: any`** (inventory line 437; spec §0 "sits on a page route") vs **`appendix-b1` §3c**: Inflozo's rule is no `{{#get}}` in `error.hbs`, and every A21 design is `{{#get}}`-driven → no A21 design is placeable on `error.hbs`. Reaches: inventory line 437, FR-G3 `compileTarget`, FR-D12/D13 placement filter.
- **spec-incomplete** — **roster "Eighty-eight controls of their own"** — derived sum is **87**. Reaches: roster footer, proof frame's control counts.
- **stale-design** — **Appendix C "Scale vocabularies are closed and distinct… no surface borrows another scale's labels"**: *Portrait size* (1, 3, 4, 8), *Card width* (12), *Lead portrait* (13) and *Row height* (10) reuse the **Vertical spacing** scale's labels Compact · Comfortable · Spacious for measures that are not spacing. (*Band padding* 5, *Bar padding* 8, *Strip padding* 15 are spacing and FR-F2 permits the labels.) Reaches: those seven control lists, Appendix C scale table.
- **stale-design** — **§0 "never `social_url`"** contradicts the brief's standing rule and rests on an uncited fallback claim (see §1 NE-A21-3). Reaches: settlement 1, finding 7, 6 item 5.
- **stale-design** — **12 Carousel item 9 "Edit-safe: it does not run in the editor"** — FR-D20: edit-safe is **the module's** declaration ("part of the module contract, not a per-instance setting"), and "edit-safe" means it *does* run while editing; the sentence inverts the term and declares it per design. Reaches: 12 item 9, §7.3 module table.
- **stale-design** — **inventory lines 437–453 vs the spec**: the inventory's fifteen (Author Cards, Byline Rows, Single Spotlight, Masthead, **Author + Latest** with a `posts` binding, Circle Row, Split Interview, **Contributor Wall** (masonry), Author Bento, Featured Band, Social Cards, Editorial Board, Compact Chips, **Cover Cards** on `cover_image`, Alphabet Index) share only the count with the export's fifteen. The spec explicitly refuses #5's per-author post row (finding 2) and #15's grouping is infeasible (§1). `research-section-js-libraries.md` §2.2 line 94 still cites "A21 #8" as a CSS-columns masonry wall — no A21 design is one. The supersede is unowned (git log: "the wholesale supersede is unowned"). Reaches: inventory 437–453, registry §2.2, FR-G1 count, Appendix A.

#### 5 · Spec completeness
- **Ten fields**: every one of the 15 entries carries items 1–10 in the brief's order (Tuple = structural descriptor) plus a Reconciled paragraph ✓.
- **Tuples**: all 15 six-slot; first five closed-vocabulary (archetypes grid-of-N ×5, stack ×2, split ×2, bar ×2, table, edge rail, carousel, feed; containment none ×14, card ×1; ground page ×9, contrast, surface ×2, transparent, image; count many ×12, few ×2, one; media top ×4, left ×6, right, inline, none ×2, background) ✓; **unique on the first five — no collisions** (2 vs 1 differ on count+media, 15 vs 8 on ground, 3 vs 7 on ground, 4 vs 6 on containment/count/media) ✓; no off-vocabulary word.
- **No-JS lines**: 14 designs "None — pixel-identical"; 12 quotes the registry's `carousel` sentence verbatim ✓ (§7 line 554). No invented module ✓. D2 waiver not needed ✓.
- **Lists**: `authorPicks[]` carries add (pre-filled) / remove (never disabled) / drag ✓ (register 44 authored half); the Ghost authors list carries no Add in any of the 15 ✓ (register 44 Ghost-bound half; "Ghost Admin cannot reorder authors" honoured — reorder exists only on the references). `roleOverride` per-row editing on the Ghost card is **outside P0·3 as written** (§4).
- **Quick Controls** 4 per design ✓ (3–5). Cap: max 7 own controls ✓.
- **Universal trio** outside every list ✓; locks (5, 14, 15) carry reasons ✓; **8 and 15 disable Top divider** — a universal control disabled by a design control (Rules) — AD-3-compatible but must be a schema flag (FR-F7 "dark-override capability flags" analogue) — state it once.
- **Strings**: every visitor-facing string is a field or named as a catalog string ✓ in intent; the keys do not exist (§3).
- **Frames vs sidebar**: five panels checked (1, 5, 8, 10, 15) — sidebar values are named, no px ✓.
- **Count**: 87 ≠ 88 (§2).
- **Field list**: 14 authored + 9 Ghost rows as stated ✓; Data-group fields live in the Data table, not the field list — acceptable, state it.

## A22 · Newsletter / Subscribe
**Counts (derived):** designs on disk 16 (frames 17 − `A22-0 Category Proof`) · spec 16 (`### 1 · Inline Row` … `### 16 · Quote`) · inventory 16 (line 455) · [Free] spec **none marked** (grep `[Free]` → 0; FR-G2 by position gives 1 Inline Row, 2 Card) / inventory #1 Center Card, #2 Inline Slim Bar (different designs, same positions) · modules declared: `member-form` ×16, `slide-in-card` ×1 (14) — both registry §2.1 (rows 17, 27) ✓, nothing invented · custom-setting slots: 0 (no "custom setting"/`@custom` in the spec) · authored lists: `reasons[]` (11 only, P0·3) · Ghost-bound lists: newsletters (9's label, 10, 15 — `{{#get "newsletters"}}`), posts (12 — P0·5) · controls of their own: **91 by summing the sixteen entries** (6+6+6+7+5+7+8+5+4+6+5+5+5+6+5+5), max 8 ✓ (the spec states no total) · shared field list: 25 authored rows (24 if `quoteAttrib · quoteDetail` is one) + 8 Ghost rows.

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **ghost-infeasible** — **all 16 · item 9, the no-JS floor** — claim (§0 settlement 2, 1 item 9, 10 item 9, 14 item 9, quoting the registry): "The `<form>` posts natively to Ghost's members endpoint; Ghost's own server response replaces the designed sent state" — evidence: `ghost/core/core/server/web/members/app.js` (read at `main`): `membersApp.post('/api/send-magic-link', bodyParser.json(), middleware.verifyIntegrityToken, …)` and `membersApp.get('/api/integrity-token', …)`. A native `<form method="post">` sends `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (unparsed by `bodyParser.json()`) and carries no integrity token (fetched by Ghost's script from `/api/integrity-token` before the JSON POST) — the request is rejected before any email is sent. `research-ghost-membership-pages.md` line 428 lists `/members/api/integrity-token` among the routes without drawing the consequence — verdict: **the no-JS state of every `data-members-form` in the library is not "a working form"; it is a form whose submit fails.** That is the registry's own `member-form` sentence (`research-section-js-libraries.md` §7 line 558) being wrong, and it makes D2 no longer the only no-JS gap. NE-A22-1 confirms per host. Reaches: registry §7 line 558, FR-G4 ("functional with JS disabled"), FR-G7(3), A22 §0 settlement 2 + every item 9, A3-4, A6-6, A30 #1–10, A31-10 (the `member-form` consumers), D2, register (a new row).
- **consistent** — **all 16 · the contract attributes** — claim: `data-members-form="subscribe"`, `data-members-email`, `data-members-name` (settlement 2; frames A22-1/A22-10 carry all three) — evidence: `docs.ghost.org/themes/members` ("`subscribe` — sends a subscribe email. Uses 'subscription' in email text. If a valid email is present, a signin email is sent instead"), `research-ghost-membership-pages.md` §4 line 409, Appendix B line 913 — verdict: buildable; the "already-subscribed address in the same slot" claim is the docs' signin-email branch (NE-A22-9 to see the class/response). The endpoint itself is read-only ✓.
- **spec-incomplete** — **all 16 · which newsletter the address lands on** — claim: "post to the newsletter named in the shared source group, defaulting to the site's own default, and the sidebar names which one"; 10/15 "post with the address" — evidence: the attribute that does this, **`data-members-newsletter`**, appears nowhere in the spec or on frames A22-1/A22-10 (`grep data-members-` → form/email/name only). Docs: `<input data-members-newsletter type="hidden" value="Weekly Threads" />` — **the value is the newsletter's name**, one input per letter; "when a member signs up via the form, they are subscribed to the site's default newsletter" — Ghost's model is `subscribe_on_signup` per newsletter (schema `newsletters.subscribe_on_signup defaultTo true`), so on a multi-letter site "the site default" can be several and "the sidebar names which one" cannot be one name — verdict: buildable with a stated change: emit `data-members-newsletter` inputs (hidden at *A named newsletter*, real checkboxes in 10, one per card in 15), resolve the stored id to the name at compile or via `{{#get "newsletters" filter="id:…"}}…value="{{name}}"`, and replace "site default" with "Ghost's subscribe-on-signup letters". NE-A22-3. Reaches: settlement 3, source group `newsletterTarget`, 1 item 7, 9 `label` default, 10 item 9, 15 item 9, component "Ghost's form contract", Appendix B line 913.

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **consistent** — **Full content (`searchIn`), all result designs** — claim: the client index can fetch `plaintext` — evidence: `docs.ghost.org/content-api/parameters.md` ("each post and page in Ghost has 2 available formats: `html` and `plaintext`… `&formats=html,plaintext`"); the key is browser-safe (`docs.ghost.org/content-api/`: "Content API keys are safe for use in browsers"); NFR-3 permits `{{content_api_key}}` explicitly — verdict: buildable. Reaches: spec §0 settlement 4, source group `searchIn`, finding 1.
- **spec-incomplete** — **Key and URL sourcing, every `search-overlay`/`command-palette` design** — claim: "A23's index is client-side over the Content API" (stated ≥ 8 times) — evidence: the spec never names `{{content_api_key}}` / `{{content_api_url}}`; Appendix B (prd.md 903) assigns those two core helpers to "A23's overlay"; §7.3 item 9 (prd.md 533) lists `{{content_api_key}}` (A23) as a bare-helper binding; FR-J4 fixes the emission channel (attributes on the module's mount element); AD-10 pins `Accept-Version` on every browser Content read; `appendix-b1-template-contexts.md` §2 (line 50) lists the universal helper set **without** the two helpers — verdict: buildable with a stated change: the module contract must say the mount carries `data-api-url="{{content_api_url}}" data-api-key="{{content_api_key}}"` plus a pinned `Accept-Version`, and which endpoints the four `searchScope` values hit (`/posts/`, `/pages/`, `/tags/`, `/authors/`). Reaches: spec §0 "Behaviour", every design's field 9, Appendix B, appendix-b1 §2, FR-J4, AD-10, research-section-js-libraries §2.1 row 4.
- **needs-execution** — **Index build, all result designs** — claim: a 400-post archive "fetches a few megabytes before the first query" — evidence: `limit` max 100 (`parameters.md`: "`&limit=100` will return 100 records (max)"; `research-contested-variants.md` §5.2 `max-limit-cap.js`), so a full index is ⌈N/100⌉ paged requests **per resource** (posts, pages, tags, authors) per visitor; the docs warn "`fields`… does not play well with include", and the spec wants `primary_tag`/`primary_author` (need `include=tags,authors`) alongside `plaintext` (needs `formats=`); Ghost rate-limits Content keys (FR-H4 names it for the editor — the live site shares the key); the spec states no build trigger (page load? focus? first keystroke?), no cache (Cache API / sessionStorage?), no 429/offline state (the catalog has `search.overlay_error`; the spec has no error state at all) — verdict: needs execution (NE-A23-1) and a stated fetch strategy. - **needs-execution** — **Titles-and-excerpts mode, all result designs** — claim: the index is built from `/posts/` — evidence: `research-contested-variants.md` §5.2: `GET /content/search-index/posts/` returns up to **10,000** posts in one request with exactly `id, slug, title, excerpt, url, updated_at, visibility` and bypasses the cap — which is the default scope's whole field set minus `published_at`/`feature_image`; whether it exists on 5.130.6 and what it returns for members-only posts is unread — verdict: needs execution (NE-A23-2); if it holds on both majors the default mode is one request instead of ⌈N/100⌉. Reaches: spec 5 §7/§10, 13 §7/§10, finding 4, finding 7, registry §7 `filter-strip`, register 45(b).
- **spec-incomplete** — **13 Facet Rail, years facet** — claim: years "with post counts… where the site has the route" — evidence: no Ghost resource is a year; counts need either the full index client-side or one `{{#get "posts" filter="published_at:>='2026-01-01'+published_at:<'2027-01-01'" limit="1" as |p pages|}}` per year server-side; year routes exist only as `routes.yaml` collections the editor can know about only when Inflozo authored them (appendix-b1 §3 `custom-{name}` route row; FR-I2) — verdict: buildable with a stated change (client-side counts from the index; route list read from the project's own routes.yaml, never from a user-uploaded one). Reaches: spec 13 §7/§8, finding 5, FR-I2.
- **spec-incomplete** — **`tagChips[]` / `trailingTags[]` compile strategy, 5 and 9** — claim: "a renamed tag renames the chip and a deleted tag drops it silently" with counts, in the publication's own order — evidence: one `{{#get "tags" filter="slug:[a,b,c]"}}` returns Ghost's order, not the authored one, and no Handlebars construct re-sequences a `{{#get}}` result (§7.3 table has none); N per-chip `{{#get "tags" filter="slug:a" limit="1" include="count.posts"}}` blocks give live names in authored order at the cost of 2–6 gets per render (each abortable, appendix-b1 §5); baking names at compile makes the rename claim false until redeploy — verdict: buildable with a stated change; the construct ("authored ordered references to Ghost objects resolved at render") is the same one D5's Hand-picked posts need and is missing from §7.3. Reaches: spec §0 repeating items, 5 §7, 9 §7, §7.3 missing-construct table, D5, register 44.

#### 2 · Contradictions
- **stale-design** — **D3 not restated (FR-G7).** The spec never names MiniSearch, the vendored file, its licence or its size; D3 (ruled 2026-08-24) puts the engine "inside the registry's `search-overlay` module (the cards.js pattern)". FR-G7 (1) still asserts "`assets/js/` contains only files authored in the Inflozo repository (`cards.js` is the declared exception)" — a second declared exception is now owed; NFR-2 still says "the largest single module (`search-overlay`) at 1.8 KB" and research §4 table row `search-overlay` 1.8 KB — with a ~7 KB engine the module is ≈ 9 KB and the maximal page ≈ 24.5 KB (still < 40). Reaches: spec §0 "Behaviour" and every field 9, D3, FR-G7 (1), FR-J4, NFR-2, research-section-js-libraries §2.1 row 4 / §4 / §7, carry-forward "Registry".
- **ghost-infeasible → contradiction with registry §3.1 (normative)** — **2 Overlay and 3 Command Palette a11y.** Both declare `role="combobox"` + `aria-activedescendant` + `role="option"` rows. Registry §3 row `search-overlay`: "Build it as a search *dialog*, not an APG combobox… This is a **normative implementation constraint**, not a preference" (`<dialog>` + `<form>` + `<input type="search">` + `<ul>` + one `aria-live="polite"` region). Settlement 1 keeps the thirteen documents on the dialog/list pattern and reserves combobox for exactly the two designs the registry forbids it on. Also 2 §10 pairs `aria-modal="true"` with "the page behind… is not made inert" — `showModal()` makes it inert; the two sentences cannot both hold. Reaches: spec settlement 1, 2 §10, 3 §10, registry §3 row `search-overlay`, `command-palette` row ("reuses `search-overlay`'s dialog").
- **spec-incomplete → contradiction with registry** — **3 Command Palette's trigger.** Registry: "needs a visible trigger too (a keyboard-only entry point fails 2.1.1)". Settlement 1 says every A1 affordance opens **2 Overlay**; nothing in the spec opens 3. 3's no-JS line quotes "the visible search trigger remains" without naming one. Reaches: spec settlement 1, 3 §1/§9/§10, A1 §0 search affordance (line 60), registry §3 row `command-palette`.
- **prd-defect (decision propagation) — D6.** `resultCap` (10 · 20 · 50 · All matches), 2's Rows shown (Five · Eight · Ten), 3's Rows per group (Two · Three · Five), 14's Batch size (Ten · Twenty) are fixed count enums; D6 rules "one stepper (1–100) with per-design min/max and locked values drawn disabled replaces them all". Showing 8 of 12." (14 §10), the button name "Loading" (14 — `pagination.load_more_loading` exists and is not cited), "Clear recent" (implied by "the reader can clear them", no field, no key). (b) Strings the spec sends to the catalog have **no key**: "Clear search", keycaps "move · open · close" (catalog §3.7 has only `search.key_hint_mac/win`). (c) Mechanical strings FR-Q6 names as chrome are authored fields instead: `countLabel` vs `search.overlay_results_count`, `emptyHeading` vs `search.overlay_no_results`, `loadMoreLabel` vs `pagination.load_more`, `progressLabel` vs `pagination.showing_range`, `exhaustedLabel` vs `pagination.end_of_feed`, `shortcutHint` vs `search.key_hint_mac/win`. Keys the catalog would need if the authored route stands: `search.clear`, `search.clear_recent`, `search.key_move`, `search.key_open`, `search.key_close`, `search.results_heading`, `search.sections_label`, `search.more_loaded` (JS, `{added}`, `{shown}`, `{total}`). Reaches: spec §0 "Editing" bullet 5, reconciliation note "Two strings became translation-catalog entries", 5/8/9/10/11/14 §10, appendix-h1 §3.7, FR-Q6, D10.
- **prd-defect — appendix-h1 §3.7 and the inventory are stale against the export.** §3.7's scope ("A23 #1–#8, #11, #14 are triggers for Ghost's native search overlay… strings inside Ghost's native overlay… neither catalogable nor overridable") and FR-Q6's "the catalog covers the theme-rendered search *trigger* and placeholder only" describe designs that no longer exist: every one of the 15 is theme-rendered; no design opens Sodo. No off-vocabulary word.

- Controls: 4–7 own rows per design (≤ 15 ✓); the trio outside every list ✓ (absent on 2/3 by design — §4); no slider, hex, px or width control ✓ (px appear only as spec readings).
- Empty states: 0/1/many stated per design ✓; the no-query state stated ✓; the error state absent (§3).
- Strings: see §2 — five hard-coded English strings and eight missing keys.

## A24 · Post Headers
**Counts (derived):** designs on disk 16 (frames 17 − proof `A24-0`) · spec 16 (headings A24·1…A24·16) · inventory 16 (line 494 "Post Headers (16)") · [Free] spec **0 marked** (no `[Free]` token anywhere in the spec) / inventory 2 (#1, #2 — FR-G2 "first two of every category") · modules declared: `reading-progress` (13 Sticky), `share` (14 Share Row) — both registry names (research-section-js-libraries.md §2.1 rows 21, 23); refused with homes named: `lightbox`, `video-facade`, `toc`, `typewriter`, `reveal`, `scroll-spy` · custom-setting slots: **0 or 1, undecided** — the Mastodon-instance "site setting" (A24·14, D15) is either compiled from an Inflozo project setting (0) or promoted to `@custom.mastodon_instance` (1 of 17); the ordered/enabled destinations list cannot be a Ghost custom setting at all (FR-Q2 has no list type) · authored lists: **none inside any section** (the one authored list is the site-wide Share-destinations setting, P0·3 inside the setting) · Ghost-bound lists: `post.tags[]` (first 3, Ghost's order) and `post.authors[]` (3 avatars) in all sixteen — no Add ✓, but **no P0·3 Ghost-list card is drawn for either** (see §3).

Binding declaration the spec never writes: `bindingContext: post` · `compileTarget: post.hbs, page.hbs` · every field inside `{{#post}}` on both targets (inventory line 494; appendix-b1 §3 `page` row, §4.2). The strings `{{#post}}`, `bindingContext`, `compileTarget` occur **zero** times in the spec — see §5.

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **needs-execution** — **all caption designs (1, 3, 4, 5 credit line, 6, 8 conditional, 9, 12, 16) — `post.feature_image_caption` "rendered as HTML so the credit link survives"** — claim: the caption renders as HTML. Evidence: Ghost stores the caption as HTML (appendix-b1 §4.2 lists `feature_image_caption`; FR-H3 fixture "image ×3 widths ×caption"); Handlebars' `{{ }}` HTML-escapes any non-SafeString value, so a link survives only through `{{{feature_image_caption}}}`; **§7.3 compiler mechanic 3 and AD-4 assert "exactly one permitted `{{{body}}}`, in `default.hbs`, and zero `{{{` in every other emitted file"** (prd.md lines 515–517; ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md AD-4 "The compiler never emits `{{{ }}}`"). Verdict: **needs execution + an architecture ruling** — either the FR-J17 gate allowlists a second triple-stash for this one Ghost-owned HTML field (AD-36: Ghost's caption HTML is an interpreting-sink input — is it sanitised by Ghost's editor?), or the caption renders escaped and the credit link is lost, which the spec's whole reason for the field ("the credit link a photographer needs survives") denies. Reaches: spec §0 shared field list row `post.feature_image_caption`, every Caption/Credit line row, component "Image credit line", A26·14 Ledger (same field), §7.3 mechanic 3, AD-4, AD-36, FR-J17 gate assertion, NE-A24-1.
- **ghost-infeasible** (buildable with a stated change) — **settlement 2 / every design's field 7 — "three or more draw the first name and 'and 2 others'"** — claim: the theme prints `authors.length − 1`. Evidence: Handlebars has no arithmetic; Ghost's helper set (research-ghost-binding-contexts.md line 822 SafeString audit; docs helper list) carries `{{plural}}` (takes a number, cannot subtract) and nothing that computes; `{{#foreach authors from="2"}}` can iterate the others but cannot count them. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — the join becomes a catalog phrase without a computed number ("{name} and others"), or the design enumerates every name with `@last` ("A, B and C"), and the three avatars stay as `{{#foreach authors limit="3"}}`. Reaches: settlement 2, fields 7 of all sixteen, §0 "Catalog strings, not fields" ("and 2 others"), appendix-h1 §3.3 (needs a key — none exists), A12/A21 (same join), P0 A1·6 meta row.
- **ghost-infeasible** (buildable with a stated change) — **settlement 2 / A1·6 inherited row — "initials fallback" in the avatar circle** — claim: the theme derives initials from the author's name. Evidence: no substring/first-letter helper exists in Ghost (helper audit, research-ghost-binding-contexts.md line 822; `{{split}}` ≥ 6.5 yields whole words, appendix-b1 §6). Verdict: buildable with a stated change — a CSS `::first-letter` over the name in an `overflow: hidden` 24 px circle gives one letter, never two initials; or a generic glyph. Reaches: settlement 2, §0 "Derived, never stored: the initials", finding 6 (initials token), A1·6 component (inherited defect), A12, A21.
- **buildable with a stated change** — **Post block Meta "Author, updated date and reading time" (D33) — "reads `post.updated_at` and draws it only when it is more than a day after publication"** — claim: a day-gap threshold. Evidence: Handlebars cannot subtract dates; `{{#match}}` compares strings/numbers and accepts sub-expressions (appendix-b1 §9 "Sub-expression: yes"). Verdict: buildable as **calendar-day inequality** — `{{#match (date updated_at format="YYYY-MM-DD") "!=" (date published_at format="YYYY-MM-DD")}}` — not "more than a day"; the spec's threshold must be restated as "on a different calendar day". **Verification gap:** the brief expects `research-ghost-empty-values.md` to settle equality when never updated — that file has **no `updated_at` entry** (grep: zero hits), so nothing on record says whether a never-edited post has `updated_at == published_at`, or what a **backdated** `published_at` does (then `updated_at` > `published_at` on a post nobody revised → a false "Updated" line). NE-A24-2. Reaches: Post block Meta row, 11 Dateline `publishedLabel` default, 12 Rail's third line, finding 8, Reconciliation note "The updated line", A26·14 Ledger, D33, catalog `post.updated_on` (exists — "Updated {date}", appendix-h1 line 122 — the spec does not cite it).
- **buildable with a stated change** — **shared field list `post.reading_time` (integer) + authored `readingTimeSuffix` "min read"** — claim: an integer field the theme suffixes. Evidence: `reading_time` is a **helper**, not a field (appendix-b1 §4.1 `{{reading_time}}`; Appendix B line 907 lists it beside fields — a PRD imprecision); its output is a formatted string with `minute=`/`minutes=` format options. Verdict: buildable as `{{reading_time minute="1" minutes="%"}}` for a bare numeral (NE-A24-4 confirms `%` alone renders), and the words then belong to the catalog (`post.reading_time` "{minutes} min read" already exists, appendix-h1 line 119) — see §2 on D10. **Carry-forward NE (A32 Meter):** `{{reading_time}}` on a paid post served to a non-member may be computed on the **preview**, not the full post — every A24 Meta value that draws it inherits that misreport. Reaches: field list row, all sixteen field 5, 11 Dateline cell, 15 Slim "min", A25·8, Appendix B line 907, carry-forward "Verifies before build".
- **buildable with a stated change** — **A24·14 field 5/7 — `post.url` "the share destination", `post.title` "sent unshortened"** — claim: two fields. Evidence: appendix-b1 §4.2 "Always bind `{{url}}` as the helper inside an open context — never `{{post.url}}`"; share intents need an **absolute** URL (`{{url absolute="true"}}`) and URL-encoding (`{{encode}}` exists — research-ghost-binding-contexts.md line 822). Verdict: buildable; the spec must name the helper forms and **the per-destination URL template** (X, Facebook, LinkedIn, Bluesky `bsky.app/intent/compose?text=`, Mastodon `https://{instance}/share?text=`, Threads, WhatsApp `wa.me/?text=`, Reddit `/submit?url=&title=`, Email `mailto:?subject=&body=`) — none is written anywhere. Reaches: A24·14 fields 5/7/9, §0 field list rows `post.url`, Reconciled paragraph, NE-A24-5.
- **buildable with a stated change** — **A24·13 Sticky — "the 56 px condensed bar is `position: sticky`, needs no module, and renders and works" with JavaScript off** — claim: CSS sticky alone holds the bar at the viewport top once the resting title has scrolled away. Evidence: a sticky element is confined to its **containing block**; field 10 puts the bar "at the header's end in the DOM" — inside the `<header>` section root, which ends where the bar begins, so the bar can never hold over the article; §7.3 (canvas geometry) and FR-G7(5) "`position: sticky` for sticky rails" both assume a rail whose parent spans the scroll range. The registry's `reading-progress` line covers only the meter ("The bar is hidden entirely (it is decorative)", §7 line 562; §3 line 134 describes an IO meter). Verdict: buildable with a stated change — the condensed bar is **module-revealed** (threshold + `position: fixed`, or sticky inside a wrapper that spans the article — which AD-3's section-root containment does not give a section), owned by `header-scroll` (sticky/shrink, §2.1 row 2) or by `reading-progress` gaining the bar; and its no-JS state is **hidden**, which reverses field 9's "mapping". Reaches: A24·13 fields 3/4/8/9/10, roster module column, registry §2.1 rows 2/21 and §7 row `reading-progress`, A25 settlement 4 (`scroll-margin-top: 96px` "the same 96 that 7 Sticky Index holds its column at" — assumes this bar), FR-G7(3) restatement rule.
- **buildable with a stated change** — **A24·5 Full Bleed field 10 — picture as a CSS background plus a visually-hidden `<img>` carrying the alt** — claim: background-image is acceptable. Evidence: §7.3 "five constructs… 4. `srcset`/`sizes` — NFR-2 asserts correct `srcset` on every image in CI"; §7.4 normative `image_sizes` map with "compile asserts that every `size=` argument… exists"; FR-H8 "media guards must enclose any `srcset`". A background carries no `srcset`, and the hidden `<img>` loads the same bytes twice. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — one `<img>` with `object-fit: cover` and Image focus as `object-position`, the scrim as an overlay. Reaches: A24·5 fields 9/10, Reconciled (Image focus), NFR-2, §7.4 `image_sizes`.
- **buildable with a stated change** — **A24·14 Reconciled — "The Mastodon instance becomes a site setting, editable, defaulting to `mastodon.social`"** — claim: an editable site setting. Evidence: FR-Q2/Q3 — a Ghost custom setting of type `text` costs 1 of 17 slots and is editable in Ghost Admin; an Inflozo project-level setting costs 0 and is editable only in Inflozo; the spec says "editable" and not where. Verdict: buildable either way; the slot count depends on the ruling (§4). Reaches: §0 "Two values… set once for the site", A24·14, finding 12, D15, FR-Q2 cap meter.
- **consistent** — **field 7 of all sixteen — "three at All tags, in Ghost's order… no counter"** — `{{#foreach tags limit="3"}}` (appendix-b1 §4.1 loop attrs; FR-H5 shim covers `{{#foreach}}`); internal `#tags` are hidden by the loop's public default (§4.1 table row `tags`), and `{{#primary_tag}}` is null when every tag is internal, which removes the eyebrow exactly as designed. Useful because the spec never names the helper.
- **consistent** — **`@page.show_title_and_feature_image` guard on page targets** — §7.3 missing-construct #10 names the compile-target-conditional wrapper for A24 "normative for all 16 designs"; appendix-b1 §3b: `@page` is **not set on list templates** and is only meaningful on `page`; A24 declares `post.hbs`/`page.hbs` only, so the undefined-on-list case never fires unless a future compile target adds a `custom-{name}` **route** template (§3 custom-route row — `@page` set only when the route resolves a real page). Consistent; the wording of what the guard wraps is not — §2.
- **consistent** — **dates via `{{date}}`** — `<time datetime="{{date published_at format="YYYY-MM-DD"}}">{{date published_at format="D MMMM YYYY"}}</time>` (pattern at research-ghost-empty-values.md lines 347–348), site timezone and `@site.locale`; D13 honoured — no client-side date anywhere in A24, `local-date` never needed.

#### 2 · Contradictions
- **stale-design** — **§0 shared floor "A page can switch the whole section off" + every design's field 7 "on a page with 'Show title and feature image' off, the section does not render" + finding 11** — vs inventory line 495 (normative): "every A24 design wraps its **title and feature-image markup — and nothing else** — in `{{#if @page.show_title_and_feature_image}}`", and Synthesis Defaults `page.hbs` row (inventory line 715): meta hidden by control value, "Title and feature image are wrapped". With the toggle off a page's tag line and standfirst (pages carry tags and a custom excerpt) still render; the spec says nothing renders. The controls prompt seeded the wrong sentence (control-prompts.txt A24 §Category-wide 2: "state that the whole section does not render (Ghost's semantics)") — Ghost has no such semantics; the theme decides what the guard wraps. Reaches: §0 floor, fields 7 ×16, finding 11, control-prompts A24 item 2, §7.3 construct #10, FR-I1.
- **stale-design** — **§0 shared floor "The standfirst. `custom_excerpt` falling back to the generated excerpt" + field list row `post.custom_excerpt` "falls back to the generated excerpt" + Post block Standfirst "From the excerpt"** — vs prd.md Appendix B line 905: "a design that **frames** the excerpt — as a pull-quote, **a standfirst**, a card blurb — must bind `custom_excerpt` only and use FR-H8's empty state when it is absent", and **D30** "framed excerpts stay custom-only". A24's standfirst is framed by name. Reaches: §0 floor, field list, Post block, designs 1–9, 12, 14, 16 field 5/8, FR-H8, D30.
- **stale-design** — **§0 "Seven authored, eleven read… every authored field is a label" (`readingTimeSuffix`, `bylinePrefix`, `filedLabel`, `publishedLabel`, `readingTimeLabel`, `shareLabel`, `copiedLabel`)** — vs **D10**: "mechanical/chrome strings go to the FR-Q6 translation catalog; claim-like lines become editable fields with defaults". All seven are mechanical chrome, and the catalog already carries five of them — `post.reading_time` "{minutes} min read", `post.by` "By {author}", `post.updated_on`, `post.share` "Share", `post.link_copied` (appendix-h1 §3.3 lines 119–127). The spec's justification in A25 §0 ("A24 owns the authored `readingTimeSuffix`; two sections authoring the same words on one page would disagree") is the D10 argument for a catalog key, not against it. Reaches: §0 field list, 11 Dateline field 5/Reconciled, 12 Rail, 14 Share Row, 15 Slim, Reconciliation note "11 Dateline's cell labels", appendix-h1 §3.3, FR-Q6, A25 §0 floor "Editing".
- **stale-design** — **scale labels borrowed by non-spacing ladders** — 4 Image Top "Gap to the words Compact 32 · Comfortable 40 · Spacious 56", 6 Edge to Edge "Gap to the picture" (same), 16 Two Column "Column gap Compact 48 · Comfortable 72 · Spacious 96", 5 "Height Compact · Comfortable · Spacious", 8 "Band height", 9 "Picture height", 13 "Bar height", 7 "Card padding" — vs **D26** (gap names settle on Tight/Even/Airy library-wide), Appendix C "Scale vocabularies are closed and distinct… no surface… borrows another scale's labels" (prd.md line 943), inventory line 21 ("never the per-section Vertical spacing labels"), and **D7** ("rename genuinely different ladders"). A24 kept the universal's three words on eight ladders it explicitly calls "genuinely different". Reaches: fields 6 of 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 13, 16; roster; Appendix C scale table; D7; D26.
- **stale-design** — **universal Background role drawn as Background · Surface · Contrast (7 Card "offers Background · Surface only", 8 "locked to Contrast", 5 "locked to Image", 2 "three values drawn")** — vs inventory line 21: Background role is the Swatch Row **Base / Surface / Accent / Contrast / Image**. The spec renames Base and drops Accent from a universal control it does not own, and 7 Card refuses one value while 8 greys Top divider at Compact — D7 permits **locking** the role where the ground is the design, not narrowing its value set or disabling another universal. Reaches: §4 note "Two universal controls disabled by other values", 2/5/7/8/9/10/12/13/15 Reconciled, inventory 21, Appendix C, FR-F3.
- **stale-design** — **D15 — "ONE site-wide ordered share-destinations list (A24/A25 currently disagree)"** — A24·14 reads it; **A25 no longer does** (A25 native-share pass, 25 Aug: `<a href="#/share">`, "A24·14's setting… is not read here"); A26·9 still reads it. The brief asks whether they now agree: **they do not**, and the disagreement is now between a ruling and a Ghost fact (Portal's `share` modal — A25.md §1). Flagged, not resolved — the owner re-rules; whichever way, A24·14 follows. Reaches: D15, A24·14, §0 Repeating items, finding 12, A25 §0/finding 9, A26·9.
- **stale-design** — **A24·13 field 9 "No-JS, quoted from the registry… Mapped to this design"** — FR-G7(3) requires the registry's sentence **restated**; the spec restates it and then reinterprets "the bar" as the meter's track so the condensed bar can be claimed to work without JS. The reinterpretation is what §1 finds false. Reaches: A24·13 field 9, registry §7 row `reading-progress`.
- **stale-design** — **A24·1 field 7 "On a page with no author, Meta resolves to Date only"** — vs A24·11 field 8 "a post with no author — which Ghost does not permit" (appendix-b1 §4.2: `primary_author` always present). Internal contradiction; the Date-only fallback is unreachable. Reaches: A24·1 field 7.
- **stale-design** — **§0 roster note "Control counts… the Post block's seven, none of which is counted"** — vs FR-F3: the ≈15 cap "governs a single design's **visible** controls". The seven block rows are visible Named Selects/Segmented controls in the sidebar. Correct total: 6 own + 7 block = 13 (+3 universal) — still under the cap, so the consequence is the accounting, not the ceiling. Reaches: roster Ctl column, Reconciliation note "Control counts".

#### 4 · Architecture asks
- **Share-destinations site setting** — one ordered, enabled list of ten + a Mastodon instance, read by A24·14, A26·9 (and A25 until its native-share pass). Ghost custom settings cannot hold a list (FR-Q2's five types); the instance alone could be `@custom` (1 slot) — owner: **no owner; needs one** (FR-D5's site-wide group is the nearest home; D15 must be re-ruled against A25's Portal finding first).
- **Route-awareness for the A1·4 Overlay precondition** (5 Full Bleed, 9 Overlap "Pair with A1·4 Overlay"; finding 5 "the picker should carry section-to-section dependencies") — carry-forward "one mechanism, four consumers" — owner: register **45(d)** covers the sticky-overlay contrast case and "A1's hero probe is resolved server-side"; the picker dependency has no FR — **no owner; needs one**.
- **Sticky condensed bar** — module ownership (`header-scroll` vs `reading-progress`), threshold, no-JS = hidden — owner: registry §2.1 rows 2/21, research §7; ruling owed (§1).
- **Triple-stash for one Ghost-owned HTML field** (`feature_image_caption`) — owner: §7.3 mechanic 3 / AD-4 / FR-J17 gate; AD-36 on the sink — ruling owed (§1).
- **D33's threshold** — calendar-day inequality via `{{#match}}` (§1); finding 8's "Ghost needs a real revision flag" is a platform ask — owner: Appendix G deferred list; **no owner** today.
- **Universal-control narrowing** — 7 refuses Contrast, 8 greys Top divider at Compact, 5 inert Vertical spacing, the three-value Background role — owner: FR-F3 / Appendix C / inventory 21; D7 covers locking only — **no owner; needs one**.
- **Pack-token asks** — findings 1–3 (title tracking/leading per heading font; dark weight step above 72 px; eleven packs with no recorded heading font), finding 6 (initials fill token), A24·5's dark scrim `#090806` "outside the seven roles" — owner: FR-E1 / AD-30; join the carry-forward pack-token list (on-accent, tabular figures, floating-overlay step…) — **no owner named there either**.
- **Picker warning before placing a header on a page** (finding 11) — editor feature; **no owner** (FR-D12 is the picker; no FR for per-template placement advice).
- **Series primitive** (finding 4) — owner: A20 Tag Collections + Routes Manager (FR-I2); recorded.
- **Image focus** as `data-image-focus` on the section root → `object-position` — owner: **AD-3** ✓ (one attribute, one value); consistent. Its placement in the Post block rather than an Image Picker popover (ground rule 10) is an owner flag (§6).
- **Registry deltas** — `share` "(3 designs, 27 reach)" and `reading-progress` "(2, 16)" no longer match: A24 declares each once — owner: research-section-js-libraries.md §2.1 rows 21, 23; merge.

#### 5 · Spec completeness
- **Ten fields:** every design carries 1 Descriptor · 2 Structural descriptor · 3 Archetype · 4 Responsive rule · 5 Content fields · 6 Controls · 7 Data · 8 Empty state · 9 Behaviour module · 10 Accessibility, plus Repeating items, Reconciled and Flagged ✓ (16/16).
- **Tuples:** six slots on all sixteen; first five closed-vocabulary — archetypes used: stack ×6, split ×3, media frame ×4, table, edge rail, sticky, bar ✓; containment none/card ✓; ground page/image/surface/contrast ✓; count one/none/few ✓; media bottom/none/right/top/full-bleed/edge/left/background ✓. **Unique:** all sixteen distinct on the first five (verified pairwise; `tuple-check-specs.txt` line 24 "A24: disk 16 · tuples 16; OK"). **First-five collisions: none. Off-vocabulary words: none.**
- **Modules:** 13 `reading-progress` — registry line quoted, then reinterpreted (§2); 14 `share` — registry line quoted verbatim and re-based on the setting ✓. Refused modules each name a home ✓.
- **Lists:** authored — none in-section ✓; Ghost-bound `tags[]`/`authors[]` — no Add/Remove/reorder ✓, no P0·3 Ghost-list card ✗ (§3). The site-wide setting uses P0·3 ✓ (subject to D15).
- **Missing:** FR-G3 declarations and `{{#post}}`; [Free]; per-target defaults; `srcset`/`sizes`; share URL templates; the Post block's cap accounting; the unreachable "page with no author" fallback (§2).

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **ghost-infeasible** (buildable with a stated change) — **§0 settlement 3 / floor "Sharing is Ghost's" / designs 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9 — every share affordance is `<a href="#/share">`** — claim: "Ghost ships a native share modal, triggered by a link to `#/share` on any post or page". Evidence: the only share surface on record is **Portal's** — `research-ghost-membership-pages.md` §4 line 379: `data-portal` value `share` → "Share modal", enumerated from `apps/portal/src/app.jsx:1044-1175` at Ghost 6.58.0-rc.0, and line 846: values beyond the four documented ones (`share` among them) are "**working but undocumented**… re-verified against Portal on each Ghost minor". Portal's hash routes are `#/portal/{path}`; `#/share` is not a Portal path and is parsed by nothing. Verdict: buildable with a stated change — `<a href="#/portal/share">` (or `data-portal="share"`), and the spec must stop calling it a theme-independent "native share" — it is **Portal**, so register 45(c) applies (Portal fragments do nothing with JS off) and FR-Q6's scope limit applies (its strings are Ghost's). Reaches: §0 settlement 3, floor "Sharing is Ghost's", 1/3/4/7/8/9 fields 5–10, components "Share mark", "Share row", "On-band share mark", "Native-share pass" section, finding 9, Appendix B line 913 Portal-action list (omits `share`), FR-F6 Link Picker portal actions, appendix-b1 §7 (Portal), register 45(c).

Nothing on record describes the modal's contents, whether Portal is injected when members are disabled (Portal is `{{ghost_head}}`'s script — appendix-b1 §7), or whether `share` exists on 5.130.6 (the research was read at 6.58.0-rc.0). Inventory 519 covers only the *treatment* surviving removal (FR-Q9), not the body. **No owner; needs one** (FR-I1 compile validation / FR-D5 singleton rule). #### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **consistent (the ruling the orchestrator asked for)** — **Is `{{#get "posts" filter="tags:[{{primary_tag.slug}}]+id:-{{id}}"}}` legal under FR-H5/FR-G3's "template-level context only"?** — **Yes.** Evidence, exactly: `appendix-b1-template-contexts.md` §5, table rows 2–3 — *"Related posts by primary tag | `{{#get "posts" filter="primary_tag:{{primary_tag.slug}}"}}`"* and *"More by this author | `{{#get "posts" filter="authors:{{primary_author.slug}}+id:-{{id}}"}}`"* — are §5's own canonical queries, and they read the current post's fields; `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` §6 lines 399–404 places both **inside `{{#post}}`** on `post.hbs` (Ghost's docs pattern); appendix-b1 §3 row `post` makes the post the template's own resource ("`post` (object)" at top level, full scope inside `{{#post}}` per §4.2). Ghost resolves the mustaches in a `filter` string against the current context *before* the query runs, which is why the post's fields work and why the constraint exists at all: the "render context" FR-H5 forbids is a **loop item** (a post inside `{{#foreach posts}}`) or **the result of an enclosing `{{#get}}`** (inside a `{{#get}}` block, `this` is the query result — appendix-b1 §5 block-params note), neither of which the canvas shim can resolve synchronously. So the related-posts filter is legal on two conditions: (i) the `{{#get}}` sits directly inside `{{#post}}` (or at the top level with the `post.` prefix — `{{post.primary_tag.slug}}`, since bare `{{primary_tag.slug}}` is empty at the root, §3a), never inside a `{{#foreach}}` or another `{{#get}}`; (ii) the mustaches are raw paths (§5: "Helpers do not execute inside `filter` strings"). Reaches: A27 §0 settlement 1, all twelve `Data` fields, FR-H5 line 324/328, FR-G3 line 277, Appendix B line 920 — the PRD sentence should say this (see PRD amendments).
- **ghost-infeasible** — **Same tag compiles to `tags:[{{#foreach tags}}{{slug}},{{/foreach}}]+id:-{{id}}`; Same author swaps in `authors:[…]` the same way** (§0 settlement 1, line 59) — claim: a block helper builds the filter's tag list — evidence: appendix-b1 §5 "Helpers do not execute inside `filter` strings — pass raw attributes"; Ghost's filter resolver substitutes `{{path}}` tokens by path lookup, so `{{#foreach tags}}` is not a path and `{{slug}}` resolves to the **post's** slug — verdict: **not buildable as written; buildable with a stated change**: the canonical `primary_tag:{{primary_tag.slug}}` (matches the primary tag only — the spec's "any of the current post's tags" promise narrows), or Ghost's documented any-tag form via the `post.tags` path alias at the top level of post.hbs (`tags:[{{post.tags}}]`, which the resolver expands to the slug list) — **NE-A27-1** settles which forms resolve on T1/T3 and what "any tag" costs. Same author: `primary_author:{{primary_author.slug}}` (FR-I2's own mapping) or `authors:[{{post.authors}}]` if the alias exists. Reaches: settlement 1, every `Data` field, finding 2, FR-H2.
- **needs-execution** — **`whenEmpty: Show latest posts` — the fallback chain** — claim: an empty related set falls back to a latest-posts query under `fallbackHeading` — evidence: `{{#get}}`'s `{{else}}` fires only on error (appendix-b1 §5); emptiness is tested inside the block (`{{#if posts}}` — an empty array is falsy, `research-ghost-empty-values.md` §2.2 line 473), so the fallback `{{#get "posts" filter="id:-{{id}}"}}` must sit **inside the first get's block**, where `this` is the first query's result and `{{id}}` no longer names the post — the exact render-context case FR-H5 forbids; §7.3 item 3 already names "A27's by primary tag **with fallback to latest**" as a missing two-armed construct — verdict: **needs execution** (NE-A27-2): whether `{{id}}` or `@root.post.id` resolves inside an enclosing `{{#get}}`, and whether Ghost's resolver reaches `@root` at all. Until then the value is not buildable; the **default (Hide) is**: `{{#get …}}{{#if posts}}<section>…</section>{{/if}}{{/get}}` wraps head, plane, band and rail. Reaches: §0 settlement 4, Data group `whenEmpty`, field list `fallbackHeading`, 1–12 `Data`, §7.3 item 3, FR-H2 (carry-forward "adopt A19's fifth field `fallback` library-wide"), FR-H4 rule 2.

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **ghost-infeasible** — **all ten · the count** — claim (spec §0 settlement 1, §9, §8, every "No-JS" line): `{{comment_count singular=… plural=… empty=…}}` "renders whether or not the block does" and "the frame is unchanged" with JS off; 9 Big Count's `h2` *is* the figure; 8 Prompt shows a signed-out reader "the count of the discussion they cannot see" — evidence: `frontend/helpers/comment_count.js` returns **only** `<script data-ghost-comment-count="{{id}}" data-ghost-comment-count-empty/-singular/-plural/-tag/-class-name/-autowrap>` — no number is server-rendered; the number is fetched client-side by `public/comment-counts.min.js` (injected by `ghost_head.js:366-367` only when `comments_enabled !== 'off'`) from `/members/api/comments/counts/?ids=…`, which then inserts a `<span>` (or the `autowrap` tag) after the placeholder and removes it — verdict: **buildable with a stated change**: (a) with JS off **no design has a count** — 1–10's "frame unchanged" lines are wrong for the count line, 9 Big Count's whole head is absent, 7's bar carries no count, 8's signed-out prompt has no count; the `<noscript>` line is the only honest text; (b) 9's `<section aria-labelledby>` names an element whose text arrives client-side — with JS off the accessible name is empty, so the section must carry `aria-label` (catalog `comments.heading`) as the fallback in every design, not only at Heading None; (c) the theme styles the *injected* span via the `class=` hash (`data-ghost-comment-count-class-name`), which the spec never names; (d) "the comma is the helper's" (9, four digits) is false — the script inserts the raw integer (`${e}`); (e) 9's bare figure is reachable (`singular="" plural=""` → bare number; `empty="0"` for At zero: Figure), and (f) with commenting **off** the counts script is not injected at all, so any closed-state head that keeps its count shows nothing — 9 says "no figure" ✓, 1–8/10 do not say. Reaches: spec §0 settlements 1–2, shared floor "No JavaScript", "Behaviour", every design's No-JS and Accessibility lines, §9 Data/Accessibility, finding 3; FR-G4; `research-section-js-libraries.md` §7 (no registry line covers a Ghost-injected count); FR-H3(2) ("the count header has a real number" is a canvas fact only). Probe under NE-A28-2.
- **prd-defect** — **all ten · the count's three words** — claim (spec field list, Reconciliation notes): `countSingular` "comment" / `countPlural` "comments" / `countEmpty` "No comments yet" are authored fields passed bare — evidence: `comment-counts.min.js` composes `` `${count} ${singular}` `` / `` `${count} ${plural}` `` and shows `empty` verbatim at 0 — there is **no `%` substitution** in `{{comment_count}}`; `appendix-h1-string-catalog.md` §3.9 lines 257-259 assert the opposite ("`comments.count_one` / `count_many` use `%` … because Ghost's `{{plural}}`/`{{comment_count}}` helpers substitute `%` themselves") and ship defaults `% comment` / `% comments`, which would render **"1 % comment"** — verdict: the **catalog line is the defect** (only `{{plural}}` substitutes `%`); the spec's bare-word form is right. Reaches: appendix-h1 §3.9 (keys `comments.count_one`, `comments.count_many` — S2 default revision, not a new key), the compiler's `{{comment_count … singular=(t "comments.count_one")}}` emission rule, spec field list. See also Contradictions (D10) for *where* the words live.
- **needs-execution** — **8 Prompt · free member under paid-only commenting** (carry-forward "Verifies before build" · finding 5 · ARCHITECT: verify on the frame) — claim: what Ghost renders inside the block to a signed-in free member when commenting is Paid-members only is undocumented — evidence: `frontend/helpers/comments.js` **does not decide it**: the helper returns nothing only when `comments_enabled === 'off'` or `!this.access`; on a public post it emits the script with `data-comments-enabled="paid"` and `comments-ui` (jsdelivr, `MEASUREMENTS.md §15c`) decides client-side, which no companion has read — verdict: **needs execution** (NE-A28-1); it blocks 8 Prompt and decides whether the other nine need 8's arrangement (the spec says so itself). What *is* settled from source: 8's server-side branch is `{{#if @member}}{{#unless @member.paid}}{{#match @site.comments_access "paid"}}` (`@site.comments_access` carries the raw `all`/`paid`/`off`, `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` line 178; appendix-b1 §6 "not gated"; `@member.paid` = `status !== 'free'`, `update-local-template-options.js:38`) — the spec names none of these bindings (spec-incomplete, §3 below). Reaches: spec §8 Data, finding 5, proof frame; §7.3 missing-construct #4; register (new row).
- **ghost-infeasible** — **4 Contrast Band · `mode` computed from the band** — claim (§4 Data): `mode="dark"` in a light pack, `mode="light"` in a dark one, "a band that inverts the page cannot follow the reader's system" — evidence: `comments.js` reads `options.hash.mode` once, server-side, into `data-color-scheme`; on a project whose FR-Q5 `color_scheme` is **Auto** (FR-E4: `prefers-color-scheme` in pure CSS) the band itself flips per visitor, but the literal cannot — verdict: **buildable with a stated change**: on Auto sites 4 renders the thread in the wrong scheme for one of the two audiences; either 4 is offered only when `@custom.color_scheme` is pinned Light/Dark (compile `{{#match @custom.color_scheme "Dark"}}mode="light"{{else}}mode="dark"{{/match}}`), or the mismatch is stated on the frame. Reaches: spec §4 Data/Reconciled, Data group `blockMode` "forced in 4", AD-30 (a second place selects on mode), FR-Q5, FR-E4.
- **stale-design** — **all ten · "Match the page resolves to `auto` on a dual-mode site"** — claim (§0 "The block's mode", Reconciliation notes): `auto` when the site ships both modes, the pack's mode when it ships one — evidence: FR-Q5 — **every** project compiles `color_scheme` (Auto/Light/Dark) and a site owner may pin Dark in Ghost Admin after deploy; `comments.js` accepts only `dark`/`light`, anything else → `auto` — verdict: **buildable with a stated change**: "Match the page" must read the built-in — `auto` only at Auto, `mode="dark"`/`"light"` when pinned — otherwise a pinned-Dark site with a light-system visitor gets a light thread, the exact defect the withdrawal fixed. Reaches: spec §0 Data group `blockMode`, Reconciliation notes bullet 1, AD-30, FR-Q5.
- **spec-incomplete** — **all ten · `{{#if comments}}` as the closed test** — claim (Data group `whenClosed`, every Empty state): `{{#if comments}}` false → the notice "Comments are closed on this post." or Hide — evidence: `server/api/endpoints/utils/serializers/output/mappers/posts.js:94-101` sets `comments = access && comments_enabled !== 'off'`; it is therefore also **false for a free member (or signed-out reader) on a members/paid post** — verdict: **buildable with a stated change**: on a gated post the notice says "closed" to a reader who merely lacks access, beside A32's paywall; the closed branch must be `{{#unless @site.comments_enabled}}` (the theme-facing boolean, `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` line 178) and the `access:false` case must render **nothing** (the paywall owns that route). Reaches: spec Data group, every design's Empty state, `closedNotice`, A32 (adjacent), FR-H8.
- **needs-execution** — **all ten · `{{comments title="" count=false}}`** — claim (settlement 1): the block's own title and count are switched off — evidence: `comments.js` — `count=false` (a Handlebars boolean literal) is honoured (`options.hash.count === false`); `title=""` is a string and is passed as `data-title=""` — the helper comment says `null` is what lets comments-ui "handle the default title", so whether `""` suppresses the heading or falls back to the default is comments-ui's call — verdict: needs execution (NE-A28-3). Reaches: settlement 1, every Data line.
- **consistent** — `mode` (`dark`|`light`, else `auto`) and `saturation` (int, default 60 → Muted 40 · Standard 60 · Vivid 80) are exactly the two attributes the spec claims (`comments.js`; Ghost docs https://ghost.org/docs/themes/helpers/comments/ list title/count/mode/saturation); `{{comments}}` returns nothing without `this.comment_id`, i.e. must sit inside `{{#post}}` on a post — consistent with `compileTarget: post.hbs` only (FR-G3, appendix-b1 §4.2), though the spec never states its compileTarget/bindingContext (§3).
- **consistent** — **finding 1 / D17** — `comments.js` sets `data-accent-color` from `options.data.site.accent_color` — Ghost's site setting, never `@custom`; FR-Q3's accent promotion therefore cannot reach the thread. The spec's ask ("write the pack's accent into Ghost's accent setting at deploy") is an **Admin settings write outside AD-10's four-item write allowlist** — see §4.
- **consistent** — **finding 2 / §7.6 item 15** — theme CSS cannot reach inside: `{{comments}}` emits exactly one `<script>` and no DOM (`MEASUREMENTS.md §15c`, register 15 CLOSED 2026-08-20). `prd.md` line 703 and FR-H3(2) still describe item 15 as open → PRD amendment.
- **needs-execution** — **8 Prompt · `member-form` no-JS line** — claim (§8, quoting registry §7): "The `<form>` posts natively to Ghost's members endpoint; Ghost's own server response replaces the designed sent state" — evidence: `server/web/members/app.js:81-92` mounts `POST /api/send-magic-link` behind `bodyParser.json()` **only** and `verifyIntegrityToken` (`middleware.js:200-222`, throws when `verifyRequestIntegrity` is set); a native `<form>` submits `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` with no `integrityToken`, so `req.body.email` is undefined and the likely "server response" is a **400 text error**, not a sent state — verdict: needs execution (NE-A28-4); if confirmed, the registry sentence every `member-form` design quotes is false and A28-8's "the one A28 design that still does its job" with it. Reaches: research-section-js-libraries.md §7 `member-form`, FR-G7(3), A30 ×13, A16, A22, A31-10.
- **arch-gap** — **8 Prompt · upgrade state** — claim (§8 Behaviour): "none in the upgrade state, which is a link to Portal … with JavaScript off this is the one A28 design that still does its job" — evidence: register 45(c): `#/portal/…` / `data-portal` do nothing with JS off — verdict: the upgrade state does **not** do its job with JS off; the spec must say so (never invent a fallback). Reaches: spec §8 Behaviour/Flagged, register 45(c).

#### 2 · Contradictions
- **stale-design** — **inventory line 566-577 vs the export** — the inventory's ten names, its `Controls:` line (count header toggle · header size Normal/Display · width Match content measure/Full width · signed-out note toggle) and its `[Free]` pair (#1 Card Panel, #2 Minimal Thread) describe designs that do not exist in the export; the spec carries **no** `[Free]` marker at all. D11 accepted an export-over-inventory model for A31 and said the merge re-derives; no such ruling exists for A28. Reaches: inventory A28 entry, FR-G2 (first two = #1 Rule, #2 Split Head unless the owner re-tiers), Synthesis Defaults post.hbs row 5.
- **prd-defect (Synthesis Defaults) / stale-design** — **Synthesis Defaults §3 post.hbs row 5** picks "A28 #2 Minimal Thread — bare native output renders nothing when comments are disabled, no orphaned panel chrome" (inventory lines 705-709, FR-H4(2) repeats the reasoning). The export's #2 is **Split Head** — a 320 px column of head + rules beside the block, whose Data group default is `whenClosed: Show the notice` (Hide is only 10 Slim's default). An untouched project on a site with comments off would therefore synthesize a "Comments are closed on this post." column into every post. Either the synthesized instance is emitted with `whenClosed: Hide` and House rules Off, or the default maps to the export's genuinely bare design (10 Slim — which is not [Free]). Owner rules (§6). Reaches: inventory lines 705-709, FR-H4(2), FR-D6, spec §2 Data group defaults.
- **stale-design** — **settlement 3 "A28 sits below A26 and above A27"** vs the Synthesis Defaults' post.hbs stack (A24 · A25 · A26 · A27 · **A28 last**, inventory lines 703-709). Every A28 frame draws A27 *below* it; the synthesized template puts A27 above it. One order must win. Reaches: spec settlement 3, every frame's context strips, inventory line 709, A27 spec.
- **D10 / FR-Q6** — **the count's three words** are authored fields "edited in the panel", with the spec's reason being that "a non-English site could not change them" — that is exactly what the Translations surface (FR-Q6) does for catalog keys, and the catalog already holds `comments.count_none/one/many` (appendix-h1 §3.9). D10: mechanical strings go to the catalog. The spec's fields orphan three catalog keys and create a per-section copy of a site-wide string. Reaches: spec field list (`countSingular/Plural/Empty`), Reconciliation notes bullet 3, appendix-h1 §3.9 (fix the `%` first — §1 above).
- **D10 / FR-Q6** — **7 Disclosure `showLabel`/`hideLabel`** ("Show"/"Hide", authored) duplicate catalog keys `comments.show` / `comments.hide` (which also happen to be marked **JS** in appendix-h1 although 7 is native `<details>` with no JS — the catalog's channel mark is wrong for this use). Reaches: spec §7 Content fields, appendix-h1 §3.9 rows `comments.show`, `comments.hide`, `comments.show_count`.
- **FR-G7 / registry §2.2** — **7 Disclosure declares `accordion`**; registry §2.2 ("Things that look like modules and are not") lists A28's toggle-reveal as **zero JS** (`<details>/<summary>`), while §2.1 row 11 lists "A28 #3 Toggle Reveal" under `accordion` — the registry disagrees with itself, and the spec picked the side that ships 0.2 KB for nothing (registry §3.1: `accordion` JS exists "only for single-open groups and A9's default state"; a lone `<details>` with a server-rendered `open` needs none). Reaches: spec §7 Behaviour/roster, research-section-js-libraries.md §2.1 row 11 vs §2.2 row 1, FR-G7(2).
- **register 45(c)** — 8 Prompt's Portal `account/plans` button is described as working with JS off (see §1). Reaches: spec §8.
- **Appendix C / FR-F3** — the universal trio is named **Background · Surface · Contrast** in the spec; Appendix C's Swatch Row roles are **Base / Surface / Accent / Contrast / Image** and the Synthesis Defaults default Background role to **Base**; and 10 Slim locks the row at **Inherit**, a value nowhere in the vocabulary (finding 7). Library-wide naming (D7's wording), plus a genuinely new value. Reaches: spec §0 shared floor, §10, finding 7, Appendix C Swatch Row row, FR-F3, D7.
- **appendix-h1 S1** — `comments.noscript` ("Comments need JavaScript.") is not a catalog key; the spec invents it. `aria-label="Comments"` at Heading None is "a translation-catalog string" with no key named — the catalog's `comments.heading` is it. Reaches: spec shared floor, §1/§10 Accessibility, appendix-h1 §3.9 (append `comments.noscript`).
- **inventory line 567 · `headingText` default** — spec "Discussion" vs catalog `comments.heading` "Comments" (marked prop). One default. Reaches: spec field list, appendix-h1 §3.9.

The spec must state that the canvas shows the fixture at **14** (two digits — what 9's 76/104 px figure and 7's bar were sized for) and whether `blockMode`/`avatarSaturation` are honoured by the fixture (owner: the E4 shim). Reaches: spec §0, FR-H3(2), FR-H5, appendix-h1 `comments.placeholder`.

- **spec-incomplete** — **8 Prompt's server-side branches** are undeclared as bindings: `{{#if @member}}` + `{{#unless @member.paid}}` + `@site.comments_access` — the four-value member conditional is §7.3 missing-construct #4 and the spec should name it. - **spec-incomplete** — `member-form` registry row 17 lists claimants "A30 #1–#10 … A31 #10"; A28-8 is a new claimant. Reaches: research-section-js-libraries.md §2.1 row 17.

#### 4 · Architecture asks
- **D17 — consented seeding of Ghost's accent colour** (finding 1; "architect drafts the FR; confirm at merge") — the seed is `PUT /admin/settings/` on `accent_color`, which is **not** one of AD-10's four permitted Admin writes (theme upload · theme activate · `routes.yaml` upload · consented announcement-bar clear; "the allowlist is a literal in one file with a test asserting its exact membership"). The FR does not exist yet and the write is not in the spine — owner: **AD-10 (must grow a fifth consented write) + the D17 FR — no FR yet; the architect owns the draft, the owner confirms at merge**. Note FR-Q3's promoted accent does not help: `comments.js` reads `@site.accent_color`, not `@custom`.
- **Route awareness** (finding 6; carry-forward "Product mechanisms": A24 Overlay precondition, A26/A27 duplicate-post and stacked padding, A28 spacing — one mechanism, four consumers) — verified: no AD and no register row owns it; A28's 192 px stacked Comfortable padding under A26 is real. **No owner; needs one** (a compile-time "previous sibling category" fact the compiler already has, or a CSS adjacency rule per AD-3's data-attribute mechanism).
- **Background role "Inherit"** (finding 7) — a new value on a universal control (FR-F3 / Appendix C Swatch Row), or A28-10 changes its ground slot. **No owner; needs one** (owner ruling; it recurs for every `transparent` design).
- **Mode selection in two places** — AD-30 says exactly one file selects on mode; `{{comments mode=…}}` is a second, server-side literal selecting on mode (and 4's inversion). Owner: **AD-30** — rule whether `mode=` derives from `@custom.color_scheme` (see §1) and what 4 does on Auto.
- **`member-form`'s no-JS truth** (NE-A28-4) — owner: **FR-G7 §7 / registry (E4)**; every design quoting the sentence inherits the answer.
- **`accordion` vs native `<details>`** on 7 — owner: **registry §2.1/§2.2** (settle the self-contradiction once; the carry-forward already flags `tabs`' no-JS ruling in the same family).
- **Third-party script on the page** — comments-ui from `cdn.jsdelivr.net` and the counts script are outside NFR-2's budget and the theme's CSP (`MEASUREMENTS.md §15c`, register 15) — already recorded on §1.2's carve-out list; **consistent**, no new ask.
- **Canvas shim** — the FR-H5 shim must render the FR-H3 fixture *inside* the A28 section and decide whether `mode`/`saturation` affect it — owner: **FR-H5 (E4)**; the spec does not ask, but the canvas cannot be built without the answer.
- **No new module names** — confirmed: the spec invents none; the "no drawer module" refusal is stated as a finding, not a licence. Consistent with P0·8 rule 4.

#### 5 · Spec completeness
- **Ten fields**: every design 1–10 carries Descriptor · Structural descriptor · Archetype · Responsive rule · Content fields · Controls · Data · Empty state · Behaviour module · Accessibility ✓.
- **Tuples** (first five, closed vocabulary): 1 `stack·none·page·none·none` · 2 `split·none·page·few·none` · 3 `stack·none·surface·none·none` · 4 `stack·none·contrast·none·none` · 5 `stack·box·page·none·none` · 6 `edge rail·none·page·few·none` · 7 `bar·none·page·none·none` · 8 `form·none·page·none·none` · 9 `split·none·page·none·none` · 10 `stack·none·transparent·none·none`. All words in vocabulary; **no first-five collisions** (1 vs 10 differ on ground; 2 vs 9 on count) ✓. Register-46-class note: 1 vs 10 differ **only** by `page` vs `transparent`, and `transparent` is a ground the universal control cannot express (finding 7) — if the owner declines "Inherit", the two collapse to a collision.
- **Modules' no-JS lines**: 7 quotes `accordion` ✓; 8 quotes `member-form` ✓ (sentence itself under NE-A28-4); 8's upgrade state lacks the register-45(c) Portal sentence ✗.
- **Lists**: `rules[]` (2, 6) carries add ("+ Add a rule", arrives "Be kind") / remove (never disabled; last removal → House rules Off) / drag reorder ✓ P0·3; no Ghost-bound list ✓; the thread is correctly refused as an item source ✓.
- **Strings**: `comments.noscript` invented; `comments.heading` unnamed; count words and Show/Hide duplicated as fields (D10, §2).
- **Universal trio**: Vertical spacing / Top divider / Background role outside each list ✓ (D7); px only as spec readings ✓; no slider/hex ✓; ≤ 15 controls (max 6) ✓; Quick Controls 3–5 ✓.
- **P0**: P0·1 ✓ (lock pill on the count; Link disabled in `<summary>` recorded), P0·2 ✓ (8 only), P0·3 ✓, P0·4 ✓ (8, twice), P0·5 correctly absent, P0·6 ✓; P0·8 rule 1 (no Preview) ✓, rule 3 (named values) ✓, rule 4 (no invented modules) ✓.
- **compileTarget / bindingContext / [Free] / fixture**: absent (§3).

#### Needs execution (this category)
- **NE-A28-1** — what comments-ui renders to a **signed-in free member on a public post** when Membership → Commenting is **Paid members** — probe: on T1 (ghost6.inflozo.com 6.58.0) and T3 (ghost5.inflozo.com 5.130.6) set `comments_enabled = paid`, create a free member, sign in, open a public post whose template carries `{{#post}}{{comments}}{{/post}}`; record the rendered UI (CTA text, whether the thread is visible, whether an upgrade button appears and what `data-portal` it uses); repeat signed out; repeat on a members-only post. Expected outputs decide 8 Prompt's `freeMembers` row and whether 1–7, 9, 10 need the prompt.
- **NE-A28-2** — `{{comment_count}}` is client-rendered — probe: view-source of the same post on T1/T3 with `{{comment_count singular="comment" plural="comments" empty="No comments yet" class="c"}}`: expect a `<script data-ghost-comment-count=…>` and no number; load with JS off: expect no count; with JS on: expect `<span class="c">14 comments</span>` and confirm (a) `singular="% comment"` renders a literal `%`, (b) a 4-digit count is unformatted, (c) `singular="" plural=""` yields the bare number and `empty="0"` yields "0", (d) `GET /members/api/comments/counts/?ids={id}` returns a count to a signed-out reader when commenting is paid-only, (e) with commenting **off** no `comment-counts.min.js` is injected.
- **NE-A28-3** — `{{comments title="" count=false}}` — probe: render on T1/T3 and check the block shows **no** heading (vs the default "Member discussion") and **no** count.
- **NE-A28-4** — the registry's `member-form` no-JS sentence — probe: with JS off submit a plain `<form method="post" action="/members/api/send-magic-link/" data-members-form="signup"><input name="email" …>` on T1/T3; record status and body (expected: 400 — `bodyParser.json()` only; and whether `verifyRequestIntegrity` rejects a missing `integrityToken` on either host). Reaches FR-G7 §7 and every `member-form` design.
- **NE-A28-5** — `mode="dark"` on an Auto site — probe: pin nothing (`color_scheme: Auto`), visit with a light system preference: expect a dark thread on a light page (confirms 4's Auto-site defect).
