#### 2 · Contradictions
- **stale-design (owner ruling needed)** — **the product model**: inventory lines 596-610 + prd.md line 230 + FR-G2 describe thirteen **single-surface** designs with an explicit surface partition Shuffle and Site Remix never cross, [Free] = #1 Signup Center Card and #2 Signin Minimal, and a member-home surface "where a Free user may find only Pro options". The export's thirteen each draw **all three routes**, so there is no partition, [Free] would be #1 Centred and #2 Split Pitch (which would in fact close FR-G2's member-home gap), and the emitted file set is three fixed templates rather than one per design. Neither model is unbuildable; the PRD wins on product decisions unless the owner rules as in D11. Reaches: inventory A30 entry, prd.md line 230 (Shuffle partition), FR-G2's A30 sentence, FR-I6 (files per deploy), §7.4 reserved stems, FR-L3 (block-sheet remediations).
- **FR-H6** — no `@site.paid_members_enabled` gate and no `type:paid+visibility:public` filter (see §1); `tiersSource: From Ghost, all` contradicts the mandatory visibility filter.
- **research §10 / inventory #11** — the account page renders **`@member.email` server-side** ("Signed in as …"; the name-slot fallback; 9 Big Type sets the email at 72 px). Research §10(3): under `cacheMembersContent:enabled` member responses are cached **publicly, keyed by tier**, so a server-rendered email is served to other members on the same tier; its recommendation for A30 is "Do not render email or card digits"; inventory #11 scopes Member Home to "greeting, plan badge and status". The spec's choice is a product/security call the owner must make explicitly (§6). Reaches: settlement 3, `rowLabels` "Signed in as", 9 §7, 1 §8, print rule.

## A31 · Error and Utility
**Counts (derived):** designs on disk **10** (11 frames `A31-0`…`A31-10` − the proof) · spec **10** (`## 1`…`## 10`) · inventory **9** (line 612: #1–#7, #9, #10 — no #8) · [Free] spec **0 marked** (no `[Free]` token anywhere in the spec) / inventory **3** (#1, #2, #10) · modules declared: `core` ×10 + `nav-transform` (9 Directory at *Nav children = From Ghost prefixes* — not in the 31; the D2 carry-forward adds it) · custom-setting slots: **0** · authored lists: `links[]` 0–6 (drawn by 1–7, 10; stored by 8, 9) · Ghost-bound lists: `posts` via `{{#get}}` (8), `@site.navigation` / `@site.secondary_navigation` (9).

The export's model (D11, ruled): every design draws all three pages (404 · 500 · gate) from one copy set; "the template decides". That collapses the inventory's per-design `compileTarget` into one declaration for the whole category — every A31 instance compiles `error.hbs` **and** `private.hbs`, `bindingContext` `error` + `private` — and there are no utility custom-page designs left (the inventory's #6 Coming Soon, #7 Maintenance, #9 Subscribe Success have no counterpart in the export; the export's 6/7/9 are Contrast Band, Cover, Directory).

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **prd-defect** — **A31 §0 settlements 1 and 4, every design (the 404 keeps A1's header, nav, search and A3's footer; the 500 keeps nothing and queries nothing)** — claim: one `error.hbs` renders both. — evidence: A1/A3 are `default.hbs` partials (FR-D5, FR-I1); `appendix-b1-template-contexts.md` §3c: "`error.hbs` must be self-contained in Inflozo output: no layout inheritance, no `{{#get}}`" and "`error-404.hbs` may be rich… **Inflozo does not emit it** (FR-I1's file list stops at `error.hbs`)"; inventory line 614 "one `error.hbs` serves 404, 500 and every other status (FR-I1 emits no `error-404.hbs`)". `{{!< default}}` is a file-level directive — a file cannot extend `default.hbs` for one status and not for another. — verdict: **buildable with a stated change**, and the change is the PRD's: either (a) FR-I1 emits Casper's split — `error-404.hbs` (extends `default.hbs`, may run `{{#get}}`; carries the 404 copy set and 8/9's lists) plus a self-contained `error.hbs` (the 500 copy set, and the fallback for every other code) — which is exactly the split §3c already documents and register 13 proved on both majors; or (b) `error.hbs` carries its own `<head>` and includes the header/footer partials inside a `{{#match statusCode 404}}` branch, which makes the 500's "no settings image, no navigation" ceiling a branch condition rather than a file property. The spec's finding 1 calls this "the build's call"; it is not — FR-I1's file list and §3c's rule are PRD text. Reaches: spec §0 (settlements 1, 4), §0 page-source row 1, finding 1; FR-I1; appendix-b1 §3c; inventory 612/614; appendix-h1 §3.5's premise ("`error.hbs` serves every status… both copy sets in one template"); Synthesis Defaults `error.hbs` row (inventory 734–740).
- **needs-execution** — **A31-8 Elsewhere (`{{#get "posts" limit="5" order="published_at desc"}}` on the 404 only), A31-9 Directory (hand-offs)** — claim: an error template may run `{{#get}}` on a 404 and the same file must not on a 500. — evidence: appendix-b1 §3c/§5 ("Permitted by Ghost; §5 forbids it in Inflozo output" for `error.hbs`); register 13 executed `{{#get}}` inside `error-404.hbs` on a real 404 (both majors) but never inside a single `error.hbs`, and never on a 500. Handlebars only executes the taken branch, so a get inside `{{#match statusCode 404}}` never runs on a 500 — but nothing has proved that. — verdict: **needs execution** (NE-A31-1). If the file split above is adopted the question dissolves for 8 and 9 (they compile into `error-404.hbs`); the spec's finding 2 ("if the answer is no, both hand off on all three pages and A31 loses two of ten") stays open until then. Reaches: spec §0, 8 §7, 9 §7, finding 2, note 11; appendix-b1 §3c; carry-forward "Verifies before build".
- **consistent** — **all 10, the chip and the field-list rows *statusCode · message*** — claim: `{{statusCode}}` and `{{message}}` are the error context's names ("Variable names to be verified ⚑"). — evidence: `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` §10 (`{message, statusCode, errorDetails}` set in `frontend/web/middleware/error-handler.js`); appendix-b1 §3 `error` row; register 13 ran `{{statusCode}}` in a real 404 on 5.130.6 and 6.58.0. `{{code}}` is not a context variable — it is only the `{code}` placeholder in `error.code_label`. — verdict: **buildable; the verify is closed** — the spec's finding 1 and note 11 must be struck, not carried. Reaches: spec field list, finding 1, note 11.
- **consistent** — **the 404 header's member state (A31 §0 settlement 1, finding 7)** — claim: whether `@member` reaches `error.hbs`. — evidence: research §10 "`@site`, `@custom`, `@config`, `@member` — Available… the middlewares have already installed [them] onto the render options"; appendix-b1 §2 (`@member` universal). — verdict: **buildable; finding 7 closes by citation.** But the thing it decides is stale — see Contradictions (A1's member pill is withdrawn).
- **consistent** — **A31-9 Directory, *Which navigation = Primary and secondary*** — claim: "whether Ghost exposes a secondary navigation list to an error template" (frame verify, note 11, Flagged). — evidence: `@site.secondary_navigation` is a settings global present on every render (research §3 table line 141: "`secondary_navigation` — yes (indirectly) — `[{Sign up,#/portal/}]`"); the helper reads it by hash param — Ghost 6.44.1 `core/frontend/helpers/navigation.js:24` `const key = options.hash.type === 'secondary' ? 'secondary_navigation' : 'navigation'`; appendix-b1 §2 lists `{{navigation}}` as available everywhere. — verdict: **buildable; the verify is closed by citation.** Reaches: spec 9 §7/Reconciled/Flagged, note 11, frame `A31-9`.
- **spec-incomplete** — **A31-9 Directory §7 "`{{navigation}}` — label and URL only"** — claim: the directory is drawn from the `{{navigation}}` helper. — evidence: `{{navigation}}` emits Ghost's `partials/navigation.hbs` (or the theme's one site-wide override — appendix-b1 §7/§9), the same markup A1's header uses; a two-column page-scale list with 56 px rows is a different rendering of the same data. The per-item fields the design needs (`label`, `url`, `current`) are reachable by `{{#foreach @site.navigation}}` / `{{#foreach @site.secondary_navigation}}` (appendix-b1 §3 `default` row: "`{{#foreach}}` written in this file (e.g. `@site.navigation`)"). — verdict: buildable with a stated change: 9 loops `@site.navigation` (+ `@site.secondary_navigation` at the second value); it must not name the helper, because the helper's output is A1's. "0 items → hand-off" is sound: research line 140 — "user may empty it". Reaches: spec 9 §7, §0 field-list row *navigation*; A1's `partials/navigation.hbs` ownership.
- **ghost-infeasible** — **every design's gate: `<form action="/private/?r={{@path}}" method="post">` (§0 settlement 1; page-source row 4; frames `A31-1`…`A31-10`)** — claim: the form posts to `/private/?r=` with a `@path` variable. — evidence: `@path` is not a Ghost global (appendix-b1 §2 universal set: `@site`, `@member`, `@custom`, `@config` — nothing else; §0: an unknown path renders **empty**, silently). Ghost's own view posts **action-less** to the current URL — Ghost 6.44.1 `core/frontend/apps/private-blogging/lib/views/private.hbs:80` `<form class="gh-signin gh-private-signin gh-private-access-form" method="post" novalidate="novalidate">` — because the gate middleware has already put the return target in the URL: `lib/middleware.js:67-68` `redirectUrl += '?r=' + encodeURIComponent(req.url)` and `:41` `decodeURIComponent(query.r || '/')` on submit, host-validated (research §11). — verdict: **not buildable as written; buildable with the change**: emit the form with **no `action`** (or `action=""`), which preserves `?r=` and lands the visitor where they were going. As drawn, `?r=` is empty and every successful unlock lands on `/`. This also closes the spec's finding 4 ("whether the `?r=` redirect parameter is required" — it is, and the form must not rebuild it). Reaches: spec §0, page-source row 4, finding 4, note 11, all ten frames' gate annotation.
- **consistent** — **the gate's field (`{{input_password}}` with `class` and `placeholder` from `gatePlaceholder`)** — evidence: research §11 (`apps/private-blogging/lib/helpers/input_password.js` — accepts `class`, `placeholder`, `data-1p-ignore`); Ghost 6.44.1 source confirms and adds two facts the spec should carry: the helper hardcodes `autofocus="autofocus"` (so "focus returns to the field" on a wrong-password render is the helper's, not the design's — and focus lands in the field on every gate render, before the skip link), and with no `class` it emits `private-login-password`. — verdict: buildable. Reaches: spec §0 settlement 2, 1 §10 focus order.
- **prd-defect** — **the gate's wrong-password line (§0 settlement 2: "The message is Ghost's string and never a field"; page-source row 4; note 6; field-list row *{{error}}*)** — claim: render `{{error.message}}` ("Incorrect access code.") and nothing else. — evidence: `appendix-h1-string-catalog.md` §3.6 (normative on chrome strings, rank 3): "**Prefer `private.error`**, so the page is translatable; a design that renders `{{error.message}}` ships an untranslatable string on a page that has no other English on it"; the trigger is `{{#if error}}` (research §11). — verdict: buildable with a stated change: `{{#if error}}{{t "private.error"}}{{/if}}` — the condition is Ghost's, the words are the catalog's. The spec's "never translatable" ruling contradicts the normative companion; the PRD wins on the decision, so the spec moves. Reaches: spec §0 settlement 2, §0 Content group, page-source row 4, note 6, field list; appendix-h1 §3.6 (`private.error`).
- **arch-gap** — **the gate on a self-signup site** — claim (implicit): the gate is a password field and nothing else. — evidence: Ghost's default `private.hbs` also renders a members subscribe form (`data-members-form="subscribe"`, private.hbs:58) when `@site.allow_self_signup` is true; research §11 note: "A custom `private.hbs` that only renders the password field loses that affordance." — verdict: buildable; **owner decides** whether A31's gate drops Ghost's subscribe affordance (the spec's "refuses everything" line does, silently). Reaches: spec §0 settlement 1; owner-flag register.
- **prd-defect** — **FR-G7 registry row 17 (`member-form`) lists "A31 #10 Private Site Gate error line"** — claim (registry): the gate uses `member-form`. — evidence: `research-section-js-libraries.md` §2.1 row 17; the spec refuses it correctly (§0 settlement 2, finding 5: `member-form` posts to the members endpoint; the gate is a native POST to `/private/`). — verdict: the **registry** is wrong; row 17's designs-requiring count drops 11 → 10 and its trigger text loses A31. Reaches: research §2.1 row 17; FR-G7; spec finding 5 (consistent).
- **stale-design** — **the 404's search field (§0 settlement 3: "works with JavaScript off… searches title, excerpt and slug — body text is not indexed"; page-source row 5)** — evidence: D3 (ruled): the index is MiniSearch vendored in `search-overlay` and gains "Search in: Titles and excerpts · Full content"; A23 §0: "**No JavaScript, no results — in all fifteen**. A Ghost template cannot read a query string and cannot search server-side, so a GET to `/search/` lands on a page whose results are rendered by the same client module"; registry §7 `search-overlay`: the form "submits as a normal page navigation". — verdict: buildable with a stated change: the row reads "title, excerpt and — where the site enables it — full content (A23's index)", and the no-JS sentence is A23's ("the field is real and submits; results need JavaScript on the search route"), not "works with JavaScript off". Reaches: spec §0 settlement 3, page-source row 5, 1 §9 ("the field is a real GET form"), every design's *Search on the 404* row.
- **arch-gap** — **finding 3: the field renders only when `/search/` exists** — evidence: FR-I5 (default routing, no `routes.yaml`, is the ordinary case); A23: "No search route on the site → the design is not offered and the editor names the reason". Nothing in the PRD says who creates the `/search/` route — the Routes Manager (FR-I2) is opt-in. — verdict: a product mechanism with **no owner; needs one** (same family as the carry-forward's "the product picks its all-tags and all-authors routes once"). Until it exists, A31's *Search on the 404* value must be unavailable (FR-H7 prevention) on a project with no search route, and the spec must say so. Reaches: spec finding 3, every design's *Search on the 404* row; A23; FR-I2/I5.
- **spec-incomplete** — **A31-8 §7/§8, the aborted get** — evidence: appendix-b1 §5: a slow `{{#get}}` is aborted and yields an empty collection **plus a visible** `<span data-aborted-get-helper>Could not load content</span>`; "every `{{#get}}`-driven section must degrade gracefully (FR-H8 guards)". The spec's "the list is absent, never empty" covers the empty case, not the aborted one — on a struggling site the 404 shows Ghost's span under `postsLabel`. — verdict: buildable; the Empty-state row must name the aborted state (label and hairline leave with it). Reaches: spec 8 §8.
- **consistent** — **A31-8's rows include members-only posts** — evidence: appendix-b1 §4.1: `{{#foreach posts}}` defaults `visibility='all'`; cards show, bodies stay gated. Fine for a 404 list; the Data row should say so. Reaches: spec 8 §7.
- **arch-gap** — **hand-offs (7 → 1 on the 500; 8 and 9 → 1 on the 500 and the gate; 7 → 6 with no image; 9 → 1 with no navigation)** — claim: a design renders *another* design in some states. — evidence: FR-G7(2)/FR-J3: "the compiler emits neither the stylesheet nor the module of a design nothing places, and it strips dead CSS"; AD-3: a design switch replaces the attribute set. A hand-off places 1 Centred (or 6) without a user placing it, so its CSS must be emitted and its markup must sit in the same file behind a `{{#match statusCode}}` / `{{#if image}}` / `{{#if @site.navigation}}` branch. A1·11 and A29·5 already rely on the same mechanism. — verdict: buildable; **owner: FR-J3 + AD-3 — no rule names hand-offs; needs one** (which designs a file must additionally emit, and that the strip counts them as reachable). Reaches: spec §0 Dark, 7 §4; AD-30. (The same rule makes "card and plane depth forced to Flat in dark" a Shadow-token resolution, which is fine.)

#### 3 · Gaps
- **spec-incomplete** — the **copy-set defaults** are the strings the synthesized `error.hbs` ships (Synthesis Defaults, inventory 734–740: A31 #1 is synthesized on every untouched project) — so every default must be stated and must be a catalog key (S6). Missing keys the catalog would need (appendix-h1 §3.5/§3.6): `error.eyebrow_404` "Not found" · `error.eyebrow_500` "Our end" · `private.eyebrow` "Private" · `error.links_label` "Try one of these" · `error.posts_label` (replacing "Recently on Orbit Weekly") · `error.directory_label` "Everything the site does have" · `error.search_placeholder` · `private.display_word` "Private" · `private.help` "Ask whoever sent you the link…" · `private.field_label` "Password" · `search.submit` · plus the 500's authored-mailto secondary default (none stated). Reaches: spec field list; appendix-h1.
- **spec-incomplete** — **FR-H8 guards** are never named for the bound rows (`@site.title`, `@site.description`, `statusCode`, `message`, the 404's `@member`); the 500 in particular has no fallback for a missing `@site` (above). Reaches: every design's §7.
- **spec-incomplete** — **P0·3's Ghost-list card** ("From Ghost" mark, read-only preview rows, "Add and remove them in Ghost…") is not mentioned for 8's posts or 9's nav; the spec says only "no Add". Reaches: spec 8/9 §6, §0 Repeating items.

Under the export every A31 instance *is* the gate, and the synthesized `error.hbs` is A31 #1 — so does an untouched project emit `private.hbs`? The spec's "a publication that turns privacy on for a week does not write the gate from scratch" implies yes. Owner rules; FR-I1 and the Synthesis Defaults' NEVER list move accordingly. Reaches: FR-I1; inventory 674–676; spec §0 field list ("the copy set exists once per page").
- **prd-defect** — **FR-J15's Free credit** ("if a Free design has no visible footer section, the compiler appends a minimal credit line to `default.hbs`'s footer region") cannot reach the 500 or the gate — neither extends `default.hbs` and both refuse a footer by design. FR-J15 must say the credit rides on `default.hbs`-derived pages only. Reaches: FR-J15; spec §0 settlements 1, 4.

Reaches: spec 6/10 §6; P0·8; **no owner; needs one** (E5/E6).

Reaches: spec §0 Behaviour, finding 8.

#### 4 · Architecture asks
- `error-404.hbs` + `error.hbs` split (or a branch-per-status `error.hbs` with its own head) — owner: **FR-I1 + appendix-b1 §3c** (a PRD ruling, then E7).
- `nav-transform` registry addition (D2) — owner: **FR-G7 / register 45** (carry-forward already names it; the spec honours D2: no no-JS accommodation, flat raw-prefix degradation stated).
- Hand-off emission rule (a file that must carry a second design's markup and CSS) — owner: **FR-J3 + AD-3 — no owner; needs one**.
- The `/search/` route's existence as a project fact the editor can test — owner: **no owner; needs one** (FR-I2/A23).
- The gate's action-less form and `?r=` preservation — owner: **E7 emission** (a compile rule, cited above).
- Register 44's authored/Ghost-bound split: A31 carries an authored `links[]` (0–6) baked as static blocks (§7.3 missing-construct 1) — **register 44 and §7.3's category list must add A31**.
- `private.hbs` emission trigger under the one-instance-three-pages model — owner: **FR-I1 + Synthesis Defaults**.
- Mode-dependent scrim on 7 → a pack token — owner: **AD-30**.
- `@member` on error renders is cited, not executed — register 13's residual could absorb NE-A31-3.

#### 5 · Spec completeness
- All ten fields present on all ten designs (Descriptor · Structural · Archetype · Responsive · Content · Controls · Data · Empty · Behaviour · Accessibility) — yes, 10/10.
- Tuples: ten six-slot tuples, first five closed-vocabulary — archetype ∈ {stack ×6, split ×2, feed, nav}; containment ∈ {none ×8, card, box}; ground ∈ {page ×6, surface, contrast ×2, image}; count ∈ {none ×8, many ×2}; media ∈ {none ×9, background}. **No off-vocabulary word. No first-five collision** (`tuple-check-specs.txt`: A31 disk 10 · tuples 10; OK). Nearest pairs rest on one slot each: 1/3 (containment), 3/4 (card/box), 1/5 (ground), 6/10 (archetype), 2/10 (ground), 8/9 (archetype).
- Modules: `core` ×10 with the one-line no-JS statement; `nav-transform` on 9 carries its degradation line (D2). No invented name.
- Lists: `links[]` carries add/remove/reorder (P0·3, arriving content named — "The archive index" → `/archive/`); posts (8) and nav (9) carry no Add. The P0·3 Ghost-list card is not restated.
- Controls per design 6–8 (+ Eyebrow on 10 per the frame) — all under ≈15; universals outside the list; Background role locked on 5/6/7/10 with reasons (D7).
- `[Free]` markers: none.
- Internal inconsistencies: 10 §6 (Eyebrow), `imageFocus` (9 vs 3 values), `search.label`/`search.submit` (non-existent keys).

## A32 · Paywall / Content CTA
**Counts (derived):** designs on disk **12** (13 frames `A32-0`…`A32-12` − the proof) · spec **12** (`## 1`…`## 12`) · inventory **12** (line 627) — **but not the same twelve**: the inventory's roster is Fade + Card · Hard Stop Card · Split Benefits · Tier Cards Inline · Minimal Lock Line · Dark Lock Panel · Testimonial Unlock · Dual Path · Big Type Ask · Blurred Preview · Checklist Compact · Progress Tease; the export's is Fade · Card · Panel · Contrast Band · Boxed · Split Pitch · Tiers · Ledger · Big Type · Cover · Sticky Bar · Meter (Testimonial Unlock and Dual Path have no counterpart; Blurred Preview became a control value on 1 Fade; Progress Tease ≈ 12 Meter). No decision D1–D39 covers A32's roster. · [Free] spec **0 marked** / inventory **2** (#1, #2 → export #1 Fade, #2 Card) · modules declared: `core` (all) · `member-form` (1, 6 — at *Button and email field*) · `price-toggle` (7) · `dismiss` (11 — at *Dismissible = Yes*) · `reading-progress` (12) — all five in the 31; no invented name · custom-setting slots: **0** · authored lists: `benefits[]` 0–6 (drawn by 1–6, 8, 10; stored by 7, 9, 11, 12) · Ghost-bound lists: `tiers` (`{{#get}}`, drawn by 7, read by all).

Non-placeable: chosen in the Paywall editor, one per project, compiled to `partials/content-cta.hbs`, universal controls carried because it renders as a block (Appendix C; inventory line 21). The spec honours that framing throughout.

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **consistent** — **the surface (§0 "What A32 is", Access source rows)** — claim: Ghost renders the partial at the members-only cut and sends only the preview. — evidence: `research-ghost-membership-pages.md` §0(iv) and §9 ("Overriding `partials/content-cta.hbs`. Real and supported… already A32's target"; Solo's house-style partial), `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` §16, appendix-b1 §4.2 ("`{{content}}` self-gates… overridden wholesale by `partials/content-cta.hbs`"), `research-contested-variants.md` §3.1 (`post-gating.js` slices `html` at `<!--members-only-->`; the remainder never leaves the server) and §4.2 (`content.js` → `restrictedCta` → `templates.execute('content-cta', this, {data})`; the partial receives `{{{html}}}` and the post as `this`). **Register 11 closed it by execution on both majors — with a condition the spec does not carry:** "the override only takes effect if the theme ALSO references the partial explicitly… the compiler emits an explicit `{{> "content-cta"}}` reference wherever it emits the partial". — verdict: buildable; **spec-incomplete** on the register-11 condition — the Access source group must state it as a compile fact (owner: E7 / register 11). Reaches: spec §0, Access rows; register 11.
- **consistent** — **what the partial can read (every design's §7)** — evidence: inside `{{#post}}` the partial's `this` is the post: `visibility`, `access`, `reading_time` (appendix-b1 §4.2), and `tiers` — Ghost 6.44.1 `core/frontend/services/data/entry-lookup.js:39` `include: 'authors,tags,tiers'`; `@member`, `@site` via the render data (appendix-b1 §2); `{{#get "tiers"}}` works in any template (research §6). — verdict: buildable. The named-tier gate's data (`post.tiers[].name`) is reachable in principle but never executed inside the partial → NE-A32-2.
- **arch-gap** — **`{{{html}}}` in the emitted partial** — evidence: AD-4: "The compiler never emits `{{{ }}}` — there is no user HTML to emit"; the paywall partial *must* emit `{{{html}}}` (research §4.3's recommended shell `<div class="inflozo-gated-preview">{{{html}}}</div>`). It is Ghost-sourced HTML, like `{{content}}`, not user text — but AD-4's sentence has no carve-out and AD-36's sinks rule reads the same way. — verdict: buildable; **owner: AD-4 (+ AD-36)** must name the one compiler-authored triple-stash. Reaches: spec §0 settlement 1; AD-4; FR-J17 gate.
- **consistent** — **prices (§0 "Prices, and the flag that guards them", 7 §7)** — evidence: `{{price monthly_price currency=currency}}` (research §6; docs `helpers/data/price`); FR-H6 and the carry-forward. — verdict: buildable. Three things the spec does not say: (a) the "lowest paid price" is the **first** row of the filtered get — tiers return in ascending monthly price (research §6, `docs.ghost.org/content-api/tiers`) — so "From …" is `@first`, and the spec should name that rather than imply a computed minimum Handlebars cannot do; (b) the price clause lives **inside an authored default** ("From $6 a month, and you can stop whenever you like" — frames `A32-1`, `A32-7`; the named-tier heading "This piece is for Patron members" and `ctaLabel` "See Patron" embed a Ghost tier name the same way) — **there is no token mechanism for a bound value inside a text prop** (AD-4: text-plus-marks; `{placeholder}` syntax is catalog-only, appendix-h1 S3) → the clause must be a compiler-generated fragment beside the blurb (`{{#if @site.paid_members_enabled}}{{t "member.from_price" price=(price …)}}{{/if}}`), and the tier name likewise (`{{t "member.tier_gate_heading" tier=name}}`), never part of the prop; (c) "From", "a month" / "a year", the free card's "Free" and the currency-symbol rule for non-symbol currencies (A7 carry-forward) are chrome with **no catalog keys** (appendix-h1 has no pricing namespace). Also a cross-category tension the owner should see: A7 §0 refuses "a 'from' price… anywhere in A7: Ghost's Offers own them", while A32 states one. "From Ghost, all" is an unfiltered get. — verdict: buildable with a stated change: the query is `{{#if @site.paid_members_enabled}}{{#get "tiers" filter="type:paid+visibility:public" limit="100" …}}`; the *Tiers* row loses "From Ghost, all"; the 0-paid-tier hand-off tests the **filtered** set. The catalog encodes the same split: `member.read_so_far` "About {percent}% read" (**JS**) and `member.read_so_far_static` "You're partway through this post." (no number). The registry §7 line the spec quotes — "The bar is hidden entirely… renders at its server-known static value" — is contradicted by the spec's own reading that the fill is static and the module merely animates: with JS off there is no share to fill. — verdict: **not buildable as written; buildable with the change** research §3.4 already specifies: server-rendered baseline sentence carrying `{{reading_time}}` (the `{total}` half); the fill and any `{read}`/share number written by `reading-progress` from `previewWords / (reading_time × 275)`, bucketed, and **hidden when `reading_time < 3`** or the preview is empty. Reaches: spec 12 §6/§7/Flagged; inventory 628/640; appendix-h1 `member.read_so_far*`.

- **consistent** — **the "last visible block" class (§0 settlement 4 "the third is not settled… asks the build for a class"; carry-forward "A32 needs the last visible block class")** — evidence: research §4.2/§4.3: Ghost emits the preview blocks **bare**; the theme owns the partial, wraps `{{{html}}}` in `.inflozo-gated-preview`, and `> :last-child` is reliable because the wrapper holds nothing else; the paywall card is a top-level block so the slice lands between blocks. The type suppression is then a selector, not a class: `.inflozo-gated-preview > :is(p, ul, ol):last-child { mask-image: … }` — headings, figures, code and embeds simply do not match. — verdict: **buildable; no class is needed — the flag and the carry-forward close by citation.** Two residues: (a) "**suppressed under two lines of visible text**" (§0 shared floor) is **not a stylesheet condition** — CSS cannot count lines; drop it or accept that a one-line last paragraph fades entirely (a fixed-px gradient from the bottom, `mask-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, #000 calc(100% - 160px), transparent)`, is the nearest CSS); (b) research §4.3(3) says **mask, not `filter: blur()`** — 1 Fade's *Blur the last block* (2.6 px) contradicts the normative mechanism for #10 (blur bleeds outside the box and forces a stacking context) → **stale-design**. No design's Empty-state row mentions it; the Access row says "Ghost's preview, unchanged". — verdict: buildable; every design states the empty-preview state (FR-H4 makes it a required field), 12 hides its meter, 2's Overlap and every fade are inert. Reaches: all twelve §8; §0 Access row 4.
- **arch-gap** — **which element is the paywall's section root (AD-3)** — evidence: the landing-type rules — the fade suppressed after a heading/figure/code/embed; "after a heading the space above the gate grows 72/132" (§0 settlement 4); 2 "Overlap is refused after a heading and after an image"; 5 "Top and bottom only is refused after an image"; 7 "Padding is forced to Spacious after a heading"; 8 "After an image the design forces Detail line = Show" — all read the **preview wrapper's** last child, which is outside the gate. AD-3: a control writes one attribute on the section root and the stylesheet selects on it. Expressible only with `:has()` — Baseline Widely 2026-06-19, inside the 2026-08-18 pin (FR-G8 Tier 1; research §2.2 cites it): `.inflozo-gated-preview:has(> :is(h2,h3,figure,pre):last-child) + .gate[data-overlap="rise"] { … }`. Two rulings are missing: (1) **is the section root the partial's outer wrapper (preview + gate) or the gate alone?** Background role on the outer wrapper would recolour the preview (breaking "the page ground unchanged at the seam"); on the gate alone, 11 Sticky Bar's `position: sticky; bottom: 0` has no containing block that extends above it and never pins. (2) **The editor cannot "refuse" a value by landing type** — the canvas never renders the real body (NFR-3; FR-D16: a gated body is the style-guide fixture), so every "refused after a heading/image" is a stylesheet neutralisation on the live site, never an editor refusal; the spec's wording says the reverse. — verdict: buildable; **owner: AD-3 — needs a ruling on the paywall's root and the landing-type mechanism.** Reaches: spec §0 settlements 1, 4; 2/5/7/8/10 Flagged; 11 §3/§9; AD-3; FR-G8.

#### 2 · Contradictions

And under FR-J4 a declared module ships whenever its design is active — a treatment is always active — so `accordion` lands in every theme's `main.js` for a card that never runs it (FR-G7(2)/FR-J3 emit-only-if-used). Reaches: roster; items 9 ×6; Findings 2, 5; Reconciliation note 8; inventory 642 (declares no module); FR-G7(2)(3); FR-J4; registry §2.2, §7.

## A34 · Pagination Styles
**Counts (derived):** designs on disk 10 (frames 11 − proof `A34-0`) · spec 10 (`## 1 · Numbers` … `## 10 · Slim`) · inventory 10 (line 651) · [Free] spec **none marked** / inventory #1, #2 (lines 653–654: Numbered Classic, Load More Solid; by position in the export = Numbers, Prev and Next — no Free design declares a module any more) · modules declared: `load-more` (6 Load More), `infinite-scroll` (7 Endless), none in the other eight ("`core` assumed") vs registry §2.1: both names exist (rows 24, 25); registry rows 19/24/25 name inventory designs (`reveal` for "A34 #9 Infinite Fade skeleton"; `load-more` for "#2, #7, #8"; `infinite-scroll` for "#9, #10") that the export does not contain · custom-setting slots: 0 · authored lists: 0 · Ghost-bound lists: 0 (page links are route-derived; no `{{#foreach}}`) · controls: 4 shared Pager-block fields + 5 (1, 3, 4, 5) or 4 (2, 6–10) per design · strings: 13 claimed, all catalog (D10).

**Naming note:** the inventory's ten are Numbered Classic · Load More Solid · Numbered Pills · Minimal Prev/Next · Big Arrows · Rule + Numbers · Load More Ghost · Load More Ticker · Infinite Fade · Infinite Dot Pulse (3 load-more + 2 infinite); the export's ten are Numbers · Prev and Next · Bar · Pill · Counter · Load More · Endless · Contrast Band · Cards · Slim (1 + 1). Every registry/catalog reference below is to the inventory names.

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility
- **ghost-infeasible** — **1 Numbers / 3 Bar / 4 Pill "Numbers: Windowed · All pages", and the floor's "the window appears only above seven pages" (≤ 7 pages draws every page)** — claim: a row of every page link — evidence: Ghost's helper set (`research-ghost-empty-values.md` line 572 list; `research-ghost-binding-contexts.md` §12 helper audit) has **no numeric range loop** — `{{#foreach}}` iterates arrays (`posts`), never `1…pages`; §7.3's missing-construct #6 lists `{{pagination}}`, `{{#if pagination.next}}`, `{{page_url}}` and nothing that counts — verdict: **not buildable on Ghost** as an unbounded row; **buildable with a stated change** as a fixed unroll: the seven-slot window is seven literal slots (`{{page_url 1}}` · ellipsis gated by `{{#match pagination.prev ">" 2}}` · `{{page_url prev}}`/`pagination.prev` · current · `{{page_url next}}`/`pagination.next` · ellipsis gated by `{{#match pagination.next "<" pagination.pages}}` · `{{page_url pagination.pages}}`), and "All pages" must be capped at a compile-time unroll (N slots each guarded by `{{#match pagination.pages ">=" n}}`) or dropped. 4 Pill's "above fourteen pages scrolls" presumes ≥ 15 numerals. Reaches: 1 item 6/7, 3 item 4/6, 4 item 4/6, floor "The window"; §7.3 construct #6; NE-A34-2 (match operators).

## P0 · Editor Primitives (shared spec — not a category)

**Counts (derived):** frames on disk 7 (`P0-1`…`P0-6` + `S14 Editor Cards`; no `-0 Category Proof` frame exists for P0) · primitives in the spec 8 (P0·1–P0·8; P0·8 is rules-only, no frame) · no design headings, no tuples, no [Free] markers (the spec is editor software, not library designs) · modules declared: **none** (P0·8 rule 4 — the primitives "declare no modules"; the 15 example names it cites — `marquee` `rotator` `dismiss` `mode-toggle` `search-overlay` `price-toggle` `member-form` `lightbox` `countdown` `count-up` `accordion` `tabs` `carousel` `share` `filter-strip` — all exist in `research-section-js-libraries.md` §2.1) · custom-setting slots spent: 0 · authored lists: P0·3 *is* the authored-list control · Ghost-bound lists: P0·3's "Ghost-sourced list card" + P0·5's panel. Derivation: `ls | grep -E '^P0-'` → 6 files; `S14 Editor Cards.dc.html` is P0·7's frame; spec `## P0·n` headings → 8.

**How this file is read.** P0 has no "Reconciliation notes" section. Its equivalent is the **"Flagged ⚑"** paragraph closing every primitive plus inline ⚑ marks; every one of them is a row in §6. The spec's own precedence line ("where this file and a drawn frame disagree, the frame is wrong and this file wins") is honoured below — the S14 frame is read only where the spec is silent.

#### 1 · Ghost feasibility

- **needs-execution** — **P0·5 Hand-picked** — claim: "the picked list is the count *and the order*" (Count and Order hide). — evidence: Appendix B query rules (`{{#get}}` mirrors Content API `filter` + `order`); Ghost's `get` helper takes `filter="id:[a,b,c]"` and an `order` attribute — NQL has no positional-order operator, so an `id:[…]` "in" filter returns rows in `order` (default `published_at desc`), never in list position. — verdict: **buildable with a stated change** — either the compiler emits one `{{#get "posts" filter="id:{id}" limit="1"}}` per pick (N ≤ the design max; each is a server query — NFR-2 render cost), or Order re-appears for Hand-picked and drag order is dropped. Probe NE-P0-1. Reaches: P0·5 §Filter table, D5 (hand-picked everywhere), A17/A18/A19/A27/A3-9 posts sources, A20/A21/A12 tag/author refs, FR-H2, §7.3 missing-construct #2.
- **needs-execution** — **P0·6 form states** "sent / invalid / failed / expired / subscribed" (A16, A22, A30). — evidence: Appendix B — Ghost's `data-members-form` exposes exactly `loading` / `success` / `error` classes on the `<form>` plus a `data-members-error` slot (`research-ghost-membership-pages.md` §4). "Expired" is a magic-link *landing* state Ghost reports to Portal via query params, and "already subscribed" is answered by Ghost as `success` (a magic link is sent to an existing member). — verdict: **needs execution** — two of the five states may have no server-side or class hook a theme can style. Probe NE-P0-2. Reaches: P0·6 §Drawn, A22/A30/A16 state lists and their `member.*` copy fields, appendix-h1 §3.4, FR-Q6.
- **buildable with a stated change** — **P0·4 three-state compile** — claim: "compiles to server-side member checks". — evidence: Appendix B `@member` = `{ …, status: free/paid/comped, paid }`; FR-D16 "`comped` previews as Paid". — verdict: buildable as `{{#if @member}}…{{#if @member.paid}}` (never `{{#match @member.status "paid"}}`), and the spec must say `comped` takes the Paid branch — it is silent. Probe NE-P0-3 confirms `@member.paid` for a comped member. Reaches: P0·4 §Anatomy, FR-D16, Appendix B, §7.3 missing-construct #4.
- **buildable with a stated change** — **P0·2 icons on the live site** — claim: "production ships the set verbatim"; the rendered icon is `aria-hidden`. — evidence: no PRD text and no AD says *how* an icon reaches a `.hbs` (inline `<svg>` per slot as content, or a sprite partial), nor how Tabler's MIT notice ships (FR-J4 declares vendored `cards.js` in the README — the same obligation applies), nor how icons count in FR-J3's theme-size budget. — verdict: buildable; the emission is unowned — see §4. Reaches: P0·2, FR-F1 Icon Picker, FR-J3, FR-J4, §7.4.
- **consistent** — **P0·1 Portal chips** `signup` · `signin` · `account` · `account/plans` are Appendix B's verified values and `upgrade` is correctly absent (Appendix B: "`upgrade` is not a Portal value"). Useful because Ghost's own Source theme ships the broken value.
- **consistent** — **P0·5 "No relative-date filters"** matches FR-I2's ruling that relative dates are a `routes.yaml` capability, not a Data-group one — and P0·5 gives the same reason. Useful because S9c (below) got the Routes-side half wrong.
- **consistent** — **P0·5 secondary feed renders nothing at zero items, heading and container together** is FR-H4 (2) verbatim; the meta-toggle set (date · author · excerpt · reading time · tag chip) is FR-H2's exactly.

#### 2 · Contradictions

- **stale-design** — **P0·1 §Plain-text-locked** — "Editing the text edits the Ghost setting" for site title / description / member counts / author names / tier names. This is a **write to a Ghost setting**, which P8 forbids ("never writes a Ghost setting that is not presentation"), AD-10's allowlist forbids (theme + `routes.yaml` only — restated in `BACKUP-GATE.md`), and FR-C3's proxy has no route for. The spec conflates three cases: (a) a `@site.*` / tier / author / count **binding** is read-only on canvas and what the user edits is the **static fallback** FR-H8 compiles as `{{else}}`; (b) an **FR-Q3 promoted** text prop is editable *in Inflozo* (it compiles as the Ghost Admin default) and plain-text-locked; (c) Ghost data is never editable anywhere. The lock pill's wording "set in Ghost" fits (a), not (b). Reaches: P0·1 §Plain-text-locked + pill string, component inventory "Plain-text lock pill", FR-Q3, FR-H8, P8, AD-10, FR-C3.
- **stale-design** — **P0·2 §Filled-slot popover** — Size (S/M/L) and Colour per *slot*. AD-3: every control value writes one `data-*` on the **section root**; register 44: "a control that styles *one* item is impossible by construction". Where slots are per item — feature/stat/step/contact icons (A5, A10, A13, A16), social rows (A3, A21, A24/A26) — a per-slot Size/Colour is per-item styling. P0·3 itself says "Per-item layout, spacing or emphasis does not exist". Either the popover is a shortcut to two **section-level** controls (Icon size · Icon colour — every slot follows, and the popover says so) or it cannot exist. Reaches: P0·2 §Filled-slot popover, component inventory "Icon slot popover", AD-3, register 44, FR-F3's ≈15 cap (+2 controls on every icon-bearing design), the category specs that reuse it by name.
- **stale-design** — **P0·2 Colour row** — "role swatches: Text · Muted · Accent · On-accent — never a hex". *Answer to the orchestrator's question:* yes — it is a Swatch-Row-role rule and not a colour picker, so P2/Appendix C's hex ban is honoured. But Appendix C's Swatch Row allowed values are **Base / Surface / Accent / Contrast / Image** (background roles); Text / Muted / On-accent are FR-E1 *tokens*, off Appendix C's vocabulary. A second, closed **foreground-role** value set must join Appendix C (or icon colour becomes a Named Select) — until then the value set is not "closed and enumerable" (Appendix C's rule for data-attribute selectors). Reaches: P0·2, Appendix C Swatch Row row, FR-F1, §7.3 (closed value sets), every icon-bearing category.
- **stale-design** — **P0·2 §Library ruling** — "production ships the set verbatim" (Tabler ~6,100). D1 rules a **curated Tabler set** whose subset "must explicitly include the nine Ghost social platforms"; Appendix C's row is "curated … subset (~120)". No curated subset is named and the nine platforms (`facebook`, `twitter`, `threads`, `bluesky`, `mastodon`, `tiktok`, `youtube`, `instagram`, `linkedin` — `appendix-b1-template-contexts.md` line 191) are not listed. The picker's category chips (Arrows · Interface · Media · Commerce · Social / Brands) are not a subset definition. Reaches: P0·2 §Library ruling + §Icon Picker, D1, Appendix C Icon Picker row, FR-F1, A1/A3/A21/A24/A26 social rows.
- **stale-design** — **P0·7 §Right sidebar** — Callout "Background role (Base · Surface · **Tint** · Accent)". "Tint" is not an Appendix C Swatch Row value and not an FR-E1 token; FR-Q7 holds each card panel "to the same 4–7 control discipline as a section" (named values from the closed vocabularies). Drawn identically on S14a/S14e. Reaches: P0·7, S14a/S14e, A33 §1 Plain/Callout rows, Appendix C.
- **stale-design** — **P0·7 §Chrome card roster** — "all twenty Koenig cards, Ghost's order: image, markdown, HTML, gallery, divider, bookmark, email content, call to action, public preview, button, callout, GIF, toggle, audio, video, file, product, header, embeds, signup". FR-H3 is explicit that `research-ghost-koenig-cards.md` §6.6's enumeration "**is** the design surface, and FR-Q7's panel set must cover exactly it" — image, gallery, video, callout, button, product, `header_v2`, signup, cta, file, toggle, **code**, bookmark (+ audio per FR-Q7). P0·7 offers panels for cards with nothing the theme can style — *public preview* renders nothing on the site (it is the `content-cta` cutoff), *email content* is email-only, *markdown*/*HTML* render the author's own HTML, *GIF* is an image-card variant — and omits **code** and **transistor** (research line 72), and collapses `header`/`header_v2`, which FR-Q7 says are "separate exclude names and both must be listed". Reaches: P0·7 §Chrome, S14a dropdown, FR-Q7, FR-H3 (1), research §6.6 + line 72 + Appendix A chunk table, A33 roster.
- **prd-defect** — the PRD's own card lists disagree, so the design could not have picked a roster the PRD had settled: FR-Q7 names "code, **table, blockquote**" (Lexical nodes; the research's chunk table has a `blockquote` chunk but no `table`), FR-H3's enumeration omits **audio** while FR-Q7 names it among the four JS-dependent cards, and the research counts **27 design surfaces** (header v1/v2 split). One roster must be declared normative (the research §6.6, per the precedence order). Reaches: FR-Q7, FR-H3 (1), research-ghost-koenig-cards §6.6 / line 72 / Appendix A, P0·7, A33, S14.
- **stale-design** — **P0·1 §Search state / P0·4 Link** — Portal actions "always all four" (Sign up · Sign in · Account · Upgrade). FR-F6 names those four — but Appendix B's "**verified set** (Link Picker → `data-portal`)" has **eleven**: `account/profile` · `account/newsletters` · `signup/{tierId}` · `signup/{tierId}/monthly|yearly` · `support` · `recommendations` in addition. No surface offers them; A22's manage-newsletters and A30's account links need `account/newsletters`/`account/profile`. Also a **prd-defect**: FR-F6 and Appendix B disagree on the picker's set. Reaches: P0·1, P0·4, FR-F6, Appendix B, A22/A30/A7 specs.
- **stale-design** — **P0·3 §Ghost-sourced list** — "posts, tags, authors, tiers … Count stepper · Order Newest/Oldest at minimum". Newest/Oldest is post vocabulary: **tiers** return in ascending monthly price and are never re-ordered or paginated (Appendix B); **tags/authors** order by name or `count.posts` (carry-forward: an `authors` source shape with its own Order). Reaches: P0·3, P0·5 (posts-only), FR-H2, carry-forward "Data & FR-H2", A7/A12/A20/A21.
- **stale-design** — **P0·7 §Entry point** — "Pages · Layers · Editor cards", "the page switcher". The PRD's unit is the **template** (FR-D6 *template switcher*; Appendix I). "Pages" collides with Ghost pages, which FR-I6 binds *to* templates — the one place a user must tell the two apart. S14d draws "Pages 6". Reaches: P0·7 §Entry point, S14d, component inventory "Surface switcher", FR-D6, FR-I6, Appendix I.

#### 5 · Spec completeness

- Not a category: no ten-field designs, no six-slot tuples, no [Free] markers — nothing to collide. Per primitive the spec carries Anatomy · Behaviour · States (explicit on P0·1; implicit elsewhere) · Accessibility (all seven) · a ⚑ list. **Missing per primitive:** P0·1 — the 390 scope (gap 14) and the three lock cases (contradiction 1); P0·2 — the curated subset (contradiction 4) and the slot/section scope of Size/Colour (contradiction 2); P0·3 — Del/⌘D on an item (gap 5) and schema home for min/max (gap 6); P0·4 — `comped` branch, JS-off sentence, catalog-keyed defaults (feasibility 3, gaps 7–8); P0·5 — non-post sources and the main-feed variant (gaps 2–3); P0·6 — empty-feed and page-2 states, edit-safe scope (gaps 4, 13); P0·7 — roster, Free badge, nine-hue mapping (contradiction 6, gaps 10–11); P0·8 — the Preview toggle (gap 15).
- **Modules:** none declared and none needed — rule 4 is honoured; the 15 example names all resolve in §2.1. No no-JS lines are owed by P0 itself; the one it *creates* (Portal links in P0·4) is gap 7.
- **Lists:** register 44's rule (authored → add/remove/reorder; Ghost-bound → none, count + order) is P0·3 by construction. The Ghost-list card's order vocabulary is wrong for non-post resources (contradiction 9).
- **Strings:** P0's own strings are editor chrome (not catalog) — correct per Appendix H's "canvas-state markers are app copy" rule — except the four action defaults (gap 8) and the new-tab a11y string (gap 1), which reach the theme.
- **S14 frame vs spec:** the frame agrees with the spec everywhere read (roster, Tint, NO COLOUR CTLS rows, read-only block, reset copy, nav group) — so every S14 finding above is a spec finding, not a drawing error.

**Method.** Visible text extracted from each `.dc.html` (scripts/styles stripped, tags removed, whitespace collapsed) — the frames are inline DOM, so the text pass is complete. Every finding cites the frame's own sub-frame label (e.g. `S8a′`, `B19`) and the FR. Numbers are derived by counting what the screens say, never taken from a doc.

## 37 · Cross-cutting — what the 36 sections say together

### 37.1 Counts, and what D11 obliges the PRD to change

- **prd-defect** — **The library total.** 485 design frames and 485 tuples on disk; `prd.md` says **484** in FR-G1, FR-G5, FR-G6, FR-G8, Appendix A, F.1 and §7.3 (34 occurrences), `sections-inventory.md` says 484 three times, the spine eight times, `INDEX.md`, `build-sequence.md`, `CONTROL-PROMPTS.html`, `MEASUREMENTS.md`, `appendix-b1`, `appendix-h1` and `tools/doc-audit.py` restate it. **The PRD already disagrees with itself:** FR-G1 line 275 says "**457** are placeable sections and **28** are non-placeable" (= 485) while the inventory's carve-out (line 9) says "**456** of the 484 are placeable" (= 484). D11 rules the count is re-derived at the merge; the derived values are **485 designs · 457 placeable · 28 non-placeable**, and every restatement above moves with them (standing rule 4). Reaches: FR-G1, FR-G2, FR-G5, FR-G6, FR-G8, Appendix A table row 886 (A31 "9" → 10), F.1, §7.3, inventory lines 9/11/612/886, spine, `INDEX.md`, `doc-audit.py`. (§31 states the A31-specific changes.)
- **prd-defect / owner ruling** — **[Free] count.** 70 in the inventory (2 × 34 + A29 #7 + A31 #10). Under the export's A31 model every design draws the private gate, so `private.hbs` already has two Free options (#1 Centred, #2 Split Reason) and #10's re-tier is moot: **70 stays 70 only if the owner keeps #10 Free; otherwise 69** (§31). A29's third Free design (#7, "the author-archive binding context") also has no basis in the export, where all 14 designs bind "either" archive (§29) — the owner names which A29 design carries it. Reaches: FR-G2, F.1, inventory lines 9/587/623, Appendix A "Tiering" line 842.
- **spec-incomplete (35/35)** — **No spec marks a [Free] design.** Every reviewer derived the pair positionally (first two of every category); the inventory's names for those two differ from the export's in most categories (§37.2), so the merge cannot map [Free] by name — the specs must carry the marker, or the merge rules "positional". Reaches: every spec's roster, FR-G2, F.1, FR-L3's exit sheet (which names the Free swap target).
- **prd-defect** — **The module count.** FR-G7 says "31 modules — 30 feature modules plus one shared `core`" (7 restatements in `prd.md`); the carry-forwards add `nav-transform` (D2) and `contact-form` (D28) and grow `search-overlay` (D3, the vendored engine) and `member-form` (D36, OTC). After this pass the registry is **33 named modules**, and at least five of the 31 are claimed by no export design (§37.3). Reaches: FR-G4, FR-G7, FR-G8, FR-J4, NFR-2, research §2.1/§4.4/§7, Appendix I.

### 37.2 Rosters — the inventory's names are not the export's

The controls pass patched the specs; it did not touch `sections-inventory.md`. Reading the two side by side, **the inventory's per-design rosters no longer describe the export in at least 24 categories**: A1 (at most 9 of 16 names map; #2 Minimal Center has no counterpart), A4 (7 inventory designs absent, 7 new), A5 (7/7), A6, A7 (#12 Founding Member dropped — `research-contested-variants.md` §2 KEEP vs the export), A8, A10, A11, A12, A13, A16, A17 (order), A19 (order swapped), A20, A21, A22, A23 (zero names coincide but one), A24, A25 (order), A26 (every name differs), A27 (#11 Fresh Picks, #12 Continue Sticky absent), A28 (all ten differ), A29 (none coincide), A30 (different product model — one surface per design vs every design drawing all three routes), A31 (ten, D11), A32 (Testimonial Unlock and Dual Path absent), A33, A34. **D11 set the precedent for A31 only.** Each reviewer tagged this `prd-defect` and named the inventory lines; the ruling this pass asks for is **one wholesale supersede at the merge** (the HANDOVER's standing item for `derived-fields-A1-A12.md`, extended to the rosters, content unions, control unions, Data lines, `bindingContext`/`compileTarget` declarations and the Synthesis Defaults' named designs) rather than 34 individual rulings. Consequences that are not editorial: the FR-G7 registry's "Designs requiring it" and "Trigger in the inventory" columns cite inventory numbers that no longer exist (§37.3); `research-contested-variants.md`'s six settlements name inventory designs (A7 #12, A19 #11, A27 #11, A29 #13, A32 #10/#12) of which at least three have no export counterpart; the Synthesis Defaults (inventory 691–740) name A3 #1, A17 #1, A25 #1, A26 #1, A27 #1, A28 #2, A29 #1/#2, A31 #1 by inventory identity; §7.3's missing-construct table names designs by inventory number in rows 3, 5, 7, 8. Reaches: all of the above; `tools/category-prompts.py` (reads the inventory).

### 37.7 Gaps at library level (question 3, consolidated)

- **Editor surfaces with no frame** (§36): the **Paywall editor** (FR-H6), the **backup gate** consent checklist (`BACKUP-GATE.md`), the **drift report** (FR-J16), the **credit toggle** (FR-J15), FR-D21's page-2 preview, FR-D6's auto-generated marker and membership/Private canvases, FR-D7's project mode + "Clear dark overrides", the **New project** sheet (FR-B2), the **downgrade / over-limit** sheet (FR-L3), FR-J10's first-deploy name confirm, FR-J8's partial-success state, FR-I1's empty-custom-template warning, FR-D22's preview subject, the main-feed marker/reassign, the Staff Access Token step and its decline path (FR-C1 — journey J1's core), history **pinning** (`BACKUP-GATE.md`).
- **Drawn but on the wrong mechanism** (§36): B19's template-binding checklist uses `page-{slug}.hbs` (FR-I1 forbids it); B12's snapshot fires on every deploy and counts against history (FR-J13 says first upload, exempt); B16's routes card blames integration-key permissions (FR-I4: the Staff token); B13's exit sheet offers two of four remedies; B22's redesign proposals are per-section swaps, not FR-C7's starter × pack combinations; B11 draws a user Zoom (FR-D14: none); B24's grace banner says deployed themes stop rendering (FR-L3: never touched); S9 routes `/subscribe/` and `/` (FR-I1); B17's Theme Settings lacks `posts_per_page` and would write Ghost's logo (P8); B18's translation keys are flat (FR-Q6: dotted); S4d offers tier-level View-as (FR-D16: three states — and B9 contradicts S4d).
- **Flows (eight):** F4 (library-update confirm) and F5 (Preview-only) are right; F1, F2, F3, F6 are drawn on wrong semantics; F7 (backup gate) and F8 (pinning) have no surface. **Journeys:** J2 and J3 hold; **J1 lacks the token step**; **J4 has no over-limit flow**.
- **Plan matrix:** the 2026-08-17 numbers survive on S11c, S12a/b, M5 (3 sites, unlimited projects, "Last 2 / Full", 30 MB uploads, Free storage never shown); every screen prints **485** while the PRD says 484 and Appendix H forbids a design total in product copy.
- **Epics:** E1–E3, E5–E8, E12–E14 have screens with the gaps above; E4's kit still names no icon library; E9–E11 have the category specs; E15 none expected.

### 37.8 Strings — the catalog the specs need

D10 sent every mechanical string to `appendix-h1`. The reviewers found the catalog short of the specs in every category; the namespaces and keys are itemised per section and roll up to: `nav.*` (A1, A2, A3 — ~20 keys incl. the announcement bar's show/pause/play/dismiss), `search.*` (A1, A4, A23, A31 — `clear`, `submit`, `see_all`, `results_heading`, `key_*`, `placeholder_site/archive`), `a11y.*` (A1, A3, A12, A13, A20, A21, A24 — ~15), `carousel.*` (A5, A8, A19, A20, A27), `stats.*` (A10), `logos.*` (A11), `faq.*` (A9), `contact.*` (A16, eight), `video.*` (A15, fifteen), `tier.*` (A7), `member.*` additions (A2, A3, A6, A22, A30, A32 — status labels, gate headings, pricing chrome), `post.*` additions (A24, A25, A26, A27), `archive.*` additions (A17, A18, A29 — `group_other`, eyebrows, `posts_none`), `pagination.*` additions (A34 — `seen_of_total`, `end_of_feed_total`, `no_older/newer`, `loaded_announce`), `comments.*` corrections (A28 — strike `%`, add `noscript`), `card.*` (A33/A25 — `anchor_link`, `latest`), `error.*`/`private.*` prop-default keys (A31). Two systematic defects: **prop defaults that disagree with the catalog's default for the same string** (appendix-h1 S6 says the catalog default *is* the prop's initial value — A31 lists five pairs, A2/A3/A6 the `member.*` trio) and **keys cited that do not exist** (`search.label`, `search.submit`, `card.latest`, `error.code_label` as a variable). Owner: appendix-h1 at the merge (S9 — before the design is authored).

### 37.9 Spec completeness (question 5, consolidated)

- **Ten fields:** present on all designs in 31 of 34 categories; exceptions named per section (A1-14, A1-16 lack Behaviour; A4/A5 preambles invert edit-safe; A22's `imageFocus` value set stated two ways; A31-10's control list vs its frame). P0 has no tuples by design.
- **Tuples:** 485/485 six-slot, closed-vocabulary, unique, contiguous — verified twice (orchestrator script over all three spec formats; each reviewer per category). **First-five clusters resting on the emphasis slot alone** (register 46's documented bound) now number more than the two it records: A1 {1,13}, A4 {1,6,7} {11,15}, A5 (five designs), A10 (nine designs in four clusters), A11 {3,13} (recorded), A12 {1,2,9,14} (recorded) — register 46 should name them all.
- **No-JS lines:** §37.3.
- **Lists (register 44):** authored lists carry P0·3 add/remove/reorder and Ghost-bound lists carry none in every category that has them ✓ — with four extensions the register must bless or refuse: a **hybrid** list (locked Ghost rows + authored rows in one repeater — A3 social), **one editable field per Ghost row** (A12/A21 role override, keyed by slug), an **item-level Ghost binding** inside an authored list (A10 Value source), and **reference lists** (picked posts/tags/authors — reorder and unpick, no Add that creates — A17–A21, A23, A27, A29). And the **Remove-at-minimum** collision (§37.4).
- **Tooling:** `tools/tuple-check.py` reads only `design/derived-fields-A1-A12.md` (186 designs, its `DOC` constant) — it cannot see the 485 native tuples that now outrank the derived ones. The orchestrator's spec-reading variant (the spec-reading variant run for this pass, three heading/tuple formats) passes 485/485; **extending the tool to read the specs (or the merged inventory) is a finding for the merge**, and `doc-audit.py --check` runs the old one.

## (b) OWNER-FLAG REGISTER — the Ghost Build Room agenda

Every "flag to the owner", "overrule", "owner to confirm", "ARCHITECT:" and equivalent line from all 35 Reconciliation-notes sections (and the flags the specs raise elsewhere), one row each, in spec order. **1,078 rows.** The Provisional-decision column is what the spec did; the last column is what the owner or the architect must rule. Rows that repeat across specs (Remove-at-minimum, the Background-role value set, borrowed scale labels, the edit-safe sense, `nav-transform` coinage, route-awareness, the hand-off mechanism) are the library-wide rulings §37.4–37.6 name; ruling them once closes many rows.

## (c) PRD AMENDMENTS this pass implies — one line per FR or companion

The per-category amendment lists (each §'s last subsection) are the detail; this is the roll-up by the document that moves. Nothing here is applied — the merge lands them after the Ghost Build Room rules (step 4b).

- **FR-G1** — 484 → **485**; the placeable/non-placeable arithmetic made consistent (457 + 28); the count restated everywhere it appears (§37.1).
- **FR-G2** — strike "A31 #10 re-tiered for `private.hbs`" (every A31 design draws the gate; #1/#2 are its Free options) and "A31 #6/#7/#9 custom page templates" (no such designs); rule 70 vs 69; name A29's third Free design; require specs to carry `[Free]`.
- **FR-G3** — `bindingContext` gains `newsletters` and `pagination` (or A34 → `posts`); a design whose bound resource depends on a source switch (A6, A12, A13); `compileTarget: any` excludes `error.hbs`/`private.hbs` for `{{#get}}` categories; a `default.hbs`-class target for unplaced panels (A23); `contentSchema` per-array `min`/`max`/`placeholder`; `states[]` for P0·6; cross-category shared props; conditional `ghostCompat.minVersion`; Quick Controls "recovered mechanically" only if every spec's list leads with them (A8, A9, A16 do not).
- **FR-G4** — the no-JS guarantee names its waivers: D2's, and `member-form`'s if family 2 fails; `cards.js` gets a degradation line; a `tabs` archetype value or bespoke-exception entry (A5-12, A9-8, A13-9, A20-4); the per-pack AA check of accent on the contrast ground (A18-7).
- **FR-G5 / `tools/tuple-check.py`** — the tool reads the specs (or the merged inventory), not `derived-fields-A1-A12.md`; one count-class convention (A8 vs A9); a universal control's value never sets the ground slot.
- **FR-G7** — 31 → **33** (+ `nav-transform`, `contact-form`); rule (1) gains D3's scoped, licence-vetted exception beside `cards.js`; rule (2) permits N modules per design; rule (3)'s `member-form` sentence follows family 2; orphaned rows dropped or re-homed (`search-expand`, `typewriter`, `confetti`, `shuffle`); an **edit-safe column** with FR-D20's sense stated once.
